actors: Danny DeVito, Michael Keaton, Michelle Pfeiffer, Christopher Walken, Michael Gough, Michael Murphy, Cristi Conaway, Andrew Bryniarski, Pat Hingle, Vincent Schiavelli, Diane Salinger, Paul Reubens
description: It's Christmas in Gotham City. The population is preparing to celebrate it by listening to the traditional speech of the authorities, when the party is ruined by the men of the "Penguin". This monstrous creature, raised in the sewers after being abandoned in infants by terrified parents, is the undisputed ruler of Gotham's underworld. Now he wants to take over the whole city; for this he wants to obtain the complicity of Max Schreck, a perfidious unscrupulous tycoon. On the road to this despicable plot, Batman breaks through. Then a new super sexy heroine kicks into action: Catwoman.
notes: For this second very personal "Batman" Tim Burton mobilizes an all star cast. And it is a small masterpiece, nocturnal and misanthropic, slow and cinephile. Extraordinary Michelle Pfeiffer. Obviously it was much less successful than the first.

title: San Francisco
actors: Jeanette MacDonald, Clark Gable, Spencer Tracy, Jack Holt
description: At the beginning of the century a young singer held a show every night in a club on the so-called "Costa dei Barbari", in San Francisco. The owner is an unscrupulous individual whom a priest friend of his has been trying in vain for years to convert. The girl leaves the venue to perform at the opera house because she is the director's lover. However, he died in the terrible earthquake that razed the city to the ground.
notes: Very effective melodrama that skillfully mixes dramatic scenarios and expertly reconstructed catastrophic events. The film, at the time, had a great success with the public and is still more than enjoyable today. The screenplay is by Anita Loos.

title: Angeli a Sud
actors: Paco Reconti, Viviana Natale, Matteo Gazzolo
description: Max, a boy from Cosenza, dreams of founding a private television network: "Tv Sila". The dream will come true. A sloppy film with a flat television cut.

title: Where the Rivers Flow North
actors: Rip Torn, Tantoo Cardinal, Michael J. Fox, Treat Williams
description: The construction of a new dam in Vermont is agreed with all the owners of the affected area except one: Noel Lourdes. He doesn't want to sell, but he's not doing it for nature's sake, he's just trying to raise the price. Splendid landscapes and little more. Michael J. Fox unexpectedly takes on a villain role.

title: Processo per direttissima
actors: Mario Adorf, Bernard Blier, Gabriele Ferzetti, Ira Fürstenberg
description: A militant from a left-wing group accused of a terrorist attack dies during police interrogation. His sister suspects it wasn't an accident. A denouncing film, it was the modest debut of the screenwriter De Caro, on a confused story with an eccentric cast.

title: The Little Drummer Girl
actors: Diane Keaton, Yorgo Voyagis, Klaus Kinski, Sami Frey
description: Charlie, an English actress with vague sympathies for the Palestinian cause, is chosen to shoot a commercial in Greece. There she discovers that everything is organized by the Israeli services who want to make her an agent in order to eliminate the terrorist Khalil. Charlie struggles to get into the part, but eventually agrees and ends up in a terrorist training camp. From the novel by John Le Carrè; a confusing and endless spy movie, with Keaton wasted.

title: Lethal Weapon 3
actors: Mel Gibson, Danny Glover, Joe Pesci, Rene Russo, Stuart Wilson, Steve Kahan, Darlene Love, Traci Wolfe, Damon Hines, Ebonie Smith, Nick Chinlund, Alan Scarfe, Delores Hall
description: In Los Angeles, black cop Roger Murtaugh (Danny Glover), a staid and respected family man, is about to happily retire. The agent he is paired with, Martin Riggs (Mel Gibson), is instead white, wild and with something wrong with his head (because of Vietnam), so much so that he has earned the nickname "Lethal Weapon". In addition to this Martin is also quite convincing when he insists on Roger to investigate a theft of illegal weapons destined to be destroyed. They are joined by Lorna Cole, a smarter and more aggressive detective than Martin and Roger are willing to believe, at least at first. After a series of chases, shootings and explosions, the culprits are framed, Martin falls in love with Lorna and Roger gives up on retirement.

title: Captain from Castile
actors: Tyrone Power, Jean Peters, Lee J. Cobb, Cesar Romero, John Sutton
description: In 1518 Pedro Vargas, a Spanish gentleman, saves a runaway slave, escapes the Inquisition, which however kills his sister, and injures Don Diego De Silva, owner of the slave, in a duel. Then follows Fernando Cortez to America. Here Don Diego reappears, who is murdered. Pedro is immediately suspected of the murder and risks hanging but, acquitted, he will follow Cortez until victory.
notes: The historical background acts as a simple support for a show in which adventure predominates. Enjoyable.

title: The Guns of Navarone
actors: Gregory Peck, Anthony Quinn, David Niven, Irene Papas
description: On the island of Keros, opposite the Turkish coast, there are two thousand British soldiers to be rescued before the German forces arrive. For this it is necessary to organize a naval bridge, but the passage is blocked by two German guns placed on the island of Navarone. Five men are charged with annihilating them and have four days at their disposal. After contacting two Greek partisans, they are betrayed by one of them and handed over to the Nazis. In two, however, they manage to escape and penetrate the cave where the cannons are located; here they prepare the charges to blow them up.
notes: A classic of the war genre. The ingredients are all there: an "all star" cast, an evocative setting, an "impossible" mission, a love story. Jack Lee-Thompson is what is called an honest craftsman.

title: Slap Shot
actors: Paul Newman, Strother Martin, Michael Ontkean, Jennifer Warren
description: The Chiefs (ice hockey) team is very badly placed in the standings and, moreover, also has big economic problems deriving from the crisis of the industry that finances it. The coach tries in every way to avoid the meltdown and uses three brothers to set up a violent game. They will be victories, but the fate of the team is still sealed. The excess of competitive spirit did not help. Fierce portrait of an environment, inside and outside the competition field, not at all recommendable, a metaphor for a corrupt and rotten society. Hockey is tough and spectacular: it performs well in the cinema and the director shows that he knows how to use it profitably.

title: Gray Lady Down
actors: Charlton Heston, David Carradine, Stacy Keach, Ned Beatty
description: The Neptune atomic submarine of the "Gray Lady" class is returning to base after a successfully completed exercise outing. The crew celebrates the second officer who is about to take over command from Captain Samuelson. A Norwegian merchant ship, however, rams the Neptune which plunges to a depth of 450 meters, in a landslide area crossed by very insidious currents. Rescue operations begin (there are only 41 survivors, out of a crew of 93 men), while on board Captain Samuelson is too shocked to be efficient yet. The intervention of a tiny submarine, the Snack, piloted by its inventor, Captain Gates, and not yet tested is fundamental; there are acts of heroism, but also other victims, including Captain Gates himself. There is a rich cinemagraphic "genre" based on catastrophes which, in its best examples, ensures tension and spectacle. Unfortunately, this is not the case with this film, whose most evident flaw is that it has not been able to effectively dose its various components: the human drama of the castaways is only sketchy, the suspense is obvious, the spectacular dimension is weak and not even underwater shooting is recommended for particular vigor. The actors and their solid profession are saved by all means, but the overall balance is a bit disappointing.

title: La donna più bella del mondo
actors: Gina Lollobrigida, Vittorio Gassman, Robert Alda, Anne Vernon
description: The beautiful singer from Trastevere Lina Cavalieri makes her debut by replacing her sick mother on the stage of a popular theater. Here he meets Prince Sergio Bariatine, generous with aid. Lina studies singing and follows her teacher to Paris, but then separates from him. Her life is a climb to success, full of fame, of suitors, also marked by some dramas, but finally crowned by the love of the prince ...
notes: The heavily fictionalized biography of the famous opera singer active in the early 1900s. A production made with relative commitment and destined for a popular audience, with Lollobrigida and Gassman at the minimum wage.

title: Grand Canyon
actors: Danny Glover, Kevin Kline, Mary McDonnell, Steve Martin
description: Mack (Kline), a 40-year-old lawyer, is stranded in his car in a slum area of ??Los Angeles where he is surrounded by a gang of thugs. A black mechanic, Simon (Glover), saves him. The man tells him about his life: married, separated, with a deaf daughter and a sister who lives in that neighborhood. Davis (Martin), Mack's producer friend, is wounded by a robber who shoots him in the leg to steal his watch. After this tragic experience Davis promises to stop producing violent films. Mack regrets an affair with his secretary, while his wife decides to adopt a girl abandoned in the trees. Davis, recovered, resumes producing the usual films.
notes: Kasdan investigates his favorite territories, which are those of the wounded feelings and fractures of the soul of the metropolitan man. The result is a cruel fresco of contemporary America, between sentimentality and violence. A cinematic essay on the need for a new sensitivity, "Gran Canyon" crosses American reality, casting a shadow of doubt on the direction taken (and to be taken) in the daily lives of different characters. Golden Bear in Berlin.

title: The Lions Has Wings
actors: Merle Oberon, Ralph Richardson, June Duprez
description: The film chronicles the peaceful life of Her British Majesty's subjects busy cultivating their ideals of peace and freedom. From Nazi Germany, however, the shadow of Hitler's dictatorship is threatening. The sequences of the advance of the German troops alternate with scenes from the domestic life of English families until the dramatic outbreak of the war.
notes: Propaganda film, with documentary inserts and reconstructed skits.

title: Il giustiziere di mezzogiorno
actors: Franco Franchi, Ombretta De Carlo, Alberto Farnese, Gigi Ballista, Maria Antonietta Beluzzi, Franco Diogene, Raf Luca, Gino Pagnani, Enzo Andronico, Aldo Puglisi, Giovanni Sabbatini
description: The surveyor Franco Gabbiadini is left by his wife Agata who takes her little daughter Titina with her. In addition, he is harassed by the office manager and has to deal with the amorous offers of his colleague Barzuacchi. Exasperated, Franco turns into an avenger, until his wife and daughter return to him. Without the usual company of Ciccio Ingrassia, Franco Franchi engages in the parody of the executioner, without panache.

title: Erik the Viking
actors: Tim Robbins, Terry Jones, Eartha Kitt, John Cleese
description: In the land of the Vikings the sun never rises. The young Erik (Robbins), on the advice of the sorceress Freya (Kitt), takes courage with four hands and leaves for the land of Argard where the Gods and Heroes who died in battle live. After defeating the Monster of the Oceans and the terrible Halfaan the Black, Erik succeeds in his feat, finally bringing the sun back to his land. You can smell Monty Python in this movie (there is John Cleese as well as Terry Jones himself), but there is not their unbridled comedy. A little undecided between that and fantasy, Jones remains halfway across the ford. Still excellent Tim Robbins.

title: The Verdict
actors: Paul Newman, James Mason, Charlotte Rampling, Jack Warden
description: Frank Galvin (Newman) is an alcoholic lawyer who had to abandon his career because he was involved in a corruption case. Today he has been reduced to chasing compensation cases related to car accidents. Until an old colleague who entrusts him with a complex case: the defense of a woman who, being operated on in a Catholic hospital, lost sight and speech due to a mistake by the anesthesiologists and has now been in a coma for four years. Newman plays the role of Galvin with great energy and drama. Charlotte Rampling is perfect in a sneaky and thankless role. But the rest of the cast is also excellent, from the great James Mason, defense attorney, to old Jack Warden. Despite the apparent happy ending, Lumet is bitter, attentive, more than the facts, the atmospheres and the bitter circumstances in which the characters move. The screenplay is by David Mamet.

title: All I Want for Christmas
actors: Ethan Randall, Thora Birch, Harley Jane Kozak, Jamey Sheridan, Leslie Nielsen
description: Hallie is seven and her brother Ethan is thirteen. Hallie stays at Macy's all day because there is a gentleman dressed as Santa Claus who collects the wishes of the children. Hallie and Ethan's common desire is to see their parents reunited on the evening of December 24th. The fact is that Dad quit his lucrative Wall Street job a while ago to open a restaurant and it seems that this has severely affected Mom's esteem for him. Hallie and Ethan, trusting the righteous in Santa Claus, hatch a plan to encourage reunification. This is not just the exploitation of minors, it is the exploitation of feelings. Fortunately, the producers of this film to make money on Christmas rhetoric went badly anyway.

title: Freud
actors: Montgomery Clift, Larry Parks, Susannah York, Susan Kohner, Eileen Herlie, Fernand Ledoux, David McCallum, Rosalie Crutchley, David Kossoff, Joseph Fürst, Alexander Mango, Leonard Sachs, Eric Portman, Victor Beaumont
description: In 1885 Freud experimented with the use of hypnosis in the treatment of hysteria. Interested in the case of a boy who hates his father, he delves into his unconscious and focuses on the "Oedipus complex".
notes: Huston turns a biography of the father of psychoanalysis that is both honest and compelling. A harsh film, 40 'scissored by the production, starring an excellent Montgomery Clift. Jean-Paul Sartre's original script, not used, was later released in volume. In the original version the narrator is by John Huston himself.

title: The Horror of Frankenstein
actors: Ralph Bates, Kate O'Mara, Veronica Carlson, Dennis Price, Jon Finch
description: Victor Frankenstein, already a parricide, secretly builds a killer monster and kills anyone who could betray his creature. Last, a bit tired, production of the classic Hammer series directed by the screenwriter of the house.

title: Time After Time
actors: Malcolm McDowell, David Warner, Mary Steenburgen
description: From Victorian London, Jack the Ripper escapes to modern San Francisco using H.G. Wells' time machine. The scientist-thinker-writer pursues him to neutralize him. A film with a vague literary taste, enjoyable overall, played on the thread of the fantastic and the ironic reinterpretation of the horror genre. There is no lack of love story and moralizing closure on violence in our century.

title: The Ambassador
actors: Robert Mitchum, Ellen Burstyn, Rock Hudson
description: Robert Mitchum, ambassador with a beautiful and adulterous wife, attempts a cunning and dangerous mediation between Israelis and Palestinians. Old lions for a film so-so, based on a novel by Elmore Leonard that also inspired Frankenheimer's very different 52 play or die. Rock Hudson's last appearance.

title: The Plumber
actors: Judy Morris, Ivar Kants, Robert Coleby
description: A terrible plumber breaks through the bathrooms of riotous and helpless tenants. Black comedy made in Australia, simple but fun, shot by Weir for TV.

title: Gun Fury
actors: Rock Hudson, Donna Reed, Phil Carey, Lee Marvin, Roberta Haynes, Leo Gordon
description: A woman is kidnapped by Southern outlaws after a stagecoach assault. Her boyfriend (Hudson) pursues the bandits and takes revenge. Shot in 3-D; solid, but not the best of Walsh.

title: What a Carve Up!
actors: Sid James, Kenneth Connor, Shirley Eaton
description: The very rich and crazy Brighton decides to pretend to go to the other world in order to kill undisturbed the numerous relatives greedy waiting for the inheritance. British farce, truly capable of making you shiver, but also full of tasty gimmicks.

title: Endless Love
actors: Brooke Shields, Martin Hewitt, Don Murray
description: 17-year-old David's love for 15-year-old Jade runs into a thousand obstacles and ends in tragedy. Cloying melodrama, irritating directorial emphasis and interpretation.

title: The Secret Garden
actors: Margaret O'Brien, Herbert Marshall, Gladys Cooper
description: An orphan girl moves in with grumpy and embittered Uncle Archibald, bringing optimism and serenity to her new home. Almost a fairy tale, but full of mystery and atmosphere, from a good childhood novel by Francis Hodgson Burnett.

title: The Black Bird
actors: George Segal, Stéphane Audran, Lee Patrick
description: Sam Spade's son, also an investigator, is besieged by an assorted swarm of slys who still chase the Maltese falcon. Empty parody of one of the noir classics.

title: Il prezzo del potere
actors: Giuliano Gemma, Warren Vanders, Maria Cuadra, Fernando Rey
description: President Garfield has big plans for the US but is killed in Dallas. They arrest an innocent, Willer, who escapes and discovers the real culprits. Romance on the case of J.F.K. in our own West. Disappointing, with Giuliano Gemma.

title: National Lampoon's Animal House
actors: John Belushi, Tim Matheson, John Vernon, Verna Bloom, Kevin Bacon, James Daughton, Martha Smith, Mary Louise Weller, Mark Metcalf, Stephen Furst, Tom Hulce, Douglas Kenney, Chris Miller, Karen Allen, James Widdoes, Peter Riegert
description: In 1962, Eric and Kent landed at college, eager to join one of the clubs that dominate student life. Rejected by the good guys of the Omega House, they enter the Delta club, from which all social rules are banned. The anarchic activities of the group trigger the persecution of the rector, in agreement with the Omegas. The Deltas take their revenge in their own way, with scandalous parties and carnivals. A pure fun film with which John Landis anticipated the success and thunderous comedy of The Blues Brothers, produced two years later. The main merit of the film, however, remains that of having highlighted the exceptional comic vis of John Belushi.

title: Silver Streak
actors: Gene Wilder, Jill Clayburgh, Richard Pryor, Patrick McGoohan
description: Traveling coast to coast, from Los Angeles to Chicago, on the luxurious "Silver Streak" train, George Caldwell, a young and shy editor, meets Hilly Burns, secretary of a famous Rembrandt scholar, prof. Schreiner. On the way he is killed. George discovers that, thanks to some letters he was in possession of, the murdered man could prove the colossal fraud against the state committed by a certain Roger Devereau by means of false paintings.
notes: Characters and situations are reminiscent of Hitchcock, but overall the comedy, with a few strokes of sex, here prevails over the thrill. Even in the violent ending sequence, fear never really makes itself felt.

title: Dear Wife
actors: Joan Caulfield, William Holden, Edward Arnold
description: Son-in-law and father-in-law, who live in the same house, unwittingly find themselves political opponents.
notes: Graceful comedy of misunderstandings with inevitable happy ending.

title: An American Tail
description: A family of mice emigrated from Russia to the United States. During the journey, little Fievel ends up at sea, he will be reunited with his family in New York after a thousand adventures. Don Bluth constructs a sort of intelligent "family saga" about the emigration of European Jews to America at the turn of the century and the myth of America. Traditional and pleasant animation.

title: Holiday for Lovers
actors: Clifton Webb, Jane Wyman, Paul Henreid, Carol Lynley
description: Meg, the daughter of an American psychologist, goes on vacation to Argentina. Here he meets and marries the painter Carlos. Sentimental comedy by a handyman director like Henry Levin.

title: Dov'è la libertà?
actors: Totò, Vera Molnar, Leopoldo Trieste, Franca Faldini
description: The barber Salvatore Lojacono has served a long sentence for killing his wife in a fit of jealousy and is released from prison. Since he does not know where to go, he is greeted by the relatives of his wife, who has died in the meantime. They are shady characters, enriched with the goods of the deported Jews, and intend to use the candid Savior for their own shady ends. When the poor barber realizes the deception he tries in every way to go back to prison.
notes: The film was blocked for two years by censorship, and indeed its description of postwar Italy is terrifying. Although considered a minor Rossellini (and manipulated by the production), the film has its greatest merit in this cruelty, as well as in the painful mask of a tragic version of Totò. The last scenes were directed out of friendship by Federico Fellini.

title: Astérix le Gaulois
description: Endowed with superhuman strength thanks to the magical potion of the druid Panoramix, the inhabitants of the only village in Gaul that Julius Caesar's legions have not penetrated do not intend to submit at all. The inseparable Asterix and Obelix, as soon as they can, sow terror among the invaders. Having infiltrated a spy and kidnapped the druid, the Romans hope to have won, but they don't care.
notes: The famous characters created by Goscinny and Uderzo cannot bear the transposition from the illustrated page to the screen. This first attempt at animation of the famous hero is very experimental. The later episodes improve considerably.

title: Lady Windermere's Fan
actors: Irene Rich, May McAvory, Ronald Colman, Bert Lyttel
description: Since she believes that her husband, Mr. Windermere, is cheating on her with a certain Mrs. Erllynne, his wife is ready to pay him back. But Mrs. Erlynne is Lady Windermere's mother, who had abandoned her as a child. Once his daughter's marriage has been saved, he will be saved a second time, even though he is forced to reveal his identity and go away forever, hoping for oblivion. From the homonymous comedy by Oscar Wilde, Lubitsch draws the best film of his American period before sound. Cynical and ferocious, a lesson in staging.

title: L'ours
actors: Tchéky Karyo, Jack Wallace, André Lacombe
description: The cute little bear Youk, who has been orphaned, is "adopted" by the gigantic and lonely Kaar who gradually teaches him everything necessary for survival. Written by Gérard Brach (who stumbles in numerous passages, "L'orso" is a honeyed and feeble ecological parable, played by real bears but also by puppets and mimes.

title: The Southern Star
actors: George Segal, Ursula Andress, Orson Welles, Ian Hendry
description: French equatorial Africa: a diamond of exceptional value disappears and a black man is accused of the theft, who flees into the forest. The treacherous captain of the gendarmerie, a geologist engaged to the mine owner's daughter and the same girl, set out on his trail. From a novel by Verne, a pleasant exotic film.

title: Oh, God!
actors: George Burns, John Denver, Teri Garr, Paul Sorvino, Ralph Bellamy
description: To whom could God make himself visible today if not to the American manager of a supermarket, a sort of modern temple to consumerism? So Jerry Landers, director of a department store is summoned by God himself, dissatisfied with the trend taken by humanity in the age of consumption. The young man arms himself with missionary zeal, but he only earns complaints and failures. In the end though ...
notes: Some good ideas, but the whole is weak.

title: The Swimmer
actors: Burt Lancaster, Marge Champion
description: The young Ned decides to reach his home by swimming across the pools of the neighbors' villas ...
notes: From a masterpiece of American short fiction ("The swimmer" by John Cheever) a slow and melancholy film, an original metaphor on the fall of the American dream: the pools in which Ned gets wet from time to time are, literally speaking, a dip in his past and the awareness of the developments that that (shattered) dream has had. Water purifies, promotes rebirth by washing away the superfluous. But what lies beneath it is a bitter and cruel truth. With a splendid - and extremely charming - Burt Lancaster.

title: Carefree
actors: Fred Astaire, Ginger Rogers, Ralph Bellamy, Jack Carson
description: Her boyfriend finds her a bit too extravagant and, very worried about the sudden change, decides to send her to a psychoanalyst friend of his for a decisive analysis. The girl, however, ends up falling in love with the doctor and the friend, to save the situation, is left with hypnotism. In fact, she decides to marry her boyfriend. But now the doctor has also fallen in love. Fred and Ginger's latest RKO film (there will be a late return in "The Berkeleys of Broadway" ten years later), and one of the first psychoanalyst figures (very unorthodox, to be honest) of Hollywood cinema. Songs by Irving Berlin.

title: Brigadoon
actors: Gene Kelly, Van Johnson, Cyd Charisse, Elaine Stewart
description: Jeff and Tommy, two Americans traveling to Scotland, find themselves in an enchanted village, Brigadoon, which appears out of nowhere for just one day every hundred years, thus remaining protected from evil. Tommy falls in love, reciprocated, with a girl, but the magical day ends and he must return to New York. Then, however, love brings him back to Scotland, and, miraculously, Brigadoon emerges from the mists. Excellent example of fantastic-musical film made with high professionalism by a director who is a master of the "genre", with which all the technical and artistic collaborators express themselves at their best. Great music column by Frederick Loewe.

title: Un uomo da bruciare
directors: Paolo Taviani, Vittorio Taviani, Valentino Orsini
actors: Gian Maria Volonté, Didi Perego, Spiros Focas, Turi Ferro
description: Salvatore, a young trade union activist of Marxist inspiration, returns to Sicily after two years spent in Rome and finds himself faced with a hostile reality. He tries with some comrades to occupy an uncultivated land, but the mafia first hinders him and then tries to distract him from the action by hiring him as a foreman in a quarry. But Salvatore is not a man who lets himself be bribed, and so the mafia kills him. First feature film directed by the Taviani brothers (with Valentino Orsini): a work that has the merit of full-blown social commitment, perhaps a little schematic, but very vigorous.

title: Over the Top
actors: Sylvester Stallone, David Mendenhall, Susan Blakely, Robert Loggia
description: Lincoln Hawk, a truck driver, has to take his 12-year-old son (whom he hasn't seen in many years) to his sick mother. The little boy, raised by his maternal grandfather in the contempt of his father, is at first very hostile then, little by little, he becomes convinced of the parent's love. But before everything works out for the best, many difficulties will arise and Lincoln will have to win a tournament of arm wrestling champions. A character halfway between Rambo and Rocky for the strong Stallone, with the fundamental component of the problem with his son. Psychologically rough, with Stallone trying to redeem his image in tears.

title: Way Down East
actors: Lillian Gish, Josephine Bernard, Lowell Sherman, Richard Barthelmess
description: Anna Moore, a poor country girl, left her family and goes to town in search of work. Here she meets a man who seduces her and marries her, but soon her reckless husband leaves her. A child is born but dies after a few days. Alone and desperate, Anna finds refuge with a good family, where young David falls in love with her. When her husband reappears, Anna is thrown out. Desperate she goes to the swirling river carrying ice floes, but David saves her. Strong melodrama supported by the interpretative intensity of Lillian Gish (Griffith's favorite actress) and the director's narrative mastery. From the anthology the sequence of the rescue of the protagonist on the ice, in the raging storm.

title: The Doctor
actors: William Hurt, Elizabeth Perkins, Christine Lahti, Mandy Patinkin
description: Surgeon Jack (Hurt), a brilliant 40-year-old and unscrupulous doctor, suffers from throat cancer. The disease reveals itself to him not only in its aspects of physical suffering, but also as arrogance on the part of doctors, bureaucratic hindrances, humiliations. However, he also discovers the solidarity of the sick and the inner strength of some of them, particularly the young June (Perkins), condemned by a brain tumor. Based on an autobiographical novel by Ed Rosenbaum, the film re-proposes the duo director-interpreter of "Sons of a Lesser God", with similar characteristics: a mix of sentimental analysis and social problems. Themes sometimes dealt with with concessions to effective melodrama; but the director certainly has the merit of being able to obtain intense participation from her performers.

title: Christmas Vacation
actors: Chevy Chase, Beverly D'Angelo, Juliette Lewis, Randy Quaid, Diane Ladd
description: Clark Griswold (Chase) is the head of a family that couldn't be more deranged. The Christmas holidays are approaching and, for this year, the Grinswolds have decided not to go around the world to make trouble, but to stay at home. The countless relatives announced on arrival will take care of complicating things and making the situation literally unbearable anyway.
notes: The comedy of Chevy Chase comes out only at times.

title: La vendetta dei Tughs
actors: Lex Barker, Enzo Fiermonte, Fiorella Mari, Paul Müller
description: Tremal Naik, the famous tiger hunter, ends up as a prisoner of the bloodthirsty Tughs warriors in an attempt to free Ada, his woman. Discovered, he is sentenced to death, but a column of soldiers under the command of Colonel Kennedy is moving to his rescue. The military operation is successful. Naik clashes with the leader of the sect and kills him in a duel, after which, with Ada, he is finally free. The film is inspired by the characters of Salgari's novels: the Venturini Productions specialized at the time in the sector. An Italian B-movie for the most popular consumption.

title: The Lost Boys
actors: Jason Patric, Corey Haim, Dianne Wiest, Jami Gertz, Barnard Hughes, Edward Herrmann, Kiefer Sutherland, Corey Feldman, Jamison Newlander, Brooke McCarter, Billy Wirth, Alex Winter
description: Young Michael gets into trouble with a punk gang. But everyone understands, even his younger brother Sam, that they are vampires instead. The cast is very interesting, the direction a little less, but it's still a compelling juvenile horror.

title: To Grandmother's House We Go
actors: Mary-Kate Olsen, Ashley Olsen, Rhea Perlman, Cynthia Geary
description: What makes us a gang of kidnappers on the heels of two twins? The girls are traveling to reach the grandmother and the criminals have fun molesting them.
notes: Revised and correct version in a topical key of the fairy tale of Red Riding Hood certainly not very right as for comic success. It would like to be a parody, but it doesn't make it laugh much.

title: Huckleberry Finn
actors: Jeff East, Paul Winfield, Harvey Korman, David Wayne
description: The sequel to "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" tells the escape along the Mississippi of Huck and his friend the Negro Jim, from Mrs. Douglas, who would like to "educate" him and from the drunkard father who would like to seize the treasure that Huck earned by unmasking, with Tom Sawyer, the Indian killer. Musical version of the famous novel by Mark Twain with which, however, he has little in common.

title: Tom Sawyer
actors: Johnnie Whitaker, Jeff East, Jodie Foster, Warren Oates
description: Tom Sawyer and his friend Huck Finn witnessed the crime committed by a half-blooded Indian who, however, manages to put the responsibility for the fact of blood on another. At the trial, however, Tom unmasks the culprit, but the Indian escapes. During a school trip Tom discovers the Indian's hiding place (and treasure) in a cave ...
notes: Musical version of Mark Twain's masterpiece. Among the other performers there is also a very young (and unrecognizable) Jodie Foster. A good one who guesses it

title: My Six Loves
actors: Debbie Reynolds, Cliff Robertson, David Janssen, Eileen Heckart
description: A movie star on vacation in a provincial town adopts six orphans and even finds a husband. Sweet and predictable, with divas a bit 'bambocci.

title: The Pied Piper
actors: Donovan, Donald Pleasence, Michael Hordern, Diana Dors
description: A piper frees a town from mice thanks to the sound of his magical flute. To take revenge for not having been paid, he also takes the children away. Based on the Brothers Grimm fairytale, it is a fairytale but not a children's film. The Pied Piper is played by pop singer Donovan.

title: Fabiola
actors: Michèle Morgan, Michel Simon, Gino Cervi, Henry Vidal
description: Fabiola, daughter of Senator Fabio Severo, falls in love with the gladiator Rhual at the time of the persecutions of Christians. It is one of the most famous films in the history of Italian cinema; it was the greatest productive effort of the time (produced by the Vatican). The mixture of drama and history, however, is somewhat cumbersome.

title: Turner and Hooch
actors: Tom Hanks, Mare Winningham, Craig T. Nelson, Scott Paulin
description: Scott Turner, a policeman obsessed with order and cleanliness, is on the trail of the killer of his friend, old Amos Reed, who ran a small junk yard in the harbor area. The cop adopts Hooch, the big hound owned by the dead man, who turns out to be very undisciplined and capable of unleashing an earthquake in Turner's orderly life.
notes: The film looks promising at the beginning, with a series of good jokes and the amusing confrontation between the law and order agent, even in private life, and the slobbering dog with an anarchic temperament. Then everything slips into déjà vu, the most obvious detective side of history prevails over the wits of brilliant comedy and the performance of the good Tom Hanks fails to stem the yawns.

title: Sistemo l'America e torno
actors: Paolo Villaggio, Sterling St. Jacques, Rita Savagnone, Alfredo Rizzo
description: Giovanni Bonfiglio, employed by a Lombard company, is sent to the US to pursue a business. He will discover the America of repression and racial hatred. Frayed and rhetorical.

title: La cattedra
actors: Giulio Brogi, Claudio Bigagli, David Riondino, Sabina Guzzanti, Enrica Maria Modugno
description: Professor Dal Mario, a university professor of philosophy, has two arguments, big and big and Parini, who hope to exploit his prestige to make a career. When Mario is hit by a stroke, the two have the opportunity to reveal the worst side of their character. If Parini reveals himself hypocritical, big in the long run of his behavior, so much so that he obtained the forgiveness of the professor, finally put back. Despite the presence of actors who usually stand out for their comic registers - from Riondino to Sabina Guzzanti - this film is a bitter description of a group of birds of prey. Too bad that, he can't take off.

title: Un dollaro bucato
actors: Giuliano Gemma, Evelyn Stewart, Peter Cross
description: Gary is commissioned to murder a man. She realizes at the last moment that this is her brother Phil.

title: Monte Carlo
actors: Jeanette MacDonald, Jack Buchanan, Claud Allister, Zasu Pitts
description: Prince Otto Von Seibenheim (Allister), very rich and very much in love with the beautiful but poor Countess Vera (MacDonald), is once again about to marry her, but once again she escapes at the last moment and goes to seek her fortune in Monte Carlo. Here, after a fleeting encounter with Count Rudolph (Buchanan), who falls in love with her, Vera loses all the money she had won, but continues to live in pomp and debt. Rudolph, meanwhile, in order to attend her, gets hired as a hairdresser.
notes: Lubitsch's second sound film is a pleasant and mischievous fairy tale, based on a play by Hans Muller.

title: The Crying Game
actors: Jaye Davidson, Stephen Rea, Forest Whitaker, Miranda Richardson
description: A black English soldier, Jody (Whitaker), is kidnapped by an IRA commando in an attempt to trade with an Irish prisoner. Despite his jailer, Fergus (Rea), being a human type, Jody's end is tragic. Fergus, who now lives in London as a bricklayer, follows Jody's woman, contacts her and begins a relationship with her, discovering that she is not what she appears to be.
notes: There are various reasons why this film should be seen. From Rea's painful interpretation to Whitaker's exhilarating one (forced half the time with a hood on his head). Then there are at least two sensational dialogues in the pub, with a silent bartender acting as an intermediary; the story that runs in the background (that of the Irish conflict) and every now and then comes out. So there is Jordan's shrewd direction. Oscar for the script.

title: The Exile
actors: Douglas Fairbanks jr., Maria Montez, Paule Croset, Henry Daniell
description: Because of Cromwell's followers, Charles II flees into exile in Holland. But even there he is discovered (by the group of "round heads") and then he has nothing left but to take refuge in the countryside. Having entered the service of the innkeeper Kate, Carlo takes pleasure in life in the fields and in Kate's presence, until, after escaping yet another ambush, he learns that his homeland is demanding him again. Six years after his arrival in Hollywood, the exile Ophuls makes a film about exile, full of sequence shots, packed with dollies and with a delirious theatrical setting. A Douglas jr still struggling with his father's ghost helps him, even as a screenwriter.

title: Fuga dal Bronx
actors: Mark Gregory, Henry Silva, Valeria D'Obici, Moana Pozzi
description: A construction company has decided to raze the Bronx neighborhood in New York to carry out a colossal real estate speculation. The inhabitants who live there are simply bought. Those who oppose must instead contend with the death squad of "exterminators". Among the opponents there is a gang that lives underground, very determined to resist .. If there is an Italian Serie B cinema, then Castellari is its prophet and this, sequel to "1990 - The Bronx Warriors", is one of his most famous films. Which doesn't mean much, even if the action scenes work. Henry Silva has been a villain all his life.

title: Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory
actors: Gene Wilder, Jack Albertson, Roy Kinnear, Julie Dawn Cole, Peter Ostrum, Denise Nickerson
description: Willy Wonka, owner of a candy factory, holds a competition. Among the five winning children, the capricious ones will be punished and the only honest one awarded.
notes: Based on a beautiful book by Roald Dahl (who adapted it for the screen), it is a small and imaginative film about childhood, which focuses on the dark and gothic side of fairy tales. Figuratively rich, with a truly creepy Wilder.

title: Little Women
actors: Janet Leigh, June Allyson, Elizabeth Taylor, Rossano Brazzi, Peter Lawford
description: Dr. March is off to war. His wife and four daughters remain at home: Jo, Meg, Amy and Beth. Jo is courted by Laurie, the nephew of an old general close to them, while Meg does not disdain the court of a friend of Laurie's. The news arrives that the head of the family is hospitalized in New York. Jo sells her hair to allow her mother to visit her husband. After the man's return, the family gradually falls apart. The direction of Le Roy is very accurate. But the film, despite the large number of stars and future stars, is not worth that of Cukor of 1933.

title: Lighthouse
actors: Ryan Michael, Deborah Wakeman, Stephen E. Miller, Blu Mankuma
description: To save a falling marriage, Lynn offers her husband Paul a romantic island getaway. The same one in which years before his sister and his brother-in-law had disappeared in an accident. Things between Lynn and Paul are better, but some strange events come to disturb the atmosphere and Lynn begins to suspect that her sister's death was not entirely accidental. The initial pretext (that of the wrong marriage) serves only to force the two protagonists into an isolated situation and apparently without escape routes. Which means that we have already seen the story several times and with better directors.

title: One Magic Christmas
actors: Mary Steenburgen, Gary Basaraba, Harry Dean Stanton
description: Bad Christmas for the Graingers. Dad Jack is unemployed, while Mom Ginny struggles to support the family on her salary as a clerk. Sons Abbie and Caleb, who don't even dare think about Christmas presents, are also silenced by their mom if they just try to talk about Santa Claus. Not to mention the looming eviction. But luckily, behind them, there is an angel who sees and provides. It's definitely not your usual, gooey, candy-like Christmas movie. Steenburgen is very depressed and very un-maternal. And even the angel (Harry Dean Stanton), with his hat pulled over his eyes and his dark overcoat, doesn't seem like a very sociable type.

title: The New Centurions
actors: George C. Scott, Stacy Keach, Jane Alexander, Scott Wilson, Erik Estrada, Rosalind Cash
description: Life of a group of LAPD officers: Sergio is a Puerto Rican from the underworld; Guisley is upset after he accidentally kills a thief's pursuer; the commander of the police school is a sly cynic; Andy is alone and close to retirement; Roy is the rookie, law student, married to a woman who scolds him for neglecting her. Police drama with precise sociological notations, but cloaked in a gloom accentuated by the excellent direction of Fleischer. Great actors.

title: Dekalog ieden-dziesiec
actors: Wojciek Klata, Grazyna Szapolowska
description: The precepts of the Bible seen through as many emblematic stories set in the present day.

title: Miracle on 34th Street
actors: Edmund Gwenn, Maureen O'Hara, John Payne, Natalie Wood
description: Department store executives must find a Santa for their annual parade. A handsome old man shows up who does his job very well enough to be hired. The old man, who claims to be truly Santa Claus, makes himself liked by everyone and business thrives. The doctor of the company, however, drags him to court declaring him crazy, but ...
notes: Well-written and unsweetened Christmas film, which at its release had a resounding success crowned by three Oscars (subject, screenplay and Gwenn best actor).

title: Midnight Lace
actors: Doris Day, Rex Harrison, John Gavin, Myrna Loy, Roddy McDowall
description: A young American lady confidently follows her husband, a rich Englishman who takes her with him to London. In the mists of the British capital, our Yankee is a little uncomfortable, but then comes the real terror when she is persecuted, first on the phone then by mysterious presences, with obscure death threats. The solution comes, suddenly, with a formidable twist.
notes: Apart from the imitation of Hitchcockian atmospheres, the director Miller plays here the Doris Day card. That is, he entrusts this actress-singer with the role of a dramatic actress, in the wake of "The Man Who Knew Too Much". And she is doing very well.

title: Il seduttore
actors: Alberto Sordi, Lea Padovani, Jacqueline Pierreux, Lia Amanda, Denise Grey
description: The modest employee Alberto has always dreamed of erotic adventures, unbeknownst to his wife, with all the women he knows. He has never succeeded in his intentions, but chance makes him suddenly succeed with three beautiful girls. His wife discovers everything and Alberto, unable to manage the situation, flees to South America, but ... From a comedy by Diego Fabbri, a Deaf of the heyday, with a little too much rein under the direction of Franco Rossi.

title: Landru
actors: Charles Denner, Michèle Morgan, Danielle Darrieux
description: We are in the years of the Great War. Landru (Denner) is a quiet little man, fascinated by rather mature ladies. After seducing them, he gets them to sign a power of attorney and, after killing them, he disposes of their bodies in the stove. Arrested, at the trial he uses his irony to win the sympathy of the public. This, however, does not save him.
notes: With its macabre humor, Chabrol's film also becomes a reflection on guilt and responsibility. And accepting the point of view of those who followed the trial, the director gives us the image of a rather likeable "monster".

title: Maurizio, Peppino e le indossatrici
actors: Maurizio Arena, Peppino Di Capri, Mara Berni
description: Antonella, Mara and Bice, three models steal expensive dresses from the tailor shop for which they work. The girls who, in the meantime, have gone to a fashionable mountain resort are tracked down by Maurizio, the nephew of the shop owner. The boy, to recover the stolen goods, gets help from his friend Peppino. Meanwhile, love breaks out between Bice and Peppino, while Mara accepts the court of a rich Sicilian baron.
notes: Unfortunately Peppino is not De Filippo and, what is more serious, Maurizio is not Totò and the director is a certain Filippo Walter Ratti, also known by the pseudonym of Stanley Lewis.

title: La più bella coppia del mondo
actors: Walter Chiari, Paola Quattrini, Aldo Giuffré, Fracesco Mulè, Elio Pandolfi
description: Due to a misunderstanding Walter and Paola, presenters of the Cantagiro, are given up for secretly married. Both of them would like to deny it, but Paola has a fiery Sicilian suitor she wants to get rid of while Walter could sign a fabulous advertising contract as long as he is ... married. The fiction goes on like this, between smiles in public and furious quarrels in private between the two presenters who, in reality, hate each other.
notes: Vintage songs held together by a specious frame. Instant movie shot to take advantage of the most loved singing competition by Italians.

title: Pinocchio and the Emperor of the Night
description: The adventures of Pinocchio, now a real boy, and his friend Gee Whillikers. A kind of senseless cartoon sequel to Collodi's story of Pinocchio.

title: Starchaser: The Legend of Orin
description: Robots have enslaved humans and force them to work in underground factories. The young Orin finds a magic sword, resurfaces and rushes to the rescue. Low level animation, as well as the story.

title: Ponzio Pilato
actors: Jean Marais, Jeanne Crain, Massimo Serato, Basil Rathbone
description: In the presence of Caligula, the governor of Judea Pontius Pilate retraces the events of which he was the protagonist starting from his arrival in Palestine. The hostility of the local population, the raids and massacres of the bandit Barabbas in the region. The riots and fanaticism caused by the preaching of Jesus of Nazareth that forever shook the lives of the inhabitants of Palestine and the high priests of the Jewish religion. The crucifixion of Jesus and the granting of grace to the bandit Barabbas.
notes: The film is built in the purest (and poorest) "Hollywood on the Tiber" style.

title: That Lady in Ermine
actors: Betty Grable, Douglas Fairbanks jr., Cesar Romero, Walter Abel
description: The Hungarian army arrives at the castle immediately after Francesca's wedding. The husband runs away. The great-grandmother descends from the ancient portrait and suggests to the princess that she pretend to be in love with the invading commander, so that she can then kill him. Francesca obeys, but love ends up really blossoming. Last film credited to Lubitsch, it was completed by Preminger. Pleasant in costumes, songs, performers, but dated as far as the script is concerned.

title: Dinner at Eight
actors: John Barrymore, Wallace Beery, Jean Harlow, Lionel Barrymore
description: The wife of a shipowner on the brink of bankruptcy organizes a sumptuous lunch. At the table a rather varied sample of humanity should be gathered, but several drawbacks put some diners out of the way. Fierce portrait of the American bourgeoisie under the usual sophisticated comedy atmosphere, it is one of the best films of the great American director, supported by an extraordinary cast and with a horological script.

title: Swiss Miss
actors: Stan Laurel, Oliver Hardy, Della Lind, Eric Blore, Charles Judels
description: In a Swiss boarding house Laurel and Hardy are struggling with a piano to be transported on a suspension bridge and with a gorilla. Sublime gags, as always.

title: Annie
actors: Aileen Quinn, Albert Finney, Carol Burnett, Ann Reinking
description: Annie, a very lively orphan, lives in an institute with two other girlfriends under the orders of the director, who, despite her age no longer green, still runs after men. The girls sing and dance and are lively enough to drive their manager crazy.
notes: Based on a Harold Gray comic and a successful musical comedy, the film is discreet if rather boring.

title: It's Only Money
actors: Jerry Lewis, Joan O'Brien, Zachary Scott, Jack Weston, Jesse White, Barbara Pepper, Francine York, Ted De Corsia
description: Hobby investigator Jerry Lewis has to track down a missing person for 25 years. He then discovers that he is the wanted one. Tashlin, already a catastrophic cartoonist, gives Lewis some unforgettable gags, even if the film refers more to those of the previous decade than to the "adult" rehearsals of Lewis the director.

title: Noi non siamo angeli
actors: Michael Coby, Paul Smith, Renato Cestié, Woody Strode
description: Raphael, a man with a forbidden fist, has a brother, Angel, who constantly gets him into trouble. But Angel, despite being a bungler, is anything but dumb; so much so that it involves Raphael in a business (the concession of a transport service) that promises well.
notes: Gianfranco Parolini, under the pseudonym of Frank Kramer, realizes a variant of the adventures of Trinity (with the clones of Spencer and Hill), between fracassone disputes, jokes and jokes and little else.

title: The Hucksters
actors: Clark Gable, Deborah Kerr, Ava Gardner
description: An enterprising young man (Gable) works as an advertiser for an extravagant and irascible industrialist whose anger he suffers. Meeting the young widow of an English officer (Kerr) opens up the conflict between business and love.
notes: Drumming and lively Mgm comedy, one of Conway's latest directories. American debut of the English Kerr.

title: The Citadel
actors: Robert Donat, Rosalind Russell, Ralph Richardson
description: A young doctor takes on a conduct in a village of miners where he has the opportunity to show honesty and self-denial even if this does not allow him to have a high standard of living. Later he goes to London where he enters high society and, dazzled by success and money, forgets the ethics of the profession. The death of a friend who had come to him to call him back to his duties makes him return to ancient righteousness.
notes: Effective product of the English studies of MGM, based on the novel by A. J. Cronin.

title: The Last Run
actors: George C. Scott, Tony Musante, Trish Van Devere, Aldo Sanbrell
description: Former Chicago gangster Harry Grames, who has retired to Albufeira, Portugal, decides to accompany a killer who has been released from prison from Spain to France. With the two men there is also the woman of the fugitive and the trio is wanted by the police as well as hunted by other criminals who are enemies of the young killer.
notes: Unusual picaresque noir actually started by John Huston (who is also an uncredited co-writer), forced to leave the set due to an argument with Scott. But the absence of the great old man did not affect the final result. The characters are splendid, their story desperate.

title: Piedone lo sbirro
actors: Bud Spencer, Adalberto Maria Merli, Enzo Cannavale, Juliette Mayniel, Raymond Pellegrin, Mario Pilar, Angelo Infanti
description: In Naples, police commissioner Rizzo, known as Piedone, has always been respected for his good-natured nature and for his "preventive" methods, based on the deterrent of punches. One of his direct superiors disapproves of the metosi, and when the Marseillais arrive in the city the situation becomes difficult.
notes: Piedone is the character who made Bud Spencer's fortune in the 70s, in the films in which he did not appear alongside Terence Hill. This is the first of the series, a kind of classic punch comedy.

title: The Pursuit of D.B. Cooper
actors: Robert Duvall, Kathryn Harrold, Treat Williams
description: On Thanksgiving Day in 1971, a man jumps out of a plane flying three thousand meters high with the help of four parachutes and the comfort of $ 200,000 stolen. The unleashed manhunt is colossal and involves cops and bounty hunters, plus a diehard insurance company detective. The incident actually happened and it excited American public opinion a lot.
notes: Treat William has already carried his thick eyebrows around in Sidney Lumet's "The Prince of the City". Robert Duvall in his life had an Oscar and three nominations, but he would always deserve at least three times.

title: The Prisoner of Zenda
actors: Ronald Colman, Douglas Fairbanks jr., Madeleine Carroll, C. Aubrey Smith, Raymond Massey, Mary Astor, David Niven, Montagu Love, Philip Sleeman
description: The heir to the throne of Ruritania, kidnapped by a usurper, is saved by a brave English tourist, his double. Compelling and humorous, a small masterpiece of the genre based on a successful novel by Anthony Hope, already brought to the screen several times during the silent.

title: Pennies from Heaven
actors: Steve Martin, Bernadette Peters, Christopher Walken, Jessica Harper
description: Chicago, 1934: a musical agent ruined by the Great Depression projects his illusions into the soothing universe of songs. But it will end tragically.
notes: Musical of great visual and choreographic suggestion, which uses the original engravings of the 30s during the musical numbers in an "alienating" key.

title: The Lone Star
actors: Clark Gable, Ava Gardner, Lionel Barrymore, Beulah Bondi
description: In 1845, Texas was still not part of the United States Confederation. Opinions differ in the country: there are those who want annexation and those who favor independence. In such circumstances, faced with the danger of an armed conflict, the former president of the Confederation decides to make a peaceful attempt to achieve annexation. This is where adventurer David Burke (Clark Gable) steps in.
notes: The story is fictional and the characters are hardly recognizable to the European audience. The cast is, as always in these cases, top notch but fails to be fully convincing. There is also a colorized version.

title: Astérix et Cléopâtre
description: For a bet with Julius Caesar, Cleopatra orders the architect Numerobis, under pain of an atrocious punishment, to build a palace in three months. The architect just has to ask his friends Obelix, Asterix and Panoramix for help. Thanks to good doses of cunning and the magical potion of Panoramix, they neutralize the woes of Amonbofils, rival of their friend, and of Caesar, who does not want to lose.
notes: The animation, as usual, is not very accurate, but compared to the others in the series, this film benefits from greater creative freedom on the original comics.

title: Jackpot
actors: Adriano Celentano, Kate Vernon, Carroll Baker, Christopher Lee
description: A decrepit and narcissistic billionaire funds the search for a product that restores youth, found by a team of child prodigies, led by grandmother Prudence as the guinea pig. The fake Professor Balestra, who, in reality, is the ignorant sage Leonardo (Celentano), brings grandparents and children back to normal. The disjointed moral fable directed by producer Mario Orfini ("Mamba") fails to rise even thanks to the valiant contribution of technicians such as Luciano Tovoli (photo), Giorgio Moroder (music) and Pietro Scalia (editing).

title: 32 Dicembre
actors: Luciano De Crescenzo, Silvio Ceccato, Enzo Cannavale, Massimo Serato
description: Three episodes, three apologues. In the first two figures are "hired" by a lady to indulge the madness of her husband, or who believes herself Socrates, but he says he is not mad: he does it only for the wife who believes herself to be Santippe. In the second, a more than mature couple is hindered by narrow family members, fearful of losing their inheritance. Final in Naples where Alfonso does not have the money to buy the traditional end-of-year "barrels" for his children.
notes: De Crescenzo director, screenwriter and interpreter (he has reserved a small part in each story) juggles between cultural pretensions and entertainment. With him a cast of excellent Neapolitan actors.

title: 3 Ninjas
actors: Chad Power, Max Elliott Slade, Michael Treanor, Victor Wong
description: Rocky, Colt and Tum Tum are three Southern California kids. Their father, FBI agent Sam Douglas, is investigating a dangerous arms dealer, Hugo Snyder, but in the end who gets in the way are the three young men who are kidnapped by the bad guys. And luckily, since childhood, the three brothers have learned all the tricks on martial arts from their grandfather ... The usual film of unlistenable beatings and screams with the only variation that here the three protagonists are almost microscopic. Seeing them take down mammoth opponents with karate shots, all in all, it's not bad. Apart from that, the film does not otherwise exist.

title: Un genio, due compari, un pollo
actors: Terence Hill, Miou-Miou, Robert Charlebois, Klaus Kinski
description: Joe Thanks, brains up, convinces Locomotive Bill and his friend Lucy to organize a scam against Major Cabot who kept $ 300,000 for the Red Indians. The gang disguises itself, then the major discovers the trick and then loads the money on a stagecoach which is attacked by Thanks. This is the plan that is punctually implemented, but the ending reserves a surprise even for the smart ones.
notes: Of European production but shot in the United States (by a director other times "busy"), the film tells a funny story, but all too intricate and with a very panting rhythm. In practice it is yet another parody of westerns and not the best.

title: The Sins of Rachel Cade
actors: Angie Dickinson, Peter Finch, Roger Moore, Woody Strode
description: During the last world war, Rachel Cade treats indigenous people in a missionary hospital in the Congo. The colonel from the local garrison asks for her as a wife, but Rachel refuses. An English pilot, Paul, crashes near the hospital, and this time it's love at first sight. Then Paul leaves, ignoring that Rachel is pregnant. He will return but, placed in the alternative between the man and the activity at the mission, Rachel chooses the latter. Based on the novel Rachel Cade by Charles Mercer, the film does not lack formal merits and a certain narrative elegance. It is more lacking in terms of the definition of the characters, presented according to cliché.

title: Double Trouble
actors: Elvis Presley, John Williams, Yvonne Romain, Chips Rafferty
description: Jill is in love with singer Guy Lambert, but he is reluctant to marry such a young girl and, as Jill's uncle is also against the wedding, continues his tour. He meets Jill again and saves her from a series of attacks (he is the uncle who wants to take over the girl's fortune). When she comes of age, nothing can stand in the way of the love of the two doves.
notes: Within the limits of what you can ask of a film with Elvis Presley, the story is pleasant enough in its well-calculated musical-sentimental combination, with the addition of a dash of yellow. And, for his fans, "The Pelvis" is the top.

title: Le ragazze di San Frediano
actors: Antonio Cifariello, Rossana Podestà, Giovanna Ralli, Corinne Calvet
description: Andrea known as Bob, a young mechanic, holds up "stories" with five girls at the same time. One of them, Gina, expresses suicidal intentions and Bob, who feels guilty, becomes engaged to her. But here is that Tosca claims to have been seduced by the Don Giovanni, the friend whom Silvana stole from, crushes him and Mafalda leaves him. Bob would only have to leave for the Riviera with Bice, but ...
notes: Zurlini's brilliant directorial debut, from the novel of the same name by Vasco Pratolini, "purged" of its political-social connotations. Good acting by the group of young performers, sustained the narrative rhythm.

title: Plaza Suite
actors: Walter Matthau, Maureen Stapleton, Barbara Harris, Lee Grant
description: On the day of the twenty-fourth anniversary of the wedding, in the same suite in which she spent the first night with her husband, a woman discovers the adulterous relationship of her spouse. A film producer seduces a woman, now a mother, whom he met fifteen years earlier. A mature landowner tries to calm his temperamental daughter who is determined to screw up her marriage at the last minute. A triptych that bears the signature of a very skilled playwright, played by a performer in a shining form. The first level of reading is that of comedy, but each micro-story also contains, in different shades, an undertone of bitterness.

title: Le doulos
actors: Jean-Paul Belmondo, Serge Reggiani, Jean Desailly, Fabienne Dali
description: Maur, just released from prison, kills Gilbert who killed his friend. Then, at the home of his mistress Thérèse, he plans, with his friend Silien, a robbery which, however, fails. Maur is now suspicious of Silien, especially after Thérèse was killed. Arrested, Maur will discover the truth only when he is released from prison: too late because an unstoppable mechanism of death has now been triggered.
notes: A ruthless but excellent "noir", based on the values ??of friendship in the environment of evil and on the fate of destruction that hangs over the characters. Melville tells, as always, with vigor and essentiality. The performance of the interpreters is excellent.

title: Captain Newman M.D.
actors: Gregory Peck, Tony Curtis, Angie Dickinson, Eddie Albert
description: At the head of the neuropsychiatric section at the Camp Colfax military airbase, Captain Newman often finds himself in conflict with his superiors who would demand from him a more speedy recovery of the soldiers under his care. To send them back to fight and perhaps to die. But the reasons of science must prevail over those of the military.
notes: Unusual subject treated in a key even too inclined to comedy, but not without a certain capacity for reflection. From the novel by Leo Rosten, a decorous reduction embellished by the cast.

title: Le vie del Signore sono finite
actors: Massimo Troisi, Jo Champa, Marco Messeri, Massimo Bonetti, Enzo Cannavale, Clelia Rondinella
description: Since Vittoria left him, Camillo has been paralyzed. The disease is clearly psychosomatic, says her doctor, so much so that at the news that Vittoria broke up with her new boyfriend, he immediately starts moving again. Meanwhile, fascism came to power, Camillo went to jail for a joke about the Duce and Vittoria went to live in Paris. Camillo, however, now knows how to move.
notes: Although with some uncertainty, in his third film Troisi confirms that he is not the usual television cabaret artist who has gone to directing, but a full-blown author. Soundtrack by Pino Daniele.

title: Emigrantes
actors: Aldo Fabrizi, Ave Ninchi, Adolfo Celi, Nando Bruno
description: Giuseppe Borbone (Fabrizi), who works as a bricklayer by profession, decides to emigrate to Argentina with the whole family. Nostalgia continues to haunt his wife Adele (Ave Ninchi) who, in the end, convinces her husband to go home. Joseph is about to give up, but Maria's love for an Argentine engineer will make them stay.
notes: It is a film, Aldo Fabrizi's first work, which at its release was judged by critics as too steeped in rhetoric to sincerely describe the condition of the emigrants. Of course, it tends towards the funny and pathetic, but its description is moved and participatory.

title: The Merry Widow
actors: Maurice Chevalier, Jeanette MacDonald, Edward Everett Horton
description: The government of a small state fears that the very wealthy widowed owner of most of the nation's capital will remarry by taking the money abroad. He then sends to Paris, where the woman resides, a young officer of the guard with the mission of capturing the heart (and, consequently, the patrimony) of the lady. Surprises and misunderstandings, but then, inevitably, love triumphs. Struggling with Franz Lehar's famous operetta, Lubitsch finds ground perfectly suited to his best vein. The result is a brilliant film, meticulously calibrated, in short, a product marked by the inimitable Lubitsch touch.

title: Un orso chiamato Arturo
actors: George Segal, Carol Alt, Doris von Thury, Mattia Sbragia
description: Billy, a Rome-based American musician who specializes in soundtracks, is about to go on vacation when a producer urgently asks him for a score. From here begins a very intricate puzzle, with a mysterious Alice looking for a teddy bear, with assorted secret agents, with murdered deaths, transvestites, milirdaires, inventors of synthetic gasoline, and even an Oscar winner. The only valid aspect of the film is the elegance of the setting; otherwise one gets bored with a non-inventive rehashing of various comedies such as The Pink Panther. For the "elephant graveyard" series: meet George Segal and Edmund Purdom.

title: Operation Petticoat
actors: Cary Grant, Tony Curtis, Joan O'Brien, Dina Merrill
description: Partially restored after a bombing, thanks to the "inventive" skills of Officer Nick Holden, the submarine Sea Tiger resumes its movements in the Pacific, under the command of Captain Sherman. After landing on a small island for supplies, Holden gets some female officers left cut off from the departments to be boarded.
notes: A very successful "reinterpretation" of the war epic in the form of a paradoxical comedy, entrusted to skilled filmmakers such as Stanley Shapiro and Maurice Richlin for the screenplay and to Blake Edwards for directing. Grant and Curtis have fun and play along.

title: Don Giovanni
actors: Ruggero Raimondi, Kiri Te Kanawa, José Van Dam, Edda Moser, Teresa Berganza
description: Don Giovanni kills the father of one of his conquests. So, as a joke, he invites his funeral monument to dinner. The statue, animated, drags him to hell. Intelligent cinematic version of Mozart's work, with the setting in a funeral Venice and political metaphor intentions clarified by a caption by Gramsci: Don Giovanni is the immorality that manifests itself when the old is dead and the new is struggling to be born. The orchestra is conducted by Lorin Maazel.

title: The Wings of Eagles
actors: John Wayne, Maureen O'Hara, Dan Dayley, Ward Bond
description: In 1919 Frank W. "Spig" Wead is a Navy air pilot who argues for the importance of aviation in the future. His career is dazzling, which however distances him from his wife and family life. After a fall he remains paralyzed, but finds the strength to react, becoming a successful writer and screenwriter. After Pearl Harbor, rejoin the Navy. The life of Frank Wead, aviation pioneer and writer, but above all a great friend of Ford, is treated by the director with great affection. According to habit, Ford knows how to mix humor, adventure, drama in a perspective of senile detachment. Enjoyable self-parody with Ward Bond as director John Dodge.

title: Scrooge
actors: Albert Finney, Edith Evans, Kenneth Moore, Alec Guinness
description: It is Christmas Eve in 1860 and everyone is feeling better. All except the wealthy Ebenezer Scrooge who can't stand parties or people, least of all his secretary Bob. At night, however, Scrooge is visited by three ghosts: one revives his youth, the other takes him to Bob's house and the third promises him a gloomy future. Upon awakening Scrooge will never be the same again. Christmas musical based on the classic Dickens tale. Finney is worth seeing as Scrooge and Guinness making the specter.

title: Horror of Dracula
actors: Christopher Lee, Peter Cushing, Carol Marsh
description: Jonathan Harker dies victim of Count Dracula and Lucy, his fiancée, is transformed into a vampire by the diabolical count. It is Professor Van Helsing who uncovers the hideous creature behind Dracula's identity. He is joined by Lucy's brother Arthur and his wife Mina. With their help, Van Helsing will eventually get the better of the vampire, disintegrating him with the light of day. With this personal reinterpretation of the story of Dracula, Terence Fisher relaunches the vampire genre and makes the fortune of the production company Hammer. Dense and essential script at the same time; refined staging, between poetry and terror. Color photography (unusual for the horror genre at the time) and Christopher Lee flawless.

title: Junior Bonner
actors: Steve McQueen, Robert Preston, Ida Lupino, Ben Johnson
description: Junior Bonner is the son of a former rodeo champion who now has a dream of moving to Australia in search of gold. Junior's career is also in decline; when he goes to Prescott, his hometown, his brother Curly wants to involve him in construction business but Junior is not there.
notes: Junior is the loser par excellence, privileged protagonist of Sam Peckinpah's cinema: unable to measure himself with reality but capable of moving and noble gestures. Steve McQueen and Robert Preston are extraordinary. The film is moving and beautiful.

title: The Boys from Brasil
actors: Laurence Olivier, Gregory Peck, James Mason, Lilli Palmer
description: Ezra Liebermann (Olivier), a hunter of Nazis with no more credit, on the recommendation of a young man, who is then killed, investigates almost alone until he discovers an impressive fact: Josef Mengele (Peck), former surgeon of Auschwitz, managed to obtain by genetic manipulation 94 descendants of Hitler. It will be up to Liebermann to face Mengele, in turn abandoned by his accomplices, in a dramatic face to face. In the film there is a bit of everything: from science fiction to horror, passing through the cinema of espionage and political commitment. The suspense is not lacking and there is a curious counter-role for Gregory Peck (but also for Olivier, who had just played the Nazi dentist of "Il maratoneta"). From a novel by Ira Levin.

title: Cross of Iron
actors: James Coburn, James Mason, Maximilian Schell, Senta Berger
description: We are in 1943, on the Russian front; the Germans try to resist the Soviet advance. Captain Stransky is an aristocrat, who would like to obtain the Iron Cross for military valor without deserving it. The valiant corporal Steiner thwarts his attempts and is therefore abandoned with his patrol in the face of the enemy offensive.
notes: For Peckinpah the heroes are the losers, therefore the Germans, and the best of all has the pointed face and lanky gait of James Coburn. War is just a hell of tattered flesh and no morals: we might as well die laughing at it.

title: Robin and the Seven Hoods
actors: Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin, Sammy Davis jr., Bing Crosby, Peter Falk
description: In Chicago in 1930 the fight is between the gangster Carmelo Rapaci and his rival nicknamed Robin Hood. More pleasant for the performers than for the story. Harmless musical comedy of retro taste (in a small part there is also the "Little Caesar" Edward G. Robinson) with the complete Sinatra clan.

title: The Big Circus
actors: Victor Mature, Rhonda Fleming, Peter Lorre, Red Buttons, Vincent Price
description: In order to obtain a loan, the owner (Mature) of a circus accepts the presence of the administrator (Fleming) sent by the bank. Film not very original, but which has a good fluidity of development. Worth a look at least for Peter Lorre who is a clown.

title: Rascal
actors: Bill Mumy, Pamela Toll, Steve Forrest, Elsa Lanchester
description: Two cute little boys would like to raise a little raccoon, but their parents object. Parents are especially afraid of backyard chickens. The boys then try to distract the puppy with more food. Disney remake of an autobiographical tale in the classic style, correct but predictable, of the American house.

title: Beauty and the Beast
actors: George C. Scott, Trish Van Devere, Virginia McKenna, Bernard Lee
description: To save her father, a prisoner in the castle ruled by a monstrous being and guilty only of having picked a rose in his garden, a beautiful girl agrees to marry the Beast thus breaking the spell and freeing the monster-prince from a terrible curse.
notes: Television version of the famous fairy tale by Madame Leprince de Beaumont. Scott received an Emmy nomination for Best Television Actor, as did the creators of the makeup and costumes.

title: Tom Thumb
actors: Russ Tamblyn, Jessie Matthews, Peter Sellers
description: Woodcutter Jonathan and his wife Anna dream of having a child. The Queen of the Woods then gives them a child so small that he is immediately nicknamed Tom Thumb. With a deception two thieves make him steal the treasure of the country. Jonathan is blamed for the theft, but Tom Thumb will save the day.
notes: Musical version of the famous fairy tale of which he accentuates the fantastic tones. Pal was a wizard of handcrafted fantasy.

title: The Light at the Edge of the World
actors: Kirk Douglas, Yul Brynner, Samantha Eggar, Fernando Rey
description: A pirate ship lands on a small island near Cape Horn, its crew occupy the lighthouse and kill two of the three guardians. The third manages to escape by throwing himself into the sea. He will start a fight to the death against the marauders of the filibusta, which will give him a hard time.
notes: Based on a little-known short story by Jules Verne, played by Kirk Douglas as the hero and Yul Brinner as the villain, it is an adventure film that wastes a lot of possibilities and has involuntarily comic overtones. In a small part Massimo Ranieri, who does not understand how he ended up here in the middle.

title: Corruzione al Palazzo di Giustizia
actors: Franco Nero, Fernando Rey, Umberto Orsini, Martin Balsam
description: A surprise search by the industrialist Carlo Goja ends up in a soap bubble due to a tip-off. An investigation promoted immediately by the CSM causes suspicions to be dropped on the president of the Palace of Justice, Judge Vanini, who is therefore removed from office. In his place, Cusani is promoted, but he too discovers almost immediately that corruption cannot be eliminated.
notes: Usual film of fake denunciation that was in fashion a few years ago. The authors went to fish out an old drama by Ugo Betti that told the corrupt Fascist judiciary with metaphysical tones (it was in 1944). That the protagonist is called Cusani is a singular coincidence.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
actors: David Niven, Cantinflas, Robert Newton, Shirley MacLaine, Frank Sinatra, Fernandel
description: An irreproachable English gentleman, Mr. Fogg, is betting with some friends of his club that he will be able to travel around the world in eighty days. The stake is £ 30,000. Accompanied by his young waiter Passepartout the man immediately begins the adventurous journey. Arriving after various adventures in India, he rescues a young local princess from the stake, who was to be sacrificed to the goddess Kali. Soon an English detective joins the party who believes he has identified Mr Fogg as the author of a daring theft at the Bank of England.
notes: Light-hearted, very long and very lively Kolossal, with appearances of various stars (Sinatra, Peter Lorre, Buster Keaton, Marlene Dietrich, the torero Dominguin, John Gielgud etc.). Five Oscars: Best Film, Screenplay, Photography, Editing, Music. However, no Oscar went to the superb David Niven.

title: War and Peace
actors: Audrey Hepburn, Henry Fonda, Mel Ferrer, Vittorio Gassman
description: Natasha (Hepburn) loves Prince Andrei (Ferrer), who must join the army engaged against Napoleon. During her absence she is almost seduced by Anatoli, but Piotr (Fonda), a friend of Andrej, calls her back to her duties as a girlfriend. The prince, having become aware of the facts, breaks his commitment with the girl; but when the two meet again, after the siege of Moscow, he forgives her before dying from the wounds sustained in battle. Natasha and Piotr will discover that they love each other and will be able to crown their feeling.
notes: From the immortal novel by Tolstoy, the director King Vidor obtains a spectacular film, whose interest does not end in the majestic battle scenes (directed by Mario Soldati). But the elephantine weight of the mega-production Ponti-De Laurentiis makes itself felt.

title: 29th Street
actors: Anthony La Paglia, Danny Aiello, Lainie Kazan, Frank Pesce
description: When Frank comes into the world, his mother is taken to the wrong hospital. Fortunately, because the "right" one is destroyed by the flames of a raging fire. When he grows up, Frank gets a stab and the doctors discover a lung tumor, still benign. Today, Christmas Eve 1976, he won six million dollars in the lottery, but he is desperate because there is a mafia boss who is demanding them. The cast, led by Italian-American Anthony La Paglia, looks promising. However, stereotypes about New York's Little Italy are redundant and annoying.

title: Serafino
actors: Adriano Celentano, Ottavia Piccolo, Saro Urzì, Francesca Romana Coluzzi
description: Serafino Fiorin, a somewhat dull shepherd, has a good fortune with women. Both cousin Lidia and prostitute Asmara see nothing strange in ending up in bed with him. Something wrong is instead found by Lidia's father, uncle Agenore, who, seeing that Serafino became rich on the death of his aunt Gesuina, now demands a reparative wedding. Serafino reaches the altar and then thinks about it.
notes: Halfway between the mockery and the exaltation of the simple life of the countryside, Germi certainly does not sign his most memorable film. The only stroke of genius is to have chosen Celentano for a role that is entirely congenial to him, apart from the dialect.

title: Little Lord Fauntleroy
actors: Ricky Schroder, Alec Guinness, Eric Porter, Colin Blakely
description: An old and severe English Lord appoints his American grandson as his heir. He hosts him with him but without his mother, with whom he does not get along. Cold at first, the relations between the grandfather and the grandson gradually become more affectionate and prevent another person from trying to appropriate the title.
notes: Based on a well-known children's novel, the film tries to keep the original's tear rate high. Guinness would be good too, of course, but little Ricky Schroeder challenges anyone's patience.

title: Performance
actors: Mick Jagger, James Fox, Anita Pallenberg
description: A runaway criminal takes refuge in a basement, chased by his accomplices and the police. In the shelter he finds a drugged singer with his two lovers. Man, having sensed the mechanism of the "triangle", insinuates himself into the game, becoming the dominant element and making his other "subjects".
notes: Directorial debut by Nicolas Roeg, who he co-directs with Donald Cammel (the latter also a screenwriter). Evident, starting from the presence of James Fox, the references to _The servant_ of Losey.
