description: A Huston financier discovers, on the death of his hated brother, that he has a son who was raised in a gerontocomio. He recovers it, but Pinocchio (as the young man is called) does not fit the life in which his father would like to insert him. He escapes with the delinquent Lucy Light (female version of Candlewick), knows love and freedom. Then Lucy Light dies, but Pinocchio does not betray himself. Cost a blunder and very little paid at the box office, the film is more wrong than ugly, oppressed by a heap of unrealistic ambitions to which the pulse of the author-performer proves inadequate. We laugh a little, but we yawn a lot.

title: The Room Next Door
actors: Mark Benninghofen, Thomas Patrick, Mary Sellers, Massimo Sarchielli
description: Martin Yakobwsky, a young and brilliant Polish-born lawyer, returns for professional reasons to the Iowa village where he grew up. At first there are difficulties due to the maneuvers of a local politician against a community of laborers, but then threatening memories of a tragedy of which his then girlfriend was the victim and for which a man was sentenced to death. Based on a screenplay by Pupi Avati, Laurenti makes a film in which the atmosphere is appreciated more than the story itself, where the tension has at times some failure.

title: Mardi Gras
actors: Pat Boone, Christine Carere, Tommy Sands, Sheree North
description: The cadets of the Virginia military academy organize a lottery that is giving away a day to spend with the Michèle Marton Diva on the occasion of the New Orleans carnival. The cadet that wins the lottery goes to the city where she tries in vain to get in touch with the famous diva. But the research is not unsuccessful. Instead, he knows a Frenchman, Ivy, with whom he is well. And there is a surprise in store. The real intent of the film seems to propagate the New Orleans carnival, so much the story on which the matter holds is fragile and obvious. Nothing bad, for heaven's sake. But we might as well be prepared.

title: Gastone
actors: Alberto Sordi, Anna Maria Ferrero, Paolo Stoppa, Vittorio De Sica
description: Gastone is "danseur mondain" in a tabarin, always waiting for the great opportunity for more prestigious taguardi. Here he meets Nannina who has all the characteristics to become a diva of the light stage. However, she lacks that of gratitude: taking advantage of a forced absence of Gastone, the girl is hired on her own and becomes famous. He is left with only the memory. Mario Bonnard, long-time navigator of Italian cinema (he had been one of the greatest stars of silent films, and then director for almost forty years), knows how to package a product. And the role of Sordi is a tribute to Petrolini.

title: Threesome
actors: Lara Flynn Boyle, Stephen Baldwin, Josh Charles, Alexis Arquette
description: The computer plays a trick on a boy who is very worried that he has never slept with a girl of his age. He will have to share his room with a boy and a girl. Between the three a strange love "triangle" is established: she falls in love with the shy and awkward young man who, however, feels attracted to his partner. The latter finally courts the girl, but she does not want to know.
notes: All the clichés of films set in colleges combined with a false climate of sexual liberation, irritating and artificial. One can console oneself by thinking that homosexuality is no longer considered a taboo, since it manages to find citizenship even in such a modest job.

title: The Dark Corner
actors: Mark Stevens, Lucille Ball, William Bendix, Kurt Kreuger
description: A private investigator, who at one point found himself in jail because of his partner, cleverly manages to escape a trap hatched by a hitman in a white suit. The killer killed the detective's ex-partner and wants to put the blame on him.
notes: Interesting dark and tense noir, typical of the post-war atmosphere and of a certain realist style of Hathaway: a "moral" investigation even before a detective one.

title: Torta di mele
actors: Alessandra Casella, Laura Devoti, Gian Marco Tognazzi
description: An elderly farmer, widowed, is about to remarry a young Brazilian girl. The daughters welcome the event, while the son finds food for his hatred of his father. But then it all works out. Shifts in sentiment and sentimental maneuvers between small and large complexes of guilt and twists. Depressing the direction of Anna Carlucci.

title: Blindfold: Acts of Obsession
actors: Judd Nelson, Shannen Doherty, Kristian Alfonso, Drew Snyder, Michael Woods, Scott Hillenbrand, Rudolph Willrich, Aleksandra Kaniak
description: Madeleine is very in love with her husband Mike, but their sexual relationship has lost the initial ardor. Dr. Jennings recommends Madeleine to invent seduction and mystery games. Madeleine feels the need to trust his anxieties to his sister Chris, detective of the murderous team, engaged in an investigation concerning a series of sexual murders. Classic American film for voyeurs where little and nothing is seen. In addition to this scam, plot, interpreters and direction are of total banality and amateurism. The transition from the small to the big screen does not benefit from Shannon Doherty, an unexpressive television star, armed only with a nice breast that the viewer just glimpsed and rarely together with his face, given the massive use of stunting.

title: Reality Bites
actors: Winona Ryder, Ethan Hawke, Ben Stiller, Janeane Garofalo, Steve Zahn
description: Lelaina works as an assistant on a local TV and is fired, Vicky is a clerk in a clothing store and is promoted, Troy moves from one job to another, while Sammy does not know how to confess to his folks that he is gay. Lelaina captures the important (and not) moments of the group's life and makes a documentary. But when she starts dating a young executive from another TV, her ambiguous relationship with Troy comes to a head ...
notes: Polite, agile and intelligent, the film proposes its characters, with their actions and their feelings with credibility. The good narrative rhythm and the casual interpretations of the actors help to adequately support the story.

title: Blown Away
actors: Jeff Bridges, Tommy Lee Jones, Forest Whitaker
description: Liam is the most experienced of the Boston police bomb squad. A diabolical Irish terrorist at war with the Crown and the whole world, no Ira, only holy fury. Liam believes that the devil and the past are permanently buried. You are wrong. The comrade of the past has decided to ruin his heroic deeds, with a side of vanity from television close-ups and is committed to blowing like skittles fellow bomb engineers and little family in search of happiness on the notes of U2. Jeff Bridges works as he knows and how he can to thwart the twisted and refined criminal mind of Tommy Lee Jones, who is busy building deadly toys for the triumph of the special effects department. And the fire flares up everywhere, leaving behind it the smell of sulfur, as befits the Luciferian apparitions. Even if everything seems a bit too pretentious and constructed, the games work thanks to the two antagonists and a respectable cast.

title: Striking Distance
actors: Bruce Willis, Sarah Jessica Parker, Dennis Farina, Tom Sizemore
description: Tom Hardy (Willis), a former homicide detective, was demoted to river rescue patrols for publicly challenging the police department about the identity of the serial killer who murdered his father. Convinced that a new seral killer who has recently appeared on the scene is, in fact, the same man who killed his father - and despite the fact that a person has already been jailed and sentenced for that crime - Hardy investigates to catch the killer.
notes: A suspenseful story where the Allegheny and Monongaehla rivers meet, forming Ohio. On paper there are all the essential elements for a good action movie and the show is not lacking, but in no more than a couple of sequences. The script is so complicated and convoluted that it becomes, in the middle of it, absurdly predictable. Finally Willis is forced throughout the film to a sad, frowning expression that doesn't suit him.

title: A Wedding
actors: Mia Farrow, Geraldine Chaplin, Vittorio Gassman, Gigi Proietti, Nina van Pallandt, Desi Arnaz jr., Amy Stryker
description: Dino Corelli and Meringa Brenner get married. Both are sons of enriched fathers and therefore most of the guests at the ceremony are far from fine people. The reception is organized with no expense spared, but is deserted by the exponents of the good society; the day is consumed with hypocrisy, meanness, foolishness and ends with a tragedy that does not lack elements of ridicule. Robert Altman's proverbial malice affects specific social environments and ethnic groups here. With mastery the director of "Nashville" joins in the context of the mega reception and a huge cast, weaving stories and mistreating characters.

title: Blood on the Moon
actors: James Woods, Lesley Ann Warren, Charles Durning, Randi Brooks
description: Sergeant Lloyd Hopkins, of the LAPD, is investigating the killing of a woman, although his intuition leads him to believe that this is not an isolated case. There is a maniac, Lloyd thinks, who has been killing and getting away with it for fifteen years. There is a maniac, thinks Lloyd's wife, who lives in this house and is my husband. This is why, halfway through the investigation, Lloyd is left alone and with a dangerous obsession in his head ...
notes: James B. Harris, former producer of Kubrick, is a truly unique character. This is undoubtedly his best film: Woods is so good and adherent to the character that it makes one fear for his mental health.

title: Trapped in Paradise
actors: Nicolas Cage, Jon Lovitz, Dana Carvey, Mädchen Amick
description: We are on Christmas Eve and the brothers Bill, Alvin and Dave Firpo, three small-caliber delinquents from New York, decide to spend their holidays in a pleasant town called Paradise. In the village there is the First Paradise Bank, and the three bungling rogues think they are combining business with pleasure: they carry out a robbery that leaves a large booty in their hands. But the blow succeeds, the escape does not. The car goes off the road and the clumsy criminals are rescued and hosted by the bank owner's family, who will go bankrupt following the theft. In Paradise, however, everyone is so honest and good that it becomes impossible to harm them.
notes: Struggling through the snow and molasses, "Storm in Paradise" would once have reached the parish hall at its best. Now the presence of Cage and the mechanisms of distribution - to get a good film you have to suffer ten bad ones - require it in the first visions. No one would see a story like that, set in Piedmont and directed by Giorgio (not George) Gallo. But you want to put Pennsylvania!

title: Kika
actors: Victoria Abril, Veronica Forqué, Peter Coyote, Alex Casanovas
description: Kika is a makeup artist who lives with an ambiguous female underwear photographer, Ramon, who is obsessed with his mother's death. Despite an unshakable predisposition to optimism, Kika has some sexual problems with Ramon and often it is Nicholas who solves them. But the vaudeville-style comedy changes at some point and becomes a morbid story of jealousy, revenge, unresolved childhood trauma, serial murders, marital problems, etc. and all this with television as a witness who ends up being a victim of his own. voracity. "Kika" is an unsolved point of connection between Almodòvar's cinematic past and his future: the director zaps his filmography.

title: The Private Navy of Sergeant O'Farrell
actors: Bob Hope, Phyliis Diller, Gina Lollobrigida
description: Problems with women and beer for Infantry Sergeant O'Farrell on a small Pacific island. Final career gasps for Bob Hope. Indecorous, and inglorious career end for a slapstick master like Tashlin.

title: Il toro
actors: Diego Abatantuono, Roberto Citran, Marco Messeri
description: Franco and Loris, the dismissed cow farm attendant and a small farmer on the brink of bankruptcy, are traveling from Northern Italy to Hungary, by truck, by train, on foot. They are accompanied by Corinth, the number five in the world, champion of artificial reproduction, which the two have stolen from the farm and want to sell. And its imposing and helpless rhythm is also the one on which the rhythm of the film is calibrated: smooth and unhurried, with long "ruminating" pauses during which Franco and Loris touch the sadness of war, the desolation of refugees, the arrogance of those who do business in the no man's land of former socialism. A right step for Mazzacurati, bitter, beautiful on the outside, accomplice in the night interiors.

title: Rob Roy
actors: Liam Neeson, Jessica Lange, Tim Roth, John Hurt, Eric Stoltz
description: Rob Roy works as a livestock guard for a marquis, but decides to go on his own. He therefore asks the Marquis for a thousand pounds on loan and gets them at usurer interest. The money, however, is immediately robbed by a penniless bastard of the nobility. The debt would be canceled if Rob Roy agreed to testify against another noble, suspected of plotting for the restoration of the Stuarts. But he is not there.
notes: The background (class struggle and exchange of the elites) ends up prevailing over a character tied to traditional warrior values. Caton-Jones is Scottish, therefore sensitive to the myth of Rob Roy. His work, sometimes redundant, but always diligent, was liked overseas. In Europe less.

title: The Quick and the Dead
actors: Sharon Stone, Gene Hackman, Russell Crowe, Leonardo DiCaprio
description: A mysterious woman arrives in Redemption to kill the diabolical Herod, absolute ruler of Redemption, who once a year cleans the city of all rivals. Organize a series of duels with a cash prize, which attracts killers from all over the West. Herod, however, is the fastest of all and the latest bloody battle always sees him triumphant. But this year the woman asked to take part in the challenge. Raimi is a madman with an encyclopedic and mocking taste for quotation and retelling. Here he changes genre, from horror to western, and here too he focuses on the essence of the genre: no background (only very quick flashbacks), no pauses (if not full of action), but the heart of the western: the shooting. Hilarious jokes, full homage to the bad western of Leone, Siegel and Clint Eastwood. A refined reinterpretation, guaranteed fun.

title: Soleil noir
actors: Michèle Mercier, Daniel Gélin, Valentina Cortese, Louis Seigner
description: On the death of his father, the industrialist Gaston Rodier, his daughter Christine leaves for Sudan to convince his brother Henri to take over the family business. A bit of exoticism and a bit of banality.

title: Le castagne sono buone
actors: Gianni Morandi, Stefania Casini, Patricia Allison, Milla Sannoner
description: Luigi, a young director, unscrupulous and womanizer, meets Carla, an innocent student. He tries, she doesn't give in because she only believes in lasting feelings. He then introduces her to his parents, but when he finally could have her he prefers to disappear in order not to disappoint her. Some time later he meets Carla's sister, back from a love disappointment and a suicide attempt. At the thought of Carla, Luigi understands her emptiness and returns to her, determined to put his head right.
notes: Germi in the version of good feelings does not know how to make the most of his profession, in a film without malice and rather bigoted.

title: The Road to Wellville
actors: Anthony Hopkins, Bridget Fonda, Matthew Broderick
description: We are in Battle Creek, Michigan Falls, in 1907, and it is here that Dr. John Harvey Kellogg, the inventor of corn flakes, peanut butter and over seventy-five types of so-called "healthy foods", leads and directs "The San ", his beloved health clinic. But not all that glitters is gold. Tragic events are stirring under the quiet façade. Waste of costumes and actors for a boring and repetitive story. No surprise is the recurring feeling that the same rotting germs Kellogg talks about in referring to meat have attached themselves to the celluloid in the film.

title: I. Q.
actors: Meg Ryan, Walter Matthau, Tim Robbins, Lou Jacobi
description: We are in the mid-1950s and Einstein (Matthau) has spent twenty years teaching and researching at Princeton. Her very intelligent niece Catherine (Ryan) is engaged to a psychologist (Fry), academically worthy of her, but overly accommodating on the ethical level. Foreseeing an unsatisfactory future for Catherine, Einstein personally takes it upon himself to find her a new love object. And although Catherine is determined to marry a genius like her uncle Albert, it is Ed (Robbins), a greasing guy at the local garage, who hits Einstein as Prince Charming in overalls for his niece. Director Schepisi wants to be inspired by certain black and white comedies populated by intrepid scientists who are reckless and kind, funny and crafty.

title: Boys on the Side
actors: Whoopi Goldberg, Mary-Louise Parker, Drew Barrymore
description: For the uninhibited and cynical night-club singer Jane (Goldberg), the Big Apple has become sickening. Dumped by her best friend and fired from her last gig, she decided to go to Los Angeles. Robin (Parker), a real estate agent, hopes to escape the grim reality with a nostalgic return to San Diego, following the same path she took as a child with her mother and brother. To do this, he puts an ad in the newspaper offering a ride to the West Coast. The first person to answer is Jane. The duo makes a stop in Pittsburgh to visit Jane's friend Holly (Barrymore), and Holly decides to tag along. She has two surprises in store for her traveling companions: one that she is pregnant; two, who unwittingly also became an outlaw. But Holly is not the only one to reserve surprises ...
notes: Discreet craft, but excess of rhetoric in the direction of Herbert Ross, who drowns his ability in comedy in tears.

title: Henry V
actors: Kenneth Branagh, Emma Thompson, Brian Blessed, Paul Scofield, Ian Holm, Ronald Pickup
description: Having ascended the throne of England in 1413, after a youth spent together with reckless friends, Henry V immediately proved to be a wise and morally rigorous king. Two years after his accession to the throne, he declares war on Charles VI, King of France, because he wants to claim his hereditary rights over that kingdom. Landed with an army not very numerous compared to the enemy, but disciplined, he manages to bring down the town of Harfleur and defeat the enemiesk in the bloody battle of Anzicourt. Second staging of the famous Shakespearean drama, the film) which figuratively is closer to Welles than to Laurence Olivier) was the debut of Kenneth Branagh, enfant prodige of English cinema. For the costumes Phyllis Dalton got the Oscar.

title: Caroline?
actors: Stephanie Zimbalist, Pamela Reed, George Grizzard, Patricia Neal, Dorothy McGuire
description: Caroline Carmichael, who everyone believed to have died for years with her mother in a car accident, suddenly shows up at the home of her father who has since remarried. Caroline's influence on her stepbrothers Winston and Heidi is frowned upon by their mother, Grace, with whom a dramatic disagreement arises over the education of the child, born with severe handicaps. A young woman who mysteriously "resurrects", bitter conflicts over an unhappy woman with serious mental and physical problems: melodramatic material treated with little measure. Beware of old glories Patricia Neal and Dorothy McGuire.

title: L'amore molesto
actors: Anna Bonaiuto, Angela Luce, Peppe Lanzetta, Licia Maglietta
description: Amalia, a woman in her sixties, the separated wife of a poor man who makes a living painting marines and gypsies for the fairs and markets of the Neapolitan suburbs, is found dead at sea. She is wearing only a red lace bra, too youthful and expensive for her. The daughter Delia, who has long since left her hometown and lives in Bologna, returns to Naples to shed light on the mysterious death. She tries to reconstruct her mother's last days, retraces her life tormented by her husband's jealousy and encounters ambiguous men, inhabitants of a violent and prevaricating world. Less compact than "Death of a Neapolitan mathematician", this film is more risky, precisely because it stands on the dangerous limit of the stereotype

title: Un monde sans pitié
actors: Hippolyte Girardot, Mireille Perrier, Yvan Attal, Jean-Marie Rollin
description: The young Hippo allows himself to be supported by his younger brother, who sells drugs. On the other hand, it does nothing, except for a few games of poker and meeting and ditching girls. The meeting with Nathalie, which is his exact opposite, seems to give him a reason for activity, but a trivial mishap separates their destinies. When they meet again, perhaps Hippo finds some stimulus to "live". Eric Rochant's directorial debut offers an example of a generation of young people now apathetic towards society. A credible portrait and context, for a film that portrays a worrying existential void.

title: Never So Few
actors: Frank Sinatra, Gina Lollobrigida, Peter Lawford, Steve McQueen
description: Captain Tom Reynolds commands the scarce US troops stationed in northern Burma. Having gone to Calcutta, he meets the Italian Carla Vesari who lives with a certain Regas and who rejects the captain's court. After several war actions, the two meet again at the hospital where Tom is hospitalized and declare their (now mutual) love. But serious events are still gathering in the life of the captain.
notes: Sturges directs with fairness but without passion (his field was westerns), and the film remains a melò without art or part, with big stars at the limit of the bearable.

title: The Sweeper
actors: C. Thomas Howell, Janet Gunn, Kathrin Lautner, Kristen Dalton, Jeff Fahey
description: Mark Goddard, who survived the massacre of his family as a boy, is now a brisk cop, is in a crisis with his wife and is obsessed with the desire for revenge. Hired by a death squad, made up of former agents, with the promise that he will be able to find the names of those who killed his family, Mark ends up discovering precisely in these "executioners" the killers he was looking for. The clichés screw up on themselves, offering the viewers of this TVmovie a show without surprises. C. Thomas Howell had not started his career badly: we prefer to keep reminding ourselves of him in "The Boys of 56th Street" and in "The Hitcher".

title: Jonathan degli orsi
actors: Franco Nero, Floyd 'Red Crow' Westerman, John Saxon, Melody Robertson
description: Jonathan, a six-year-old boy, witnesses the murder of his parents and finds himself alone in the forest. Saved by a bear and its cub, he leads a wild life until he is found and adopted by Tawanka, chief of the Modoc Indian tribe. Tawanka lies dying when Jonathan suddenly reappears and returns to the village after years of absence. Tawanka asks him to take back the territory usurped by the white men. Jonathan vows to protect the tribe. One day, Jonathan rushes to the aid of a trapped bear and drives the hunters to flight. He then realizes that the bear was the cub that he grew up with in the forest: "his first friend". The spirit of Tawanka now dwells in it.
notes: A simple story, perhaps obvious, but shot with professionalism and full of twists. For fans, a dip back that fascinates.

title: Viva San Isidro!
actors: Marco Leonardi, Lumi Cavazos, Diego Abatantuono
description: In the village of San Isidro, a small football tournament takes place. To make the marks on the ground, the organizers make do with what looks like white fertilizer. The San Isidro striker, after a night with the girl, has soft legs, but as soon as he falls face down and sniffs the white powder, he jumps up and scores goal after goal. With a bit of an exoticism and a lot of predictable situations, the debut film Cappelletti runs quietly until twenty minutes from the end. When Abatantuono finally takes the field, in the role of a priest armed with a gun, there is an amusing essay of skill by the actor (who is also the producer of the film). Based on a short story by Cacucci, the film is skillfully photographed by Italo Petriccione.

title: Outbreak
actors: Dustin Hoffman, Rene Russo, Morgan Freeman, Donald Sutherland, Cuba Gooding jr., Kevin Spacey
description: Colonel Sam Daniels, a US military medical officer, is sent by the government to Africa to investigate an unknown virus that is decimating villagers. The dead, already numerous, are piled up like firewood and the survivors risk facing the same end. Sam tries to warn his superiors, but in response the colonel is dismissed from office without giving him any explanation.
notes: Expanded and fragmentary screenplay, pompous and heavy direction. Yet Petersen proved that he can do thriller. His are "U-Boot 96" and "In the center of the viewfinder".

title: I Want to Go Home
actors: Adolph Green, Gérard Depardieu, Micheline Presle, Laura Benson
description: A well-known American cartoonist arrives in Paris where a professor who admires him involves him in the hectic city life. From a story by Jules Feiffer a somewhat intellectualistic but funny film. The protagonist is one of the great authors of musicals of the 1950s ("Variety Show", for one thing).

title: Hiroshima, mon amour
actors: Emmanuelle Riva, Eiji Okada, Bernard Fresson, Stella Dassas, Pierre Barbaud
description: In Hiroshima, a French actress knows and loves a Japanese. But he knows that, like another love during the war, this too will end in oblivion. Masterpiece written by Marguerite Duras.

title: Death and the Maiden
actors: Sigourney Weaver, Ben Kingsley, Stuart Wilson, Jonathan Vega
description: On a stormy night, in an isolated beach house, in an unspecified country, Paulina Escobar (Weaver) is awaiting the return of her husband Gerardo (Wilson), who has accepted the assignment to lead a commission that will investigate the violations of human rights in the years of dictatorship. Later comes the man who gave Gerardo a ride. Paulina realizes that it is the doctor who tortured her fifteen years ago. The film, based on the three-character drama by Chilean Ariel Dorfman, is transformed in the hands of Polanski into a miraculous exercise in the cinema of cruelty, conducted by a camera that never imposes its presence, but follows the faces, approaches. , investigates, moves away on long shots that frame the characters in a perfect balance of proportions. Great game of the three interpreters. Stuart Wilson stands up to the two holy monsters with an undertone part.

title: La scuola
actors: Silvio Orlando, Anna Galiena, Fabrizio Bentivoglio, Antonio Petrocelli
description: A rainy October morning. Professor Majello, a dull woman, no longer enthusiastic, is preparing the lesson timetable. Among the many colleagues, Professor Vivaldi stands out, entirely absorbed in teaching, and the energetic and aggressive vice-principal Sperone. An interminable school year passes; but the frenzy of the latest questions and the anguish of the ballots have removed from Vivaldi the attraction he has always felt for Majello.
notes: The actors work and Luchetti lightly draws this "world apart". In an (all too) explicit way, the ceiling of the school collapses and crushes expectations, misunderstood loves, frustrations.

title: Tribute to a Bad Man
actors: James Cagney, Irene Papas, Don Dubbins, Lee Van Cleef, Stephen McNally
description: Jeremy Rodock (Cagney), a Wyoming horse breeder, hides a generous heart under his hard and vengeful rind. The girl he wants is a little hard to understand.
notes: More than the development of the story itself, the gloomy description of life in the Old West convinces. First American film for Irene Papas.

title: Die Schlangengrube und das Pende
actors: Lex Barker, Christopher Lee, Karin Dor, Carl Lange, Vladimir Medar
description: A count executed for multiple murder of virgins needs the blood of another maiden to obtain immortality and take revenge on the descendants of those who condemned him. From a famous tale by Poe, a dignified German production with Christopher Lee. Directed by such a specialist.

title: The Experts
actors: John Travolta, Arye Gross, Kelly Preston
description: Two New Yorkers believe they have been hired to open a nightclub in Nebraska, but teach, unbeknownst to them, at a spy school in the USSR. Simple comedy from every point of view, with noticeable nostalgia for the good old days of the Cold War. Travolta and Preston subsequently married.

title: The Next Voice You Hear
actors: James Whitmore, Nancy Davis, Lilian Bronson
description: In Anytown, an average town inhabited by average American men and women, God makes His voice heard over the radio. Interesting idea, but the script lacks seriousness and sentimentality. Produced by Dore Schary, former Oscar for the screenplay of the "City of Boys", and in 1951 president of MGM.

title: Killer Klowns from Outer Space
actors: Grant Cramer, Suzanne Snyder, John Vernon
description: They look like circus clowns, in reality they are bloodthirsty alien beings. Low-cost fantahorror, ordinary in plot development but very captivating thanks to the lively staging and handfuls of black humor. A cult of its kind. Never released in Italian cinemas, it arrived directly on video.

title: Mollo tutto
actors: Renato Pozzetto, Barbara D'Urso, Tamara Donà, Luigi Petrucci
description: Franco (Pozzetto) is a Milanese butcher who lives in Rome. His wife Bettina (D'Urso) and daughter Melissa (Donà) would like to turn the delicatessen into a boutique because they are ashamed with their friends. Franco bears everything with resignation. In the meantime, however, he is preparing for a big step: changing his identity into that of an Arab and disappearing from circulation. He succeeds, but a policeman stops him as an illegal immigrant and sends him to a country in North Africa. Pozzetto's comical-pathetic attempt, directed bluntly by a television director. Soporific.

title: Tom Jones
actors: Albert Finney, Susannah York, Hugh Griffith, Edith Evans, Diane Cilento
description: Lovingly raised by a wealthy philanthropist along with his nephew and heir Blifil, Tom Jones, the son of unknowns, is as likable and generous as Blifil is a self-righteous and selfish scoundrel. Expelled from the house by the philanthropist for the mischief of his nephew, Tom Jones will take, after endless hardships, a series of sensational revenge, both on the love and dynastic level. From the novel by Henry Fielding (1707-1754), a "reduction" with a sparkling rhythm, full of biting irony. One of the finest examples of 1960s British cinema.

title: Amadeus
actors: Tom Hulce, F. Murray Abraham, Elizabeth Berridge, Simon Callow
description: Antonio Salieri, former court musician of Emperor Joseph II, recalls his relationship with Mozart to a young priest in the asylum where he is imprisoned. To punish the God of genius granted to a "rascal" like the young man from Salzburg and not to himself, Salieri meditates to ruin him and to steal his glory by attributing the last "Requiem" that Mozart is unable to finish before his death. Based on a fictional hypothesis originally due to Pushkin and the theatrical work that Peter Shaffer has drawn from it, the Czechoslovakian Milo_ Forman directs a film of great spectacular impact, of fascinating suggestions. Huge success and 8 Oscars.

title: La dottoressa ci sta col colonnello
actors: Nadia Cassini, Lino Banfi, Alvaro Vitali, Malisa Longo
description: While recruit Arturo Mezzancolla puts his virile might to good use, his colonel, Anacleto Punzone, is poorly gifted in this regard. When, by the American doctor Eva Russel, the opportunity arises for the officer to exchange, without the soldier's knowledge, the two ... apparatuses, the transplant is carried out. But the results are not what the colonel hoped for.
notes: Collection of jokes, particularly heavy and sleazy.

title: Message to Garcia
actors: Wallace Beery, Barbara Stanwyck, John Boles, Alan Hale, Mona Barrie
description: In 1898, during the Cuban revolt against Spain, the United States sent a secret message to the general who commands the rebels. Assorted adversities.
notes: Discreet bow of a historical fact, shot in comedy cadences with gritty stars.

title: Sostiene Pereira
actors: Marcello Mastroianni, Stefano Dionisi, Nicoletta Braschi, Daniel Auteuil
description: In Portugal, the Salazarist dictatorship has crept into the country, while the Civil War is rampant in neighboring Spain and Mussolini is in power in Italy. Pereira, a meek and fat old journalist, would like to ignore all this, to deal only with the books he loves. Spied on by his concierge, he is content to listen to the news that the waiter Manuel gives him. Until the encounter with two "subversive" young people, Monteiro and Marta, puts him in front of the pressure of dramatic reality.
notes: The film, which Faenza has taken from the homonymous, successful novel by Tabucchi, knows how to render certain characters. It does not know how to render violence, represented according to the inflated clichés of political cinema and underlined by the unbearable music of the always the same Morricone.

title: Heavenly Creatures
actors: Melanie Lynskey, Kate Winslet, Sarah Peirse
description: New Zealand, 1952. Authentic story, taken from the diary of one of the two protagonists of the terrible news story. Juliet and Pauline, two 14-year-old schoolmates, form a morbid friendship between them. The girls rebel against the conformism and greyness of the society that surrounds them and give free rein to their imagination: they take refuge in their little unreal world, contrary to the hypocrisy of the family and the formalism of the school. When Pauline's mother threatens to separate them, the girl doesn't hesitate to kill her. Peter Jackson comes from the most bloody and smashing horror, and this passage to the "high" cinema (honored with a Silver Lion in Venice) retains traces of his heterodox past. Delusional dream moments, with appearances of a double of Orson Welles, the erotic idol of the two protagonists. The film is bizarre and obnoxious (girls are no better than the world they rebel against), and it is possible to prefer other, more "dirty" titles by the same director.

title: Prêt-à-porter
actors: Kim Basinger, Linda Hurt, Julia Roberts, Tim Robbins, Marcello Mastroianni, Sophia Loren
description: While in Paris the activity for the most important fashion show in the world is bustling. In all this chaos, the head of the Fashion Council is suddenly found dead in his limo. Although he is choked on a ham sandwich, police believe it to be murder. In the circle of suspects his wife, with whom he had not spoken for years, and his mistress, a famous designer, present at the fashion show. The investigation is underway, but the show must continue. The film is not nearly as bad as they had reviewed it in America. It is, if you like, in the "light" vein of Altman and perhaps it is also "smart". The screen is there and does not capture us, even if normal physiognomies like Tim Robbins and Julia Roberts (the most appropriate episode) and Teri Garr and Danny Aiello (the most free) circulate in history. But, as always with Altman, the actors work (a doubt about the Loren-Mastroianni couple's self-irony); the camera seems to have a life of its own, adrenaline and acid are in circulation. It is not sulphurous, it is not a masterpiece, but it is still an Altman.

title: Barcelona
actors: Taylor Nichols, Chris Eigeman, Tushka Bergen
description: Ted is in Barcelona where he works for the branch of a multinational; she is also recovering from a bad relationship. The unexpected arrival of his unwelcome cousin Fred, a member of the US Navy, puts an end to his loneliness. Fred is in charge of resolving some issues relating to NATO. One evening the couple of cousins ??runs into Marta who, with friends, is on her way to a masquerade party. The woman mistakes Fred's Navy uniform for a costume, thinks the two Americans are heading to the same party, and invites them to follow. In the following days, Ted's social life takes off inexplicably.
notes: The comedy of sentimental misunderstandings is inevitable and is run by Whit Stillman with witty humor, bittersweet touches and a keen eye on the cultural differences between the two countries. On the other hand, Stillman tells his story as an American in Spain (in the early 1980s), married to a Spaniard and who has continued to commute between Manhattan and Barcelona ever since.

title: Miami Rhapsody
actors: Antonio Banderas, Mia Farrow, Sarah Jessica Parker, Gil Bellows
description: Gwyn is a young advertising woman who has to deal with her marriage to Matt, with whom she has been living for some time. Convinced that she longs for a marriage like that of her parents Nina and Vic, Gwyn realizes, soon after the engagement, that all members of her family have extramarital affairs. It would take Woody Allen to give some original verve to such a concentration of clichés. And instead there is only Mia Farrow, who is no longer a couple with Woody, but manages to seduce and abandon Banderas. And this is the only surprise. For the rest, we are navigating on a TV serial script, the kind that aspires to write the protagonist of the film.

title: Goldfinger
actors: Sean Connery, Honor Blackman, Gert Fröbe, Shirley Eaton
description: Goldfinger is a mysterious businessman suspected of leading a gold smuggling organization. James Bond is put in charge of the case and manages to get so close to Goldfinger's headquarters that he falls into his hands. He has a plan to attack Fort Knox, the United States' gold reserve and one of the most guarded and safest places in the world, but James is on a war footing ...
notes: One of the best James Bond movies. The scene in which Connery comes out of the water, takes off her wetsuit and shows off an evening dress with a boutonniere is in all Bondian anthologies. The other known scene where he is being cut in half by a laser is perhaps less well known.

title: Satan Never Sleeps
actors: William Holden, Clifton Webb, France Nuyen, Athene Seyler
description: In 1949, in southern China occupied by the troops of Mao Dzedong, two Catholic missionaries, the elderly Father Bovard and the young Father O 'Banion, were arrested for no reason and subjected to harsh pressure from Colonel Ho San. The officer meets and falls in love with Siu Lan, a Chinese Christian, who is asked to give up her faith.
notes: Leo McCarey, director of exquisite theatrical and cinematographic comedies ("The Marx Brothers Blitzkrieg"), involved in an operation of obvious anti-Maoist propaganda. There would be nothing too bad if the film wasn't really flimsy.

title: Orders to Kill
actors: Paul Massie, Irene Worth, James Robertson Justice, Miki Iveria
description: Captain Sommers is paratrooped in Paris in '44 with the order to kill a traitor of the Resistance. At the end of the war we find out that the man was innocent. More than war or spying asquith deals with psychologies and obsessions.

title: Night Visions
actors: Loryn Locklin, James Remar, Penny Johnson, Bruce MacVittie
description: Los Angeles is terrified of a maniac who kills young women and then abandons their corpses with open arms and legs, that is, "star-shaped". Sergeant Mackey thus has three problems: finding the killer, recovering from his recent divorce, and putting up with that silly psychology student he was given as a partner. The girl is called Sally and she has night visions. The film doesn't always work and, in particular, the killer is really easy to spot. But there are two or three visions that Craven packs with great skill. And then there is Loryn Locklin ("Filofax", "2013-The Fortress") who has never looked so good again.

title: The Lonely Passion of Judith Hearne
actors: Maggie Smith, Bob Hoskins, Wendy Hiller, Marie Kean, Ian McNeice
description: Due to the bigoted environment of her city, Judith Hearne (Smith), a Dublin spinster, falls into the abyss of loneliness and alcoholism after meeting a peer with whom she sketches a love affair. Dublin lends its Joycean squalor to this ordinary story of marginalization directed by an old English director of great renown. Maggie Smith is naturally extraordinary. At his side the always good Bob Hoskins.

title: Someone Like Me / A Death in the Family
actors: Tony Curtis, Roger Moore, Diane Cilento, Reginald Mars
description: The film brings together two episodes of the TV series "The Persuaders": in "Someone Like Me" Brett Sinclair, the very rich lord, tells his friend Danny Wilder, a light-hearted New York Jew, about how he was attacked and kidnapped. Could someone have created a double of the baronet? The truth is even more disturbing. In "A Death in the Family" someone is exterminating the noble family of Brett Sinclair ... The, tied together by the same character (who is not the protagonist), are cunningly passed off as a movie.

title: Zitti e Mosca
actors: Alessandro Benvenuti, Athina Cenci, Massimo Ghini, Alida Valli, Novello Novelli, Daniele Trambusti, Pina Cei
description: Before, during and after the annual Unity Festival, in a town near Florence.
notes: Types of all kinds, with political and / or existential problems. Sketching sometimes too easy, but also non-trivial situations, cultured and highlighted in their validity of authentic human depth.

title: Butch and Sundance: The Early Days
actors: William Katt, Tom Berenger, Jeff Corey, Christopher Lloyd, Brian Dennehy
description: Young Butch Cassidy gets out of jail on parole. Harry Longbaum, a skilled gunslinger, refuses to join him. Then Butch witnesses the capture of Hanks, a friend of his, who believes he was betrayed by him. Kid reappears and has changed his mind. The escaped Hanks forces Butch into a duel and is killed. With a spectacular train robbery, the two partners then begin their legend. The film, which wanted to renew the glories of the previous success with Newman and Redford, actually describes the beginning of the partnership between the two outlaws. With the usual touches of irony, Lester packs a captivating if somewhat fragmented film.

title: Light Sleeper
actors: Willem Dafoe, Susan Sarandon, Dana Delany, David Clennon
description: John is a drug dealer who works in the service of the beautiful Ann. A difficult life. John reunites with ex-wife Marianne; the two make love, but then she runs away. Marianne told him she got out of the drug addiction, but that's not true. When John discovers her by chance, she kills herself out of shame. John retaliates by killing the man who gave her the drug. Ann remains friends with him and visits him in jail. Schrader (at the time chooser of "Taxi Driver"), in a New York symbolically invaded by waste, tells us about a tragic redemption; great interpretations of Dafoe and Sarandon.

title: What's Eating Gilbert Grape?
actors: Johnny Depp, Juliette Lewis, Leonardo DiCaprio, Mary Steenburgen
description: Endora, a remote Iowa town, population 1091 souls. Gilbert is a young man, little more than a boy. He has a mother whose weight, over 250 pounds, is slowly destroying the foundations of the house. She hasn't left the house for years and lives by eating, smoking and watching television all the time, so much so that she has become a sort of monstrous attraction for the kids who come to spy on her from the window. Gilbert's younger brother is handicapped. Unable to fend for himself, but very capable of getting into trouble, he is guarded and cared for lovingly by Gilbert. One day an unknown woman arrives in Endora and triggers a series of unexpected events.
notes: Hallstrom does not push the pedal of emotion with the handicapped, he does not make irony about his mother, he is not indignant with the children of the village who spy on her as a freak. He photographs tasty details, bleak stories, with the same measured intolerance and the same understanding of his protagonist. Very good Depp and DiCaprio, right and (for once) nice Juliette Lewis.

title: Autumn Leaves
actors: Joan Crawford, Cliff Robertson, Vera Miles, Lorne Greene
description: Milly (Crawford) is still a very beautiful middle-aged woman. Milly falls in love, reciprocated, with Burt (Robertson), a man much younger than her. In short, the two decide to get married. He is a kind and nice young man who, however, after the wedding, turns out to be psychically ill. At the root of his depression is the betrayal of his first wife consummated with Burt's own father. Milly works hard to try and get him to heal. Crawford's interpretation is incisive. Robert Aldrich, a versatile director, although not at ease in psychological drama, directs with a sure hand.

title: Corleone
actors: Giuliano Gemma, Michele Placido, Claudia Cardinale, Francisco Rabal
description: In the Sicilian village of Corleone Vito Gargano and Michele Labruzzo are friends. It so happens that the first is a laborer turned mafia, the second a trade unionist ...
notes: An excessive cast (Gemma, Placido, la Cardinale) for such a modest film. The protagonist is vaguely inspired by the boss Luciano Liggio.

title: Lisbon Story
actors: Rüdiger Vogler, Patrick Bauchau, i Madredeus, Sofia Benard Da Costa
description: The story begins with a postcard and a somewhat cryptic message: "Dear Phil. I can't go on m. O. S.! S. O. S. - Come to Lisbon with all your equipment a. S. A. P.! Big hug. Fritz". Who's Who? And what do all those abbreviations mean? The S. O. S., of course it is clear. And the a.s.a.p. it only reinforces the urgency: come as soon as possible ("As Soon as Possible"). But m. or. s.? Only those who work in the cinema can know that it is an ancient and rather strange term that stands for "silent", that the expression came up in the late 1920s and that it means "Mit-on-Sound" ). The postcard was sent by a director, Friedrich Monroe, to his friend Phillip Winter, a sound engineer.
notes: A film without borders that has the lightness and acumen of the first Wenders, who knows how to move around Lisbon as languid as a fado and manages to deny any proclamation about the death of cinema.

title: Little Women
actors: Winona Ryder, Susan Sarandon, Trini Alvarado, Kirsten Dunst, Claire Danes, Christian Bale
description: It is always the story of Jo, Meg, Amy and Beth, sisters who grow up in Concord raised by their mother during the absence of their father.
notes: Accurate, well directed and well interpreted (Ryder is excellent), this elegant, slightly retro version of Alcott's novel does not look bad compared to the previous ones, indulging in some pre-feminist forcing.

title: Bullets over Broadway
actors: John Cusack, Chazz Palminteri, Dianne Wiest, Jennifer Tilly
description: New York in the 1920s. David Shayne is a young playwright who can't find the funding to bring his play to the stage. The only opportunity is offered to him by a boss who in exchange demands an important role for his protégé, Olive. The young woman shows up for rehearsals, alongside professional actors who have in the meantime been hired, and turns out to be incapable. Reducing the presence of the "registered letter" on the scene is impossible: a gangster, Cheech, watches full time for compliance with the agreements. But Cheech begins to intervene on the texts, proposes cuts and lines to the script, to make the dialogues more credible. David also doesn't object because Cheech's contribution is enormously beneficial to his work. A beautiful and very small story for Allen's twenty-fifth film, who plays lightly with his characters, teases them, accompanies them in the story, with panache, tenderness and melancholy.

title: Blame It on the Bellboy
actors: Dudley Moore, Bryan Brown, Patsy Kensit
description: We are in Venice. Scarpa is a mobster in the sights of his former cronies. The killer is called Charlton and arrives (under a false name of Mr. Lawton) on a plane, where there are also a Mr. Orton and a Mr. Horton, in quite other busy matters. The three end up staying in the same hotel; at that point, a messenger will think about shuffling the three names and the cards, with consequent trouble for everyone.
notes: Mark Herman, on his directorial debut, moves on the slippery ground of the gangster-comedy with a certain mastery of rhythm and a discreet elegance in the overall touch. Between thrill and parody the second wins. Nothing special, but fun nonetheless.

title: The Half-Naked Truth
actors: Lupe Velez, Lee Tracy, Eugene Pallette
description: A barker, who goes around town fairs exhibiting his girlfriend in belly dancing, manages, with a series of cheats, to make it to Broadway. He and his accomplices, however, do not hold up to success and return to their former life. One of the first comedies of La Cava in which his style comes out: lightness and triumph of the imagination.

title: The Other Woman
actors: Jill Eikenberry, Laura Leighton, Lloyd Bridges
description: Tessa is separated from her husband. The man got together with a girl, Carolyn, a young and attractive California model. Tessa is left with her two daughters, Kate and Lara who, like her, hate their father's new partner. But one day Tessa is diagnosed with cancer. The woman then, having a few months of life, tries to bring her daughters closer to Carolyn who will have to consider, after her death, their new mother. Already included in the television series "Stories of girls and boys", the film tackles the theme of illness and abandonment without false shame. Tinged with sentimentality without being too sentimental, it speaks of the difficult couple and generational relationships.

title: The Shadow
actors: Alec Baldwin, John Lone, Penelope Ann Miller, Peter Boyle
description: Lamont Craston is apparently a bored New York billionaire. To tell the truth, in ancient times he had been a tyrannical Tibetan baron with magical powers, however, brought back to the right path by a holy man. Now he's moved to New York and wanders around the city at night, using his prodigious powers to right wrongs as the Shadow Man.
notes: A well-known, typed and encoded character from his previous media incarnations is picked up and fed into the special effects blender. It is one of the most used systems by Hollywood to package a product that aims for success. Too bad that in the meantime much of the verve that characterized the original from the 1930s has been lost.

title: Quiz Show
actors: John Turturro, Ralph Fiennes, Paul Scofield, Rob Morrow, Dick Goodwin, David Paymer, Hank Azaria, Christopher McDonald, Johann Carlo, Mira Sorvino, Elizabeth Wilson, Allan Rich
description: New York 1958. On television, a quiz show by NBC called "Twenty-One", sponsored by a well-known pharmaceutical company, was very successful. Herbie Stempel, a Brooklyn simpleton of Jewish origin, has been the undisputed champion for weeks. But polls show that he is falling in popularity and Dan, the organizer, orders him to get the wrong answer to the final question. Now the champion is Charles Van Doren, a young university professor, typical "wasp", who soon becomes the new TV idol. But Dan doesn't accept the defeat and decides to legally appeal. The appeal is covered up, but the case draws the attention of a young prosecutor, Richard Goodwin.
notes: In the film there are no heroes (except the father of Van Doren, a very pure professor, a great Paul Scofield), but only cathode freebooters and those who let themselves be enchanted by television. Beautiful and compact script, confident direction, a perfect cast, dominated by Turturro, neurotic poor fellow and designated loser.

title: Paths of Glory
actors: George Macready, Timothy Carey, Kirk Douglas, Ralph Meeker, Adolphe Menjou
description: During the First World War, out of a stupid stubbornness, a French general orders an attack on a practically impregnable German position. Colonel Dax, a courageous and honest officer, understands the folly of the order and tries to avoid the carnage, but, faced with the obtuseness of his superiors, he is forced to carry out commands. The assault, of course, fails, but that's not all: the pompous general has three soldiers shot for cowardice.
notes: Wonderful film about the madness of military power. The logic of class, the horror of the offended body, the geometry and irony. One of Kubrick's masterpieces and one of the best performances of Douglas, who also produced the film.

title: The Field
actors: Richard Harris, John Hurt, Tom Berenger, Sean Bean, Brenda Fricker
description: An elderly Irish farmer has worked a patch of land all his life. That land, however, is not his and now, put up for auction, it was bought by an American. Having lost "his" land, Bull, the farmer, goes mad and, in a dramatic crescendo, destroys his life and his family. After "My Left Foot", Jim Sheridan returns to Ireland to tell another extreme story of loneliness chiaroscuro by madness, again from a text by John B. Keane. After a few years Richard Harris sees himself as the protagonist, but the film is rather heavy.

title: Tre colonne in cronaca
actors: Gian Maria Volonté, Massimo Dapporto, Joss Ackland, Sergio Castellitto, Senta Berger
description: A Roman newspaper, directed by Landolfi (Volonté) clashes with the aims of the Honorable Spano and a Lombard financier, a certain Leporino (Ackland). The idea is to give the rise to the everyday, but the attempt does not fail to leave victims on the field. Immediately a stockbroker dies and soon after the Arab girl who killed him. Meanwhile, Commissioner Morisi (Dapporto) investigates.
notes: The book was written by Augias and Daniela Pasti, both journalists of the Republic. Now do you understand who Scalfari is and who Berlusconi? The Vanzinas don't shine for their finesse, but Volonté's Scalfari is perfect ..

title: Yuppies. I giovani di successo
actors: Massimo Boldi, Ezio Greggio, Christian De Sica, Jerry Calà, Corinne Cléry, Valeria D'Obici
description: Lorenzo (Boldi) is a notary, has a jealous wife and two intrusive in-laws. Willy (Crude) sells luxury cars. Sandro (De Sica) is a dentist and Giacomo (Calà) is a creative in an advertising agency and in exchange for an important job he would also be willing to sell his girlfriend. All four with the same desire for success, luxury and beautiful women.
notes: It was the time when the Vanzina brothers were directing three or four blockbuster films a year. It occurred to the couple to retrace the footsteps of their fathers trying to copy the Italian comedy, but in vain.

title: Twenty Thousand Years in Sing Sing
actors: Spencer Tracy, Bette Davis, Arthur Byron, Lyle Talbot, Louis Calhern
description: A gangster (Tracy), paroled thanks to a human prison warden, accuses himself of a murder, actually committed by his mistress, (Davis) and ends up in the electric chair.
notes: A great love film from both sides of the prison parlor, the film holds up above all thanks to the realistic direction of Curtiz and the two protagonists.

title: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
actors: Robert De Niro, Kenneth Branagh, Helena Bonham Carter
description: Orphaned of a mother, son of a wealthy doctor from Geneva and passionate about scientific research, Victor Frankenstein studies medicine and deals with the mysteries of human life. He then sets up a sophisticated laboratory and develops a living creature by assembling parts of corpses. Branagh did not focus on horror, but on melodrama where the passion for women mixes with that, even more all-encompassing, for knowledge, the power of science, the exaltation of creation.

title: The Playboys
actors: Albert Finney, Robin Wright, Aidan Quinn, Milo O'Shea
description: Tara is a young Irish girl who is shown to be ridiculed in her village because, pregnant, she refuses to reveal who the father is and intends to be free with her baby. Things get worse when she starts a flirt with Tom, an actor from a wandering company, the Playboys. The fact triggers the jealousy of the local police sergeant with dramatic consequences, but eventually Tara will leave with Tom and the baby. Rural melodrama with an almost happy ending. Beautiful landscapes (and of course ...). The young Robin Wright is good and the no longer young Albert Finney is sometimes a bit too showman. Overall, a film that is pleasant to watch, but nothing more.

title: Le colonel Chabert
actors: Gérard Depardieu, Fabrice Luchini, Fanny Ardant
description: A man shows up at the office of the solicitor Derville: he says his name is Chabert, former commander of a garrison of cuirassiers and given up for dead at the Battle of Eylau ten years earlier. This may seem unlikely, but the lawyer agrees to represent him. But the one who ten years earlier was Madame Chabert, believing herself a widow, has rejoined the Count Ferraud, who aspires to the title of peer of France. For the latter, Chabert's reappearance is convenient, as the current marriage is a hindrance to his ambitions. It is with his wife herself, apparently greedy and shrewd, but ultimately vulnerable, that Chabert has to deal with. Second film version of a story by Balzac (the first was in 1943). Angelo's direction is correct: leave it to Depardieu and Luchini, who overshadow all the others, Ardant included.

title: Black Demons
actors: Keit van Hoven, Joe Balog
description: In Rio to study local culture, three boys attend a black magic ceremony. Then one of the three has the unfortunate idea of ??trying it on his own, summoning the vengeful spirits of six slaves killed by their masters.

title: The Shawshank Redemption
actors: Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, James Whitmore, Bob Gunton, William Sadler, Clancy Brown, Gil Bellows, Mark Rolston, James Whitemore, Jeffrey DeMunn, Larry Brandenburg, Neil Giuntoli, Brian Libby
description: We are in 1946. Tried for the murder of his wife and his lover, Andy, a banker from New England, is sentenced to a double life sentence and imprisoned in Shawshank Penitentiary. At first he was a victim of the violence of the prisoners, but then he became the financial adviser to the guards. He discovers that the director falsifies the books by making the accounts payable to a fictitious Randall Stevens. Escaped from prison through a tunnel built over the years, Andy assumes the identity of Randall Stevens, denounces the director and goes to Mexico. Between the bars there is the usual sample of humanity: sodomites out of necessity, guardians more delinquent than inmates, a rapacious director and for librarian an old lifer, James Whitmore, who embodies the greatness of American cinema of the past.
notes: It's a good prison movie, based on one of Stephen King's best novels. Robbins always improves, Freeman is sober and concrete enough and even the happy ending does not disturb.

title: Mask of Death
actors: Lorenzo Lamas, Rae Dawn Chong, Billy Dee Williams
description: A Hong Kong mobster, Lyle Mason, is killed in a ferocious shooting, during which policeman Daniel McKenna is also injured and scarred, whose wife is killed. At the proposal of the FBI, McKenna will have to become Mason, thanks to a plastic surgery operation, in order to be able to get back in touch with Frank Dalilo, companion of misdeeds of the eliminated criminal. Tangled history but mechanically arranged according to the frequent outlets of violence destined to hook the viewer. Lorenzo Lamas is now a familiar face for fans of the genre: he keeps what little he promises.

title: Poliziotti
actors: Claudio Amendola, Kim Rossi Stuart, Michele Placido, Nadia Farès, Luigi Diberti
description: Lorenzo, a policeman frowned upon by his superiors, leaves an inmate, Sante, who has attempted suicide. Andrea joins him, a meek and sensitive boy with whom Lorenzo befriends. The young agent agrees to accompany the inmate to a nearby nightclub where Sante is expected to meet the woman he loves. But Sante runs away and Andrea, shocked, shoots himself. Lorenzo wants to avenge him.
notes: The cliché rages: there are the redeeming whore, the hardened criminal, the candid policeman and the one who knows life, the sordid trafficker. Placido makes a fierce face, widening his eyes and picking up the white hair in the pigtail. Rossi Stuart takes the girls to buy tickets.

title: Nell
actors: Jodie Foster, Liam Neeson, Natasha Richardson, Richard Libertini
description: Nellie is a girl who has grown up completely isolated from the rest of the world. The local doctor, Jerome Lovell, discovers her. Initially reluctant, Lovell gradually develops a strange sense of responsibility towards the girl and, seeking advice, contacts a city psychologist, the energetic Paula Olson. However, the doctor soon regrets this initiative, after Olson asks for Nell to be admitted to a psychiatric institution. Jodie Foster is good at speaking in her sketchy and musical language, but in dubbing she has lost a lot and the result is disappointing. Liam Neeson, in the role of the doctor, has the right air of a savior, a little naive. But woe to expect a touch of novelty, malice or nonconformity.

title: HMS Defiant
actors: Alec Guinness, Dirk Bogarde, Anthony Quayle
description: The crew of an English warship mutinied under the harassment of an officer. But Napoleon is looming and for the homeland the rebels cover themselves with heroism. Two good stars, accurate staging, but overall the product suffers a bit of rhetoric.

title: Three Godfathers
actors: John Wayne, Pedro Armendariz, Harry Carey jr., Ward Bond
description: On the run across the desert after a hit, some outlaws come across a woman in labor who, dying, entrusts them with the newborn. The three, who became godparents, promised the woman that they would take care of the baby. In fact, they embark on a tiring and endless journey across the desert to bring the little one to the city. Two of them will die during the journey but the third will succeed.
notes: It is one of the most unusual films of the great director. It is a sort of hymn to religiosity that makes the story a parable of the nativity of Christ (the three bandits are the Magi) and of the journey an itinerary towards redemption. The film is dedicated to Harry Carey. Epic, colorful and fantastic.

title: Kiss Me Kate
actors: Kathryn Grayson, Howard Keel, Ann Miller
description: Fred Graham still loves his wife Lilli even though the two are now separated due, too, to his numerous escapades. Fred is a director on Broadway and Lilli is an actress. To stage a musical show based on the "Taming of the Shrew" Shakespeare, Fred chooses his ex-wife as the protagonist. During the performance, not everything goes smoothly, naturally due to the old rusts between Fred and Lilli, to the point that the show is likely to skip causing trouble for the rest of the company. As in the case described by Shakespeare, however ...
notes: Beautiful film version of a theatrical success.

title: Triumph of the Man Called Horse
actors: Richard Harris, Michael Beck, Ana De Sade
description: Lived among the Sioux, an Englishman became their leader. Some whites kill him, his adopted son avenges him. Third film in the series started with "A Man Called Horse". This time Richard Harris appears only fleetingly, however, the good qualities of the previous films are completely absent.

title: Beyond the Walls
actors: Arnon Zadok, Muhamad Bakri, Hillel Ne'eman
description: In an Israeli prison, Palestinian Issam and Israeli Uri fight together against the abuses of the prison regime and a corrupt guard. Between rawness and emotion, a fair Israeli production, significant above all from a civil and political point of view.

title: The Paper
actors: Michael Keaton, Robert Duvall, Glenn Close, Marisa Tomei
description: Henry Hackett, editor-in-chief of the "New York Sun" lives an intense twenty-four hour between impending fatherhood, the offer of a better seat in a competing newspaper and a "case" of double murder that could hide sensational backstories. In the short space of time in which the story is contained, a hundred things happen, complications add up, but in the end everything turns out for the best.
notes: If this were the true rhythm of a journalist's life, the category would be marred by chain suicides caused by stress. The film, therefore, "exaggerates", but does so with great acumen, with a captivating development in which everyone collaborates effectively.

title: L'estate di Bobby Charlton
actors: Giulio Scarpati, Agnese Nano, Carlotta Natoli, Enrico Guglielmi, Francesco Saverio Guglielmi
description: A young elementary teacher who is preparing the exam for the state competition "kidnaps" his two children, taking them from a villa in the Po valley where the children have lived with their mother since the couple separated. Unable to be without them, he loads the two little ones on a Beetle and heads to his grandmother's house in Salento. Much (too much) of young Italian cinema is characterized by an often unbearable "cuteness". This is not the case with Guglielmi's film, intense and tormented. As for the title, for those who find it incomprehensible, contact the so-called "experts" of football.

title: Peggio di così si muore
actors: Carla Signoris, Maurizio Crozza, Mauro Pirovano, Ugo Dighero, Rossy De Palma
description: Anna and Carlo, fresh off their honeymoon, take a suitcase that isn't theirs by mistake at the airport. At home, opening it, they discover that it contains a lot of money and - after some hesitation - they decide to keep it and buy a new apartment. But Carmine the Thin and Jack the Short, the two "robbed" gangsters, are not idle and for the two newlyweds the matter becomes excessively complicated ...
notes: The Broncoviz group makes the leap from the small to the big screen with a film that starts well, holds up for quite a while on an appreciable level but then "wraps" itself in a short-breathed second half. Weaknesses of the script, but the direction is discreet.

title: True Lies
actors: Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jamie Lee Curtis, Tom Arnold, Bill Paxton, Art Malik, Eliza Dushku
description: His wife thinks him a computer salesman, but Harry is a 007 used to risky missions. When the lady seems to yield to the court of a man who passes himself off as a secret agent, Harry takes little time to scare his rival. Then, however, the couple are kidnapped by Arab terrorists and Harry has to reveal himself for what he is and his wife is forced to "play along". This remake of a French film (Claude Zidi's "The Total") is a blast that brilliantly mixes action and family problems. And it works both on the side of the espionage story and as a comedy.

title: Il minestrone
actors: Roberto Benigni, Franco Citti, Ninetto Davoli, Giorgio Gaber
description: At the beginning there are two "starving" who rummage through the garbage to get something to eat. Then, through multiple hardships, the group thickens, the attempts to eat as well, but the results are always marked by failure and frustration. You will end up, following a kind of holy man, among snowy peaks, listening to band music, but with still unsatisfied hunger. A "parable" about the hunger of the poor. Weird, poetic, unclassifiable, with a crazy cast, like all Citti films. There is also a three-part television version.

title: Genesi - La Creazione e il Diluvio
actors: Omero Antonutti, Attori non professionisti
description: A nomadic shepherd tells his offspring gathered under a tent about the birth of the world: the creation of Adam and Eve, the sin, the expulsion from the earthly Paradise, the fratricide of Cain, the corruption and wickedness of man, the repentance of God for the distorted evolution of humanity, the choice of Noah, the ark, the flood, the new progeny, the covenant between God and human beings.
notes: Entrusted to the "poetry" of a Ermanno Olmi, who seems unconvinced, these nine biblical chapters are narrated with an illustration of little narrative force, flat and boring. No flickers, or doubts, or pain and an almost non-existent passion.

title: Uomini sull'orlo di una crisi di nervi
actors: Pino Ammendola, Vincenzo Crocitti, Gianni Garofalo, Claudia Koll
description: Vincenzo, Gianni, Nicola and Pino are four friends who have been meeting every Monday to play poker for years. But this time Nicola is in crisis with his wife. The evening is ruined, but Pino has an idea. Why not invite a "ring"?
notes: The film is verbose like the title, unrealistic like the director, dull like the female interpreter, Claudia Koll.

title: Drop Zone
actors: Wesley Snipes, Gary Busey, Yancy Butler, Michael Jeter
description: Pete Nessip and his brother Terry are two police officers charged with escorting Earl Leedy, convicted of computer hacking, to a federal prison aboard a Boeing 747. In the middle of the flight, however, an apparent terrorist attack causes an explosion on board, the death of Pete's brother and the disappearance of Leedy. Consequently, Pete Nessip is suspended and is convinced that the attack was actually an escape in which the protagonists escaped by parachuting. High altitude thriller, "Speed" style engulfed rhythm, with technological complications and not always probable resolutions. But what matters is that there is not a moment's respite.

title: Camerieri
actors: Paolo Villaggio, Diego Abatantuono, Marco Messeri, Ciccio Ingrassia, Antonello Fassari, Carlo Croccolo
description: It seems a Sunday like any other in the kitchen of the "Eden" restaurant. The characters: Loris Bianchi, old vain maitre, Mario Tangaro, former bullock and failed footballer; the waiter Agostino with his canaries; Germano, an ignorant chef from the Marche region. The restaurant is for sale and the old owner has had to give the rotunda overlooking the sea to a furniture maker, the same one who is celebrating his parents' golden anniversary in that restaurant today. A banquet that should therefore be the last for the four. But the furniture maker leaves one hope open: he will agree to keep the restaurant staff on condition that the banquet is impeccable. Tangaro, Bianchi, Germano and Agostino will suddenly have to abandon fights and spite. Will they make it? The heavy charm of the petty bourgeoisie is the raw material of this bad and indigestible Italian comedy. Pompucci confirms a certain taste for the composition of the shots and for a syntax that is never flat. The style, however, is detached from the characters and the story.

title: It Could Happen to You
actors: Nicolas Cage, Rosie Perez, Bridget Fonda, Isaac Hayes
description: Charlie Lang wants a few simple things out of life: to be a good cop and start a family. Muriel Lang, on the other hand, has very different aspirations. Muriel is a hairdresser, cheap woman, full of ambitions and demands: she wants to leave the Queens neighborhood and land in Manhattan; basically, he wants to leave Charlie behind. Then there is Yvonne Biasi, a soft-hearted waitress who runs a small club that her husband has reduced to the brink of bankruptcy.
notes: Bergman knows Frank Capra well, but ignores Georges Feydeau: so he focuses on the pathetic, not the bright-spicy. And the whole suffers.

title: Public Access
actors: Ron Marquette, Dina Brooks, Burt Williams, Larry Maxwell
description: A stranger arrives in Brewster. He's charming, friendly, his name is Whiley Pritcher (Ron Marquette), and the first thing he does is take a spot on a local TV network with a show called "What's Wrong With Brewster?". Gossip comes out, vipers' nests, political scandals, small grudges. But the real mystery is another: who is Whiley Pritcher and why did he stop at Brewster? Bryan Singer's first feature film, shot in eighteen days and for a quarter of a million dollars. A moderate success, an award at the Sundance Film Festival: enough to allow Singer to put his hand to the second work ("The usual suspects") and break through.

title: Favola
actors: Ambra Angiolini, Ryan Krause, Agostina Belli, Enzo Cannavale
description: Anita (Ambra) is an outgoing Roman girl, with a father who ran away from home years ago and a mother always at work. Anita works in a hi-fi shop and doesn't know she's about to meet the man of destiny. The prince of Homburg (Krause) is in Rome, a guest of his ambassador, but he gets bored so he starts to visit the city alone, then stops in front of the Hi-Fi shop. It was destiny. It was destiny that, after the television and musical successes, Ambra Angiolini ended up arriving also in the cinema. For his debut a standard story is chosen, infinitely tellable and told over and over again. A painless story.

title: La voce del silenzio
actors: Aldo Fabrizi, Jean Marais, Paolo Panelli
description: A group of men meet, as every year, in a convent for a course of spiritual exercises. However, a thief who tries to hide himself in this way from police searches has also sneaked in among them. The defendants all have spiritual problems to solve and each will come to terms with their conscience and their past. Subject by Zavattini, directed by a former master like Pabst. but the result is a squeeze of heavy Catholic ideology.

title: Persona
actors: Bibi Andersson, Liv Ullmann, Gunnar Björnstrand, Margaretha Krook, Jörgen Lindström
description: Elisabeth Vogel, a well-known actress, one day begins to refuse to speak, closing herself in an obstinate silence. She is joined by a nurse who begins to tell her about her private life. The woman's confessions become more and more intimate. But the actress in a letter reveals the secrets of the nurse. One of the many, beautiful portraits on the verge of a nervous breakdown of two women and their neuroses. Almost on the edge of fashion, but with an uncommon intensity. Famous is the scene of the profiles of the two women who compose a single face, the beginning with the film that physically catches fire, the final word of the protagonist.

title: Song of the South
actors: James Baskett, Bobby Driscoll, Luana Patten, Hattie McDaniel
description: Little Johnny meets Uncle Tom, an old black man who knows the art of storytelling. The two become friends and, to every difficulty that Johnny encounters in life, Uncle Tom responds with a story that exemplifies his moral. Produced by Walt Disney, the film is interspersed with animation clips (directed by Wilfred Jacjson) with Brother Bunny, Compare Bear and Comare Volpe, which remain the best. Oscar for best song.

title: Demetrius and the Gladiators
actors: Victor Mature, Susan Hayward, Debra Paget, Anne Bancroft
description: Caligula wants to take possession of the sacred tunic of the Messiah in his time collected by Demetrius. Arrested, Demetrius is sent to the school of gladiators and threatened by the perfidious Messalina, but he loves Lucia. Messalina, however, has her "rival" killed. Demetrius, upset, abandons Christianity and becomes the woman's lover, but a portentous event brings Lucia back to life. During a revolt, Caligula is killed and Claudius, elected emperor, issues an indult for Christians.
notes: Spectacular film and very rich in means, it is a weak continuation of the previous "La tunica".

title: Widow's Peak
actors: Joan Plowright, Mia Farrow, Natasha Richardson, Jim Broadbent
description: Ireland 1920. On the hill overlooking the village of Kilshannon is Widow's Peak, the neighborhood of a small group of gossiping widows. Older among them is the formidable Mrs. Doyle Counihan, who has buried two husbands and knows everything and everyone. His son Godfrey is the only living man on Widow's Peak. In the group stands Miss O'Hare, never married, but also marked by a painful past. When a young war widow, Edwina, arrives, the clash is inevitable The Clash of Ladies is also the best thing about the film, served by Hugh Leonard's script interwoven with black humor and the flawless interpretation of the three protagonists. Too bad that the final report (however unexpected) does not live up to expectations.

title: Time cop
actors: Jean-Claude Van Damme, Ron Silver, Mia Sara
description: It's the year 2004. Time travel has become a reality and with it a new sort of criminal has emerged. Suddenly it is possible to alter historical events, control the financial markets or even bring entire nations to ruin. So the Time Control Commission issues one simple law: no one goes back. But today someone has broken the law and Max Walker, known as Timecop, embarks on a tough manhunt, tempted to prevent his own personal tragedy: the murder of his wife. The time travel topoi are all there; but more than originality in temporal paradoxes, the action firmly managed by a professional like Hyams counts.

title: Terminal Velocity
actors: Charlie Sheen, Nastassja Kinski, James Gandolfini, Melvin Van Peebles
description: Ditch Brodie is light-hearted and very happy with his job of teaching people to parachute. The skydiving instructor finds himself catapulted into the world of international espionage after the parachute of a beautiful and mysterious student named Chris refuses to open during the free fall. Uninteresting adventure, with a discounted ending from the start and lots of special effects for the plane launch scenes. Charlie Sheen tries in every way to be a nice American, Nastassja Kinski has to be a European doll.

title: Maccheroni
actors: Marcello Mastroianni, Jack Lemmon, Isa Danieli, Daria Nicolodi, Maria Luisa Santella
description: Robert Traven, a sixty-year-old American manager, returns to Naples where he had fought in '45 and where he had lived a brief relationship with this Maria. He is contacted by her brother, Antonio, who for years has been writing adventurous letters to his sister signed Robert. While the American rediscovers himself, their friendship grows, even against the Camorra and (perhaps) he will be able to overcome even the death of Antonio himself. Two great actors like Lemmon and Mastroianni partly make us forget the thinness of the assumption. But the film, crammed with clichés and without structure, is not one of Scola's happiest.

title: La teta y la luna
actors: Mathilda May, Gérard Darmon, Miguel Poveda, Biel Duran
description: Tete is an imaginative little boy who feels overshadowed by the birth of his little brother. Estrellita and Maurice "the petomaniac" arrive with their show in the city. While Estrellita is dressing for the scene, Tete, hidden, observes her fascinated breasts. And he falls in love with it. But he runs up against a more dangerous suitor: Miquel, an electrician who works at the campsite where Estrellita lives.
notes: A story of erotic-surreal poetry that reflects well the somewhat delusional and very earthy humor of Bigas Luna. More tied to the myths and rituals of traditional Spain than Almodòvar (which he somehow anticipated), Bigas Luna has a beautiful critical and provocative ingenuity, loves sex, nature, bodily expressions. But his best films remain the first, where he really managed to dig into the perversions.

title: Angel
actors: Marlene Dietrich, Herbert Marshall, Melvyn Douglas, Edward Everett Horton
description: Maria Barker, wife of the English diplomat Sir Frederick, feels neglected, and during a trip to Paris accepts the passionate court of a young and wealthy American. The sentimental plot becomes complicated; however, before things take a definitive turn, Maria re-enters the marital ranks and reconciles with her spouse, whom she respects but does not love.
notes: A more nuanced and mysterious Lubitsch than usual, despite the usual perfection of the dialogues (co-script Samson Raphaelson and Melchior Lengyel) and of the staging. Marlene, ethereal and elusive, leaks questions about a probable murky past. Cinema of the past.
