description: It is sunset on the last day of the year and Poldo is preparing to spend the evening in a quiet intimacy. Suddenly his friend Rosario falls into his house, in desperation because his girlfriend has left him. Pity, even if reluctantly, Poldo resigns himself first to take his friend with him to a party, then to accompany him out of town to his parents. A friend's favor kicks off a series of daring adventures, at the end of which Poldo and Rosario will be able to promise themselves a less eventful end of the year for the future.
notes: Trained at the school of Massimo Troisi, Angelo Orlando made his directorial debut with a film full of ideas and with good lines, but here and there a bit limping. Ricky Memphis, who alternates dramatic characters with comic parts, proves once more that he is one of the best actors of the new generation.

title: While You Were Sleeping
actors: Sandra Bullock, Bill Pullman, Peter Gallagher, Peter Boyle
description: Lucy works as a ticket collector on the Chicago subway. In her fantasy, the man for her is an unknown young man who passes in front of her every day but not worthy of a glance. One day, however, the man is attacked by some thugs, falls on the tracks unconscious and is rescued by Lucy, who in the hospital is mistaken by family for his girlfriend. An easy comedy, with many situations already seen but also various funny scenes. In America it was a great success in 1995: it cost 15 million dollars, it grossed five times as much. Thanks, perhaps, to Sandra Bullock's kind and funny charm.

title: Rudy
actors: Sean Astin, Ned Beatty, Lili Taylor, Charles S. Dutton, Mary-Ann Thebus, Robert Prosky
description: In Joliet, Illinois, a country like many others lives Rudy, lacking in school and sports. In fact, he gives up university and gets a job. But when his best friend dies, Rudy turns his life around. He manages, with titanic efforts, to be accepted at the university and to enter, albeit as a reserve, in the football team. And the last minute of the last game arrives ... A caption specifies that the story told by the film really happened. All right, we take note. This, however, does not contribute at all to revive the fate of a film marked by a congenital, irremediable inadequacy.

title: Peccato veniale
actors: Laura Antonelli, Alessandro Momo, Orazio Orlando, Lilla Brignone
description: Sixteen years old, Sandro is at the seaside with his father almost as hungry for sex as he and his mother distracted. The group is joined by the boy's sister-in-law (Antonelli), who will initiate him into the joys of sex. A free-range erotic comedy, as was used then, which imitates "Malizia". The music by Fred Bongusto, as always professional photography by Tonino Delli Colli, is adequate.

title: Nine to Five
actors: Jane Fonda, Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton, Sterling Hayden, Jean March, Rita Moreno
description: Judy, who recently divorced her husband, manages to get a job with a large company. The woman is assigned to the department of the despotic office manager Franklin Hart jr. The newcomer is taken under the tutelage of the expert Violet and soon the two become friends. The group is joined by Doralee, Franklin's private secretary, who arouses the envy of her colleagues. In reality Franklin is a true despot and the three women fantasize about killing him to take control of the office.
notes: Brilliant comedy, produced and performed by Jane Fonda at the height of her feminist commitment.

title: Fragment of Fear
actors: David Hemmings, Gayle Hannicutt, Roland Culver
description: A young English writer, former drug addict, investigates the murder of his aunt. His discoveries are dangerous and surprising, so much so that they risk his life and mental health. It looks like a thriller, but it develops in another direction, pushing the spectators, together with the protagonist, not towards the solution, but towards total bewilderment. After all, Hemmings had already been the protagonist of "Blow Up" ...

title: Mi familia
actors: Edward James Olmos, Esai Morales, Costance Marie
description: In a small house on the East Side of Los Angeles an elderly couple of "chicanos" take stock of their existence from the 1920s to today, lovingly scrolling through the pages of the home album. The two are now old and tired, but the spirit of the children, grandchildren and genres still hovers in the rooms painted with the bright and ancient colors of their homeland. Everyone's memory unfolds and takes shape through the moving evocation of the son who became a writer. A soap opera in which stereotypes of melò and tears predominate. The director, fascinated by familiar scenarios and perhaps also with a desire to emulate "The house of the spirits", actually carries out his cinematic theme with a somewhat "bureaucrat of sentiment" style.

title: To Die For
actors: Nicole Kidman, Matt Dillon, Joaquin Phoenix, Illeana Douglas, Casey Affleck, Alison Folland, Wayne Knight, Maria Tucci
description: In America you are not someone if you do not appear on TV: this is what Suzanne Stone, a provincial girl who cultivates the one, supreme ambition of becoming a TV personality, says. Disillusioned with her relationship with her husband, Suzanne dedicates herself to pursuing her dream of notoriety with obsessive meticulousness and total absence of scruples, overwhelming any element that can be inserted between her and the coveted small screen. An acid and biting story about the contradictions of the respectability of the American province, all pastel colors and black souls, graceful coaxing and ruthless careerism; and on the subculture of audiovisual presentialism, with its sweetened and deformed vision of reality. Lively as a sitcom and treacherous as a black comedy, it's a decidedly fun and tasty, yet acrid film.

title: Blue Chips
actors: J.T. Walsh, Nick Nolte, Mary McDonnell, Ed O'Neill
description: Pete Bell is the coach of the Western University basketball team, which is not going through a bright moment. Find valid elements, but to sign them violates the laws of sports ethics. He accepts the compromise, but later "repents".
notes: William Friedkin, who recently declared that television will save cinema from the brink of death, is very effective in visually telling the game phases of basketball (in the film there are champions of the caliber of Larry Bird and Shaquille O'Neal); a little less in giving "moral" substance to the story. The times of the "Exorcist" are unfortunately far away.

title: The Bridges of Madison County
actors: Meryl Streep, Clint Eastwood, Annie Corley, Victor Slezak
description: In the fall of 1956 Robert Kinkaid, a professional photographer, is in Madison County, Iowa, to shoot a report on the famous covered bridges. There he meets Francesca Johnson, married and with two children, but alone at home for four days: this is the brief but intense period of time in which their passion explodes and consumes itself. Four days that must last a lifetime and must redeem it for the whole, recovering an ability to love, to choose, to feel, to help each other, which especially from Francesca's part seemed now abandoned.
notes: Romantic, crepuscular, heartbroken (the silent farewell in the rain is unforgettable, predictable but not trivial, tearful but not dull), Eastwood's work has the solemn and essential simplicity of classic cinema. Streep is stupendous, playing the Italoamicana reproducing some of the charms of the American Magnani of "La rosa tatuata" or "Snake skin". Screenplay by Richard LaGravanese from a novel by Robert James Waller.

title: Judge Dredd
actors: Sylvester Stallone, Armand Assante, Diane Lane
description: In the third millennium, what remains of humanity lives barricaded in megalopolises dominated by violence. To maintain order, a caste of judges-executioners with the power of immediate execution, equipped with personalized weapons on their vocal waves. At Megacity Uno, born out of the rubble of New York, this system is complicated by corruption. But there is a judge who is capable of fighting for the Law and Justice and determined to do so: Joseph Dredd.
notes: As usual, without a glimmer of expressiveness, Stallone here embodies a hyper-technological Rambo dressed in Versace, in an all-action film that wants to recall the "Blade Runner" in the settings without succeeding. Based on a hugely popular comic in England, the film does not come out of that dimension and only works in action scenes. When, on the other hand, he pretends to make the characters speak, the ridicule explodes: the question remains whether it is voluntary or not.

title: Bal na vodi
actors: Gala Midenovic, Milan Strjic, Dragan Bjelogrlic
description: Four boys and a girl, Esther (named in honor of Esther Williams) live happily in Belgrade in the 1950s. A little later we discover them all established, all abroad, some in Milan and some in London. Esther has died in the meantime.
notes: Acin is a television director and does his duty, the guys are nice, but the best thing is the photography of Tomislav Pinter (Oscar for "Amadeus").

title: First Knight
actors: Sean Connery, Richard Gere, Julia Ormond, Ben Cross
description: In the golden city of Camelot, the charm of the knight Lancelot disrupts the union of Guinevere and King Arthur. Surrounded by fame as an adventurer, Lancelot embodies independence and freedom. Its opposition to the figure of Arthur, symbol of wisdom and the common good, exerts a dangerous fascination on the future queen Guinevere.
notes: The dilemma of the betrothed, divided between two strong and attractive men and torn between passion and a sense of duty, is the fulcrum of the umpteenth cinematic transposition of the epic. But Zucker, a specialist in demented, makes a pompous and vulgar film.

title: Circle of Friends
actors: Chris O'Donnell, Minnie Driver, Geraldine O' Rawe, Saffron Burrows
description: Dublin: on the eve of the magical sixties, while the first signs of libertarianism and the profound changes of the decade to come are already in the air, two girls from a small provincial village decide to attend college. The city experience and the new school environment change their lives: between chatter and experiences, they will know friendship, first loves, sex, the hardness of conquests and the difficult transition from the carefree of youth to the responsibilities of age. adult. Based on the novel by Irish writer Maeve Binchy, the film diligently follows its story, skilfully making the beautiful rarefied atmosphere and the delicacy of the dialogues. However, here and there, it suffers from a certain mannerism that prevents it from fully exploiting the potential of the narrative.

title: Batman Forever
actors: Val Kilmer, Chris O'Donnell, Nicole Kidman, Jim Carrey, Tommy Lee Jones
description: In Gotham City, two new incarnations of Evil have decided to join forces to control the minds of citizens and destroy Batman: the first is Two-Face, a respectable former citizen with a face devastated by a terrible accident; the second is the Riddler, a frustrated employee who turned into the deadliest of criminals. Batman has his problems too, or at least his alter ego Bruce Wayne has them, haunted by painful childhood memories and plagued by unrequited love for a beautiful psychologist.
notes: Good special effects and big-name actors thrown to the wind in a production that tries to mimic Burton's pop style by focusing on bright colors, but Schumacher lacks style and the outcome is sickening.

title: Bidoni
actors: Giuseppe Cederna, Angela Finocchiaro, Gioele Dix
description: Giuseppe works in a small independent television network as an ecology expert journalist. He meets Sandra, apparently a simple secretary, but strangely linked to the undersecretary for the environment: Pasquale Giulivi, a shady politician with his hands all over the place; also on Giuseppe's television, which happens to be losing its independence. Meanwhile, even the company for which Sandra works is beginning to weigh suspicions for obscure maneuvers of recycling of toxic waste ... Corruption, billions, murders and a final surprise are the elements around which a pleasant but not extraordinary yellow comedy revolves. The somewhat predictable schematism (in addition to the unprofitable comparison with "Il portaborse") is his main limitation. Too bad, because the actors are good and demonstrate the reassuring vitality of Italian comedy.

title: In the Bleak Midwinter
actors: Michael Maloney, Richard Briers, Joan Collins, Celia Imrie, Julia Sawalha, Gerard Horan, Mark Hadfield, Nicholas Farrell
description: Shortly before Christmas, in a small town in Surrey, a shabby company of eccentric and neurotic performers prepares the staging of "Hamlet" in a church that is about to be demolished. Directed by Joe Harper, an actor frustrated by the abandonment of the girl and the long unemployment.
notes: A comedy full of life and vivacity, with magnificent actors and impeccable rhythms. All wisely dosed and seasoned with a crackling script and a black and white of rare elegance.

title: The Great Caruso
actors: Mario Lanza, Ann Blyth, Dorothy Kirsten, Jarmila Novotna
description: Enrico Caruso was born in Naples in 1873. Marked for his voice from a young age, he obtained popular successes, but abandoned singing hoping to ingratiate himself with the father of a girl he fell in love with. A tenor, Alfredo Brazzi, convinces him to study and Caruso, after a tour in Europe, accepts a writing for America. They will be triumphs until premature death, not yet fifty. Structured according to an extremely linear and "popular" scheme, the film is almost a pretext to align a series of famous operatic pieces, to the greater glory of Mario Lanza who plays them. Spectacularly and musically not flawless.

title: Il mattatore
actors: Vittorio Gassman, Dorian Gray, Anna Maria Ferrero, Peppino De Filippo
description: Two cronies agree to cheat a certain Gerardo, but when the "bin" seems to have been successful, Gerardo himself unmasks the fraud. And here is the story of his professional curriculum. He can be called the king of scams: his whole life has been nothing more than a series of chameleonic "blows" scored with the most unthinkable disguises and the most ingenious mechanisms. Gassman, Gassman and again Gassman. In all sorts of ways, in full swing, the star, in fact, from one end to the other of the film designed to allow him to exhibit his histrionics.

title: Lullaby of Broadway
actors: Doris Day, Billy De Wolfe, Gene Nelson, Gladys George
description: From England, where she plays small roles in musicals, Melinda goes to New York to join her mother, who always writes to her about her stage hits. The reality is quite different: the woman is now reduced to performing in clubs of the lowest order.
notes: Solid musical, spectacular, but a little rough.

title: A Child Is Missing
actors: Henry Winkler, Roma Sidney, Dale Midkiff
description: Samantha and her eight-year-old son Buddy live in Washington County. One day a stranger kidnaps Buddy and hides him in a snow-covered metal conduit in the middle of the mountains. Samantha alerts the police and prepares the ransom money. Meanwhile, Buddy is discovered and saved by a hermit who lives in the mountains. He has nothing to do but will be mistaken for the kidnapper ...
notes: John Power is an Australian who emigrated to America with a solid television background ("Alice From Nowhere"). Experience that is used here to remove Henry Winkler, the legendary Fonzie of "Happy Days" from the hermitage.

title: The Man Between
actors: James Mason, Hildegarde Neff, Claire Bloom, Geoffrey Toone, Aribert Wäscher
description: An English girl, Susan Morrison, decides to go on vacation to Berlin, invited by her brother Billy, who, by profession, is a military doctor. Billy married a German, Bettina, with whom Susan goes to visit the eastern sector of the city occupied by the Russians. Here he meets Ivo Kern, who lives on the black market. Susan allows herself, little by little, softened by a fall in love.
notes: With Berlin instead of Vienna, a sort of "Third Man" in a smaller format, but with a great cast.

title: La Haine
actors: Vincent Cassel, Hubert Koundé, Said Taghmaoui, Abdel Ahmed Ghili
description: In a suburb of a French city like many others, made up of misery, more or less assorted ethnic groups and various types of crime, the wind of revolt is blowing. The occasion that makes her explode is the brutal interrogation to which the police subject a sixteen year old boy. In the struggle, the difficulties and the different personalities of all the young people who have been involved emerge. It won't be good for everyone. To support the message there is a compelling story, with a strong impact, in which the relationships between the characters are rendered effectively, the developments are never trivial and the rhythm knows no falls.

title: L'uomo delle stelle
actors: Sergio Castellitto, Tiziana Lodato, Tony Sperandeo, Jane Alexander (II), Franco Scaldati, Clelia Rondinella, Tano Cimarosa, Leo Gullotta, Antonella Attili, Costantino Carrozza, Leopoldo Trieste
description: Joe Morelli is an enterprising character, but not very clear: he pretends to be the discoverer of new talent for cinema. Around the miserable villages of post-war Sicily, he harangues the inhabitants at the megaphone, promising a brilliant career at Cinecittà to those who pass an accurate audition. Joe is the man who can perform the miracle of transforming a poor, marginalized and miserable existence into a rich and admired life. So everyone falls for it: immature girls, frustrated women, shepherds, carabinieri, fishermen. "The man of the stars" is a story of fascination, of illusions, of lies. A celluloid scam that allows, by going beyond its own intentions, to bring to the surface thoughts never expressed, hopes, nuanced sensations and nostalgia. The first part is more interesting and original, then the melò becomes heavy. Silver Lion in Venice, ex aequo with Monteiro's "La commedia di Dio".

title: Red Dawn
actors: C. Thomas Howell, Patrick Swayze, Ben Johnson, Harry Dean Stanton, Charlie Sheen
description: Soviet and Cuban airborne troops occupy the territory of the United States of America committing violence, deportation and other acts of ferocity. A group of 18-year-olds, boys and girls, flee to the mountains and organize guerrilla warfare. Soon the young heroes know all the cruelty of the conflict: betrayal, ambushes, death. Eventually only a few supersites will see the return of freedom.
notes: John Milius doesn't joke: when the going gets tough ... Everything is taken very seriously, and this is really the least beautiful aspect of the whole thing. Too bad, because as a director of extreme situations Milius proves himself as always up to the task.

title: Congo
actors: Dylan Walsh, Laura Linney, Ernie Hudson, Tim Curry, Grant Heslov
description: Monkey scholar Peter Elliot organizes a trip to Congo to bring his extraordinary gorilla back to the jungle, which has the peculiarity of talking to humans. The scholar joins an expedition sent by an American company in search of a diamond deposit. Amidst mysteries and lost cities, adventurers will discover that they are the endangered species in Congo ...
notes: The story is taken, a little too freely, from a good novel by Michael Crichton, a brilliant author, prolific and abundantly exploited by the cinema: those who had wondered why this work had never been used for the screen, not even now have been satisfied given the low level of the result. Great display of means but few found really up to the intentions:

title: Il romanzo di un giovane povero
actors: Alberto Sordi, Rolando Ravello, Isabella Ferrari
description: The frustration and insecurity of Vincenzo, a graduate for six years and still unemployed, now a slave to an increasingly less hidden defeatism, allow an elderly roommate to insinuate himself into his life with the proposal of a feral pact: for thirty million the young man should get rid of the old man's rich and bulky wife. When the woman is actually found dead Vincenzo is immediately suspected. From a somewhat odd idea developed without great inspiration, a livid and bitter film, which tastes of some yellow films of minor French cinema. The two protagonists are good: Sordi, in one of the few evil characters of his third age, is slimy and insinuating at the right point, and the newcomer Ravello. Isabella Ferrari was awarded at the Venice Film Festival.

title: Per qualche dollaro in meno
actors: Lando Buzzanca, Raimondo Vianello, Elio Pandolfi, Gloria Paul
description: Bank Deputy Cashier Bill discovers a $ 100 shortfall in his office accounting. What to do? He improvises as a robber: cousin Frank, in agreement with him, will capture him and collect the bounty with which to smooth out the shortfall. Mattoli's latest film, it's a blown-out parody of spaghetti westerns.

title: La corruzione
actors: Rosanna Schiaffino, Jacques Perrin, Alain Cuny, Isa Miranda
description: Stefano wants to become a priest but his father, a successful publisher, introduces him to a charming and helpful woman. The vocation is reduced, but the inner conflicts do not end so quickly.

title: Mowgli
actors: Jason Scott Lee, Lena Headey, Sam Neill, John Cleese
description: Northwest India, 1871. A caravan crossing the lush tropical forest is attacked by the ferocious tiger Shere Khan. Little Mowgli, son of the Indian guide, gets lost and is believed dead. He will grow up in the jungle with his panther friend Bagheera, the bear Baloo and a pack of wolves. In the world of animals, everything is simple and natural to deal with, even enemies. Difficulties begin when he comes back in contact with humans ...
notes: What sustains this Disney superproduction, shot on four continents, is above all the animalist element: the creatures of the jungle are magnificent, they are so tender and shine for their naturalness in the midst of a cast of slightly awkward humans (apart from the very good John Cleese in the part of Dr. Plumford). The two previous versions, the '42 one and the '67 animated one, were much more fascinating and fun. Here remain the beauty and accuracy of the scenography and a certain naive naivete that guarantees the show for families. Director Stephen Sommers, who really isn't that great, is the same director who wrote and directed "The Mummy", a huge (surprisingly) hit.

title: Seven Sinners
actors: Marlene Dietrich, John Wayne, Albert Dekker, Broderick Crawford
description: Cabaret singer Bijou (Dietrich) haunts the more or less equivocal locals of the Pacific islands. In one of these he makes a young officer (Wayne) from the US Navy fall in love with himself, but it doesn't last. A sentimental drama: when charm meets innocence, love blossoms. Exoticism and (veiled) eroticism, in a fascinating classic with a magnetic Dietrich.

title: Don't Tell Mom the Babysitter Is Dead
actors: Christina Applegate, Joanna Cassidy, John Getz, Josh Charles
description: While their mother is on vacation, five kids, ages seven to seventeen, are left at the mercy of an old and hateful babysitter. Then it happens that the woman dies and the boys decide to hide the fact to enjoy a period of unexpected freedom. Swell, the eldest, does even more. He gets hired in a fashion house and, despite all the possible inexperience, he succeeds. At first it seems like a youth farce dipped in macabre humor. Then, thanks to everyone's acting (except Joanna Cassidy) and Stephen Herek's direction, it turns out that the only humorist was the man who gave the go-ahead for the film.

title: Apollo 13
actors: Tom Hanks, Kevin Bacon, Bill Paxton, Gary Sinise, Ed Harris, Kathleen Quinlan
description: Houston, we have a problem: these laconic words, spoken from a distance of 205,000 miles, left Nasa Mission Control and the whole world in suspense. The "Apollo 13" spacecraft left on April 11, 1970 from the Cape Canaveral base, headed for the moon. An explosion occurred in the advanced mission was causing loss of oxygen, power and control. For the first time in the history of the conquest of space, the lives of three cosmonauts were in danger ...
notes: The film tells this extraordinary race against time as a celebration of human inventiveness and intelligence, with an elegant direction, careful to privilege the human factor (the astronauts, their wives, the technicians) over the spectacular. The result is a classic film, not devoured by special effects, in which the two "heroes" on the ground, Ed Harris and Gary Sinise, often steal the show from the three who are instead in space.

title: Kreola
actors: Demetra Hampton, Theo Losito, John Armstead, Cristina Garavaglia
description: Following the photographer's husband, sent for a prestigious service to Santo Domingo, a rich and spoiled woman ends up falling in love with a local fisherman. A fiery relationship follows. Sort of mallrified copy in an exotic version of the "Lady Chatterley lover", without originality and with soft eroticism. Demetra Hampton, already Valentina from Crepax on the big screen climbed to the Chronicles of Tangentopoli for her Love Story with the former Milanese councilor Walter Armanini.

title: Croce e delizia
actors: Teo Teocoli, Marina Confalone, Luciano De Crescenzo, Riccardo Pazzaglia
description: An Italian troupe is busy filming an adaptation of the "Traviata" in Paris. The seamstress Rosa, in love with the leading actor, identifies with Violetta: thanks to a bad joke and a false séance, Rosa begins to believe that she is her reincarnation. From that moment on he tries to find out everything he can about his "previous life", which slowly gets closer and closer to the real one.
notes: De Crescenzo tries to free himself from the sketch structure typical of his other cinematographic tests, while maintaining a sly preference for extravagant characters and unlikely events. All this is always observed with that good-natured wit that makes him dose metacinema, melodrama and melancholy farce with shrewdness.

title: Borets i kloun
actors: Stanislav Chekan, Aleksandr Mikhailov, Anatolj Solovev
description: It is the story of the life of the wrestler Poddubni and the clown Durov, darlings of the Russian public between 1880 and 1900, and of their friendship. The circus environment of the last century is rendered with extreme accuracy by one of the best Russian directors of his generation.

title: Un indien dans la ville
actors: Thierry Lhermitte, Arielle Dombasle, Miou-Miou, Ludwig Briand
description: Stephane, a Parisian telematic speculator, must join his wife, who abandoned him thirteen years earlier, in the Amazon rainforest to obtain a divorce signature. When he finds her, among Indians and mosquitoes, he discovers he has a son. The boy, with the whimsical name of "Cat's Piss", is eager to see the Eiffel Tower and can't be said no. But the contact between the little savage and the civilized world is certainly not easy ...
notes: Amidst misunderstandings, pigeons pierced by arrows, speculations on soybeans and found in the American comedy of yesteryear, every now and then a few smiles escape. For the rest, everything flows away like fresh water and there is no trace of the probable attempt at social criticism (trite and withdrawn) on the European lifestyle all aimed at accumulating money.

title: La cérémonie
actors: Sandrine Bonnaire, Isabelle Huppert, Jacqueline Bisset, Jean-Pierre Cassel
description: One winter morning at the Saint-Malo station, Madame Lelièvre welcomes Sophie, the new waitress. Immediately seemingly at ease in handling household chores, Sophie manages to do everything and satisfy everyone. If it weren't for his strange lack of emotion ... Jeanne, the easygoing and curious postwoman of the village, manages to make friends with the newcomer; the secrets of the two young women, different but equally unacknowledged, transform friendship into an alliance. The Lelièvre family, without knowing it and unwittingly, comes dangerously close to revealing these secrets. One of those films in which apparently nothing happens, where everyday gestures weave a web of disturbing signals and drag the story towards the inevitable final explosion. From a novel by Ruth rendell (already brought to the screen in La morte non saleggere), a paradoxical private class struggle and a duel between two superlative actresses, Huppert and Bonnaire (awarded in Venice).

title: Clockers
actors: Mekhi Phifer, Harvey Keitel, John Turturro, Delroy Lindo, Regina King, Pee Wee Love
description: In a once decent neighborhood in Brooklyn, a young drug dealer finds himself with an upset existence and counted hours: he is chased by a detective and a boss willing to protect their interests at any cost. Against this background traditional values ??and the flattery of the street collide. Meanwhile, the honest citizens of the popular buildings are fighting a perennial war against drug dealers, the "clockers", who instead in the eyes of the neighborhood kids represent the image of success and popularity.
notes: Spike Lee does not fail in his snappy, colorful, merciless style, and disseminates this heartbreaking urban drama (taken from a Richard Price best seller) with doubts, anger, helplessness.

title: Die Hard With a Vengeance
actors: Bruce Willis, Jeremy Irons, Samuel L. Jackson, Colleen Camp
description: Detective John McClane is back on duty. His enemy this time is called Simon and he is a bloodthirsty terrorist with a penchant for riddles and the gold reserve of a Wall Street bank. For the most beaten up and swollen policeman in the history of cinema it is a rather abrupt return to activity, in which he involves the quiet former shopkeeper Zeus.
notes: The sure hand of the director, already author of the first chapter of the series, "Crystal trap", maneuvers actors and means of locomotion with the same energy. Lots of action, breathtaking chases, fun and entertaining actors, and all expectations are met in full.

title: Gazon maudit
actors: Victoria Abril, Alain Chabat, Josiane Balasko, Miguel Bosé
description: Laurent and Loli are apparently a couple without problems: Laurent has a good job and many extramarital affairs that she manages to keep well hidden, Loli is a resigned housewife. When Marijo, a declared and enterprising lesbian, arrives at the house, Laurent's arrogance is contrasted by the sweetness of Loli who becomes attached to this bizarre newcomer. Great success in France, it is a fake-transgressive comedy and made with cunning. John Boorman's two daughters also appear and, in the finale, Miguel Bosé.

title: Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie
actors: David Yost, Amy Yong Johnson, Jason Frank, Karan Ashley
description: The Power Rangers jump off the tailgate of a plane, open the parachute and hit the target hard. The mutants with exceptional powers are recognizable by their colors: Rocky is red, Adam black, Tommy white, Billy blue and the charming Kimberly all pink. The television series that was an audience champion in the United States since its debut in 1993, had already been replaced in the hearts of young viewers by more recent characters, and having entrusted the action to real actors is not enough to bring the success. Children struggle to find their noisy adventures, the special effects do not have the same liveliness that they sported in cartoons.

title: Showgirls
actors: Elizabeth Berkley, Kyle MacLachlan, Gina Gershon
description: Nomi Malone has a dark past and an uncertain present in the Stardust topless bar. His wildest ambition is to become the protagonist of the musical "Goddess" at Stardust. On stage and behind the scenes, between a "lap dance" movement and a murder, Nomi will find herself. The astute pioneers of the new sexual frontier of nineties Hollywood cinema, Verhoeven and screenwriter Joe Eszterhas ("Basic Instinct"), unleash their collection of glossy eros and their synthesis of perversions; painfully trying to photocopy the energy of "Flashdance", the kitsch of the dance sequences of "Staying Alive" and even the implications of the female hostility of "Eve against Eve".

title: Denise Calls Up
actors: Tim Daly, Caroleen Feeney, Dan Gunther, Liev Schreiber
description: A morning like many others. Linda listlessly gets out of bed, turns on the computer, slips a portable phone into her pocket. Like Linda, six other New Yorkers are "voluntary prisoners" of telecommunication and their computer keyboards. They don't show up on dates or parties or funerals. They live the emotions of childbirth and fatherhood, the skirmishes of courtship, the regrets of finished stories, disappointments and griefs. The telephone is the absolute protagonist of Hal Salwen's delicious, bitter, witty directorial debut. A sort of modern fable about life and love made with phone calls and call notifications, without the need (or the possibility) of personal encounters. And at the same time a touching and hilarious reflection on the lifestyle of a certain intellectual bourgeoisie of the Big Apple.

title: Johnny Mnemonic
actors: Keanu Reeves, Dina Meyer, Dolph Lundgren
description: In the twenty-first century, information technology is the last frontier of progress and the most dangerous threat is constituted by computer pirates. The only guarantee for data security are the "computer couriers", who lend parts of their personal memory to make way for industrial secrets (grafted onto microchips). Johnny has given up his childhood memories in order to carry precious data, but the load is too much for his brain, which risks exploding. Added to this is the persecution of a rival industry that wants to get hold of its head to steal the data.
notes: Robert Longo, new director, is a famous multimedia artist; screenwriter William Gibson, father of cyberpunk, is an inventive and intelligent storyteller; Keanu Reeves is perfect in the role of Johnny; the graphics of the sets, between high tech and the Middle Ages, make its effect. Yet the film does not work as it should: few inventions, boring the plot and the pace is bland.

title: Nine Months
actors: Hugh Grant, Julianne Moore, Joan Cusack, Robin Williams
description: An unexpected pregnancy throws Rebecca and Samuel (Grant )'s relationship into crisis. The latter is a child psychotherapist, yet he is the most frightened. A reluctance to paternity accentuated by repeated encounters with the numerous and chaotic kinship of his best friend - a hardened single - and by the presence of a Russian gynecologist (Williams).
notes: Apart from the gimmick of the lexical misunderstandings that are of the third order, the weakest point of this thin film, packaged (maluccio) with the optional moral message, is the mediocre interpretation of Hugh Grant. As for the rest, it is a patched-up collection of grimaces, winks, winks, dumbfounds. The whole is banal, superfluous and even annoying.

title: La seconda volta
actors: Nanni Moretti, Valeria Bruni Tedeschi, Valeria Milillo, Roberto De Francesco, Marina Confalone, Francesca Antonelli
description: Professor Alberto Sajevo has been living for twelve years with a bullet in the head. Lisa, the former terrorist who shot him, serves his sentence in semi-release. A chance encounter causes their destinies to cross again. She doesn't recognize him, he does and approaches her with a fake name. But elapsed time does not change identities, and neither explains the past nor can it make up for it. Calopreste's film does not want to talk about terrorism, but about the impossibility of fully understanding a "black hole" in our history: not a film about ideologies, but about sadness, loneliness, the relentless repression to be exercised in the present. Calopreste has the courage not to do a "political" work (in the traditional sense) and to conclude with pessimism. Too bad he didn't have the courage to dig deeper into the (reversible) executioner-victim game.

title: The Madness of King George
actors: Nigel Hawthorne, Helen Mirren, Rupert Everett, Amanda Donohue
description: In 1788, in England, King George III had been in power for thirty years. There is a great need for stability for the government and for the people: the American colonies have recently been lost and the first signs of the French revolution are visible. The sovereign's behavior, however, moves further and further away from etiquette: he shouts obscene phrases, circumvents the queen's lady-in-waiting, wakes the servants at dawn, receives guests in a nightgown. His attitude foments court intrigues and the Prince of Wales' desire for succession. A classic English film: witty, well shot and very well acted by sympathetic and sensitive actors, except for Everett who, in the role of the Prince of Wales, amply shows his limits. Cannes Award for Mirren and Oscar for scenography.

title: Jailhouse Rock
actors: Elvis Presley, Judy Tyler, Mickey Shaughnessy, Vaughn Taylor
description: The young man who is in jail (Elvis Presley) for killing a man in a fight, discovers, thanks to his cellmate, a famous variety singer, that he has a beautiful voice. He asks and gets to learn to play the guitar. As soon as he is free, he embarks on a career as a singer and, after many ups and downs thanks to Peggy, a girl who works in a record company, manages to become a rock star.
notes: The best film of the long series sewn on "the Pelvis".

title: I tre volti
directors: Michelangelo Antonioni, Mauro Bolognini, Franco Indovina
actors: Soraya, Alberto Sordi, Richard Harris, Ivano Davoli
description: A reporter learns that a mysterious princess is about to undergo a film audition. Risking everything, he convinces the editor of the newspaper to publish the news: it could in fact be Soraya, the former empress of Persia repudiated by her husband. Another woman, Linda, leads a (unhappy) worldly life alongside a well-known writer. A wealthy American passing through Rome proves reluctant towards a Roman Latin lover, placed at her disposal by his travel agency.
notes: Episodes directed without much conviction by Antonioni, Bolognini and Indovina to cast Soraya as an actress. Produced by De Laurentiis.

title: Man or Gun
actors: Macdonald Carey, Audrey Totter, James Craig, James Gleason, Warren Stevens
description: Everyone wants Smith's precision pistol, even at the cost of killing him. He refuses to use it except in self-defense and has to defend himself quite often, even from the advances of the rich and beautiful Fran. Series B production, with an unpretentious but rather lively plot.

title: Xìch lo
actors: Tony Leung Chiu Wai, Le Van Loc, Tràn Nu Yén Khé
description: In Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon) an 18-year-old orphan survives by "cyclo" (rickshaw carrier) in a very poor neighborhood. But one day they steal his work tool; to reimburse the cost of the vehicle to his mistress he is forced to commit some crimes. Very quickly it gets absorbed into the machinery of the crime world.
notes: Awarded in Venice in '95, it shines for the remarkable quality of the images, the undoubted narrative passion of the author (who made his debut with the successful "The perfume of the green papaya") and the impressive visual effectiveness. Yet there is an excess of elegance that does not fully convince.

title: Io no spik inglish
actors: Paolo Villaggio, Paola Quattrini, Chiara Noschese, Ian Price, John Armstead
description: Sergio Colombo is a wealthy middle-aged insurer. When his agency is taken over by an English company, he finds himself forced to learn the language he previously blissfully ignored. The "total immersion" course in a boarding school in Oxford holds many surprises for him: first of all that of having to go back to school together with a gang of wild kids.
notes: Even if the idea was not bad, "Io no spik inglish" is a kind of "instant movie", hastily packaged with the waste of the extra-old Italian comedy. Zero-level gag and inventiveness; flatness and squalor that seemed unattainable. Fantozzi is welcome.

title: F for Fake - Vérités et mensonges
actors: Orson Welles, Oja Kodar, François Reichenbach, Joseph Cotten
description: At first Orson Welles juggles at a station. Oja Kodar (the director's last life partner) arrives and promises the crew to tell her own story. Welles is also committed to telling the truth over the next hour. From here begins a narrative that unfolds by presenting various characters, in a complex interlocking, elegant and refined, of apparent truths and sophisticated lies. The film, beyond its totally playful appearance, becomes an interesting and full-bodied metaphor of art as the manipulation of reality, and of cinema as the main tool of this manipulation for the creation of illusions for the spectator.

title: Don Juan DeMarco
actors: Marlon Brando, Johnny Depp, Faye Dunaway, Géraldine Pailhas
description: A masked young man wants to commit suicide for an unhappy love. Dissuaded by a psychiatrist, he is hospitalized in a clinic where, during the sessions, he tells the doctor about his life, full of conquests and adventures, until he meets Ana who denies him and for which the protagonist wants to die. . The doctor, in order not to have the young man interned, forces him to take psychiatric drugs, but the ending is open.
notes: Francis Coppola has produced a film that is a rare example of wrong work. Among all the possible ways to recover the myth of Don Giovanni, that of a "pastiche" of involuntary comedy was chosen. And Marlon Brando makes things worse.

title: Léon
actors: Jean Reno, Gary Oldman, Natalie Portman, Danny Aiello
description: Léon is a killer who lives alone, having only a pot plant for company. Mathilda is a girl who lives in the apartment next to Léon's room. When Mathilda's family is exterminated over a drug affair, she asks Léon for help. A tender friendship is born between the two, between exchanges of lessons on the use of weapons on the one hand and reading on the other.
notes: High voltage power amp. What "story" can arise between a professional murderer, hard as steel, and a twelve year old already disenchanted? Besson tells it with his impetuous style, in which however he knows how to insinuate moments of touching delicacy. Excellent interpreters.

title: Maverick
actors: Mel Gibson, Jodie Foster, James Garner, Graham Greene, James Coburn
description: Bret Maverick is short of $ 3,000 to enter a poker tournament; he wins them in a match in which adventurer Annabelle Bransford also participates. But, at the most beautiful, some thugs burst onto the scene with intentions not at all friendly towards the "gambler", forced to flee. And the whole affair is a succession of traps, as well as mockery ...
notes: Inspired by a famous television series with James Garner in the role of the protagonist (here, however, is the father of Maverick). Jodie Foster takes a vacation from her dramatic roles. An unpretentious but funny film, directed by the Donner of the various "Lethal Weapons".

title: Nemici d'infanzia
actors: Paolo Murano, Renato Carpentieri, Giorgia Tartaglia, Luigi Diberti
description: In the spring of 1944, in Rome, the twelve-year-old Paolo, who has just lost his mother, "spies" what is happening around him and prepares to leave childhood. His brother Marco has enlisted with the Nazi-Fascists, but he is rather attracted by the Resistance to which a mysterious roommate approaches him; he falls in love with the same age Luciana, but unfortunately her father is a fascist hierarch ... From a previous novel, Luigi Magni has drawn this film that tries to resume the discourse of the golden age of neoralist cinema. The outcome, however, is far from flattering. The money was scarce (and it shows), but everything is pulled away at the least worst.

title: Ivo il tardivo
actors: Alessandro Benvenuti, Francesca Neri, Davide Bechini, Daniele Trambusti
description: Ivo is an ageless man, with too much hair and too many numbers on his head: strange and meaningless numbers, which clog his brain. He lives in an abandoned village, lonely but serene, all absorbed in his puzzle, his extravagant and punctual digressions. However, Ivo's psychological instability worsens in contact with the normal life of the rest of the world: the comparison is mainly due to the presence of Sara, engaged in volunteering and linked by a contradictory relationship with her twin brother, Fabio.
notes: The actor-director-screenwriter Benvenuti chisels the character of Ivo with a participation full of tenderness. The protagonist's eccentricity, bordering on madness, is not disturbing, but it makes you smile.

title: To vlemma tou Ulisse
actors: Harvey Keitel, Maia Morgenstern, Erland Josephson
description: A., a Greek filmmaker exiled to the United States, finally returns to his homeland. The return coincides with a journey back in time, in the maze of memory, and an astonished exploration of a topicality that seems almost unreal. The new Odysseus skirts the pitfalls of a world he does not recognize, from Constance to Bucharest: a pilgrimage suffered through the ambiguities and conflicts of the Balkans.
notes: A long and arduous journey (in every sense: the film lasts three hours) from which cinema, literature, war, Eastern Europe - similar to a dangerous iceberg - and socialism torn to pieces emerge, like the statue of Lenin dissected and transported by barge along the Danube.

title: Being Human
actors: Robin Williams, John Turturro, Anna Galiena, Hector Elizondo
description: The family of a Scottish prehistoric man prefers foreign invaders to him. A Roman slave refuses to commit suicide along with his master. A medieval knight dreams of marrying a young widow. A 16th-century Portuguese nobleman is shipwrecked on the African coast. A modern-day New York businessman has a weekend to make up with the children from his first marriage. Williams transforms in five episodes that propose, through a journey through history, the different human behaviors.
notes: Funny AC, uses good photography and a voiceover that holds the strings of the narrative.

title: Jade
actors: Linda Fiorentino, Chazz Palminteri, David Caruso, Richard Crenna
description: David Corelli, an ambitious San Francisco Deputy District Attorney, is at a reception at the home of his colleague Matt, a prominent attorney, and his wife Trina, a psychologist. Suddenly he is called to the scene of a murder, in the home of a well-known billionaire. Carrying out the investigation, David realizes that Trina is among the prime suspects.
notes: A little weighed down by Joe Eszterhas' repetitive script, the film struggles to take off. If you can only concentrate on the first sequence and the "permanent" chase, you will still love the director of "Live and Die in Los Angeles" madly.

title: Muriel's Wedding
actors: Toni Collette, Bill Hunter, Rachel Griffiths, Jeanie Drynan
description: In the seaside resort of Porpoise Spit, young people spend their days amidst parties, gossip and Abba songs. Muriel is not a beauty. However, he does not give up and always leafs through the catalogs of wedding dresses, constantly waiting for the charming prince. Despite the irony of her friends and the annoyance of her family, she gives up everything to focus on Sidney. This modern Cinderella has had a greater success in the United States even than at home; perhaps disproportionate to the merits of a little more than polite comedy, which owes much to the sympathy of the energetic protagonist. An exuberant and impetuous director like his interpreter. "

title: Mortal Kombat
actors: Christopher Lambert, Linden Ashby, Talisa Soto, Trevor Goddard
description: In the realm of Outworld a tournament decides (once for each generation) the fate of the Earth. For nine generations Shang Tsung, an evil priest who feeds on the strength of rival warriors killed in combat, has ensured primacy to one of his proteges. This time two men and a woman assisted by a holy man are called to avert the danger.
notes: Quick reflexes, medieval science fiction costumes, a great display of martial arts, special effects galore; accompanied by pounding music and pseudo-philosophical amenities, waiting for the final "game over". We see that the film is based on a famous video game.

title: The Jackpot
actors: James Stewart, Barbara Hale, James Gleason, Fred Clark, Alan Mowbray
description: A department store employee wins $ 24,000 in a radio quiz. Unfortunately, the prize is not awarded in cash, but consists of a huge amount of objects whose value corresponds to the amount of the win. The taxman, however, does not want to hear reasons and the poor fellow is forced to pay the taxes on the prize pool with cash. But getting seven thousand dollars in a few days isn't easy. And the man even ends up in prison.
notes: Nice script written by Nora Ephron's parents, even if the pace of the film is not irresistible. Barbara Hale is known as Perry Mason's secretary.

title: Blonde Venus
actors: Marlene Dietrich, Herbert Marshall, Cary Grant
description: An American scientist during a business trip to Germany meets and falls in love with a beautiful woman. After a short period of engagement, the scientist marries her and takes her to the United States. But one bad day the man is contaminated by radiation and so his wife, to pay him for the very expensive treatment, is forced to return to work in a night club. One night she meets a playboy she feels terribly attracted to.
notes: Mélo where precise references to the personal story of von Sternberg and Marlene Dietrich found their place. In the original project, the role of Marlene was to be that of a cold and unattached prostitute, but the production imposed a happy ending.

title: My Science Project
actors: John Stockwell, Danielle von Zerneck, Dennis Hopper, Fisher Stevens, Richard Masur
description: Michael Harlan is a little boy who, rummaging through materials abandoned by the army, finds something that, when properly set up, allows you to travel through time. His science teacher tries the car and comes back looking hallucinated in a cowboy outfit. Final with battle between Cleopatra, Godzilla, Neanderthals, gladiators and Nazis.
notes: The idea is nice but it gets pretty weak as the movie goes on. But Hopper is always an imposing figure and his return from the fourth dimension is still worth seeing. Jonathan Bethuel keeps the pace high and you couldn't ask for more.

title: A Killer Among Friends
actors: Patty Duke, Margaret Welsh, Tiffani Thiessen, Debra Sharkey, Loretta Swit
description: Jean Monroe's (Duke) daughter is good, good and beautiful. So when she is killed, everyone wonders in bewilderment who could have wanted the death of such a delightful girl. Detective Patricia Stale (Debra Sharkey) and mom get stubborn in their search for the truth and first discover that two other girls were very jealous of their partner's success. Too jealous ...
notes: Before the little girl from Piano Lessons arrived, Patty Duke was long the youngest actress to be awarded an Oscar (for "Anna of Miracles"). That she then reduced herself to making films for television is a difficult thing to understand.

title: Une femme française
actors: Emmanuelle Béart, Daniel Auteuil, Gabriel Barylli, Jean-Claude Brialy
description: Jeanne is beautiful, seductive, restless and in love with the idea of ??passion and amorous disturbance. She systematically betrays her overly patient husband, who is constantly kept away from home by his military career; and he does so mainly out of vanity, weakness and curiosity. The Second World War, the ruins of Berlin, the Indochina War, the missions in the Middle East mark the passage of time while Jeanne, always equal to herself, collects lovers and adventures.
notes: Wargnier builds an all too cloying mello that has author's claims. Unfortunately, neither Béart nor Auteuil manage to give vitality to the script.

title: Forget Paris
actors: Billy Crystal, Debra Winger, Joe Mantegna, Cynthia Stevenson, Richard Masur, Julie Kavner, Tom Wright, Cathy Moriarty, Robert Costanzo
description: The meeting between Mickey and Ellen is told by their acquaintances at a restaurant table. He, a basketball referee, had been forced on the fateful trip to Paris by the last wish expressed by his father on the verge of death: to be buried in the land of France. She, diligent employee of the airline, had managed to find the coffin "lost" during the stopover in Paris. So they met, and it was love right away ...
notes: The “coup de foudre” of the two protagonists is supported by touristic views and brilliant but stylish dialogues, which would recall Woody Allen's style if they weren't more entertaining on the script page than in front of the camera.

title: Evolver
actors: Ethan Randall, Cassidy Rae, Nassira Nicola, Chance Quinn
description: Kyle Baxter (Randall) is one of the best players in the country of the video game "Evolver". Kyle Baxter is fourteen and can't resist the temptation to play a new robotic version of his favorite video game. The problem is that this is a special version, designed by the military to fight terrorist groups. A version programmed to win at all costs. Halfway between virtual reality and political thriller, Mark Rosman's film is actually neither. The special effects are the usual and, as for the political side, the ambitions do not go much beyond the standard of the action film.

title: Stage Door
actors: Katharine Hepburn, Ginger Rogers, Adolphe Menjou, Gail Patrick
description: In New York, a group of aspiring actresses live in a lively boarding house. One day the daughter of a billionaire arrives, also determined to tread the stage. The influential parent manages to impose her in the lead role in a new production. The girl who was initially selected for that role commits suicide.
notes: A dramatic comedy (there is no shortage of funny moments) about the world of entertainment and its mechanisms, including dramaturgical ones. From a play by Edna Ferber and George S. Kaufman, one of the best interpretations of Katherine Hepburn.

title: The Longest Yard
actors: Burt Reynolds, Eddie Albert, Ed Lauter, Michael Conrad
description: Paul Crewe, convicted of car theft, severe drunkenness and dangerous driving, was once an American football champion. The director of the prison manages to convince him to put together a team of inmates capable of training that of the guards, engaged in the tournament between prisons. The idea is that Crewe's team eventually lose, but he disagrees.
notes: Aldrich constructs one of the finest final sequences in "sports" cinema. The relationships between characters are drawn with the energy and confidence of an action movie master.

title: Nessuno è perfetto
actors: Renato Pozzetto, Ornella Muti, Lina Volonghi, Felice Andreasi, Massimo Boldi
description: Guerrino Castiglioni (Renato Pozzetto), already a widower, is happily married to Chantal (Ornella Muti), a model. Only later does he discover that the girl hides a singular past. It is not even the fact that she was a German paratrooper that upset him. The real problem is that Chantal was once a man. Guerrino is desperate, the family is scandalized, but in the end everything falls into place.
notes: The film plays on the paradox of Ornella Muti as a former male. It is quite incredible that Muti, curvy as she is, can be a model. For the rest, we laugh a little.

title: Smoke
actors: William Hurt, Harvey Keitel, Forest Whitaker, Stockard Channing
description: At the intersection of Seventh Avenue and Third Street is the Brooklyn Cigar Co., a smokers' shop run by Auggie, behind whose gruff, scruffy ways hides a sharp philosopher. One of the store's regular customers is Paul Benjamin, a writer hit by a creative block. Several years earlier, right in front of Auggie's shop, his pregnant wife was killed in front of his eyes, and he is still ravaged by grief. One day, Paul is nearly hit by a bus. Rashid Cole saves him on the fly, a little boy who is running away from no one knows what, but whom Paul is hosting in his home.
notes: The events are glimpses into the neurotic life of a big city. Wang gives his best by adapting the wacky but well-articulated story of Paul Auster's novel. The actors' work is extraordinary. Memorable the final tearful tale, to the tune of "Innocent when you dream" by Tom Waits.

title: Captives
actors: Julia Ormond, Tim Roth, Keith Allen, Jeff Nuttall, Richard Hawley
description: Rachel is a beautiful dentist fresh from separation and emotionally very fragile. Chosen to treat, two days a week, the inmates of a London prison (shot from life), she ends up falling in love, reciprocated, with a "guest" of the institute. Philip has been in prison for murder for six years, and will have four more. The couple turns on erotically in a bar toilet on Philip's weekly free day. Then the relationship becomes very dangerous: people murmur, and there are those who want to take advantage ...
notes: We know how difficult loves are liked by women who feel special. "Captives", an unusual prison film, is a true film in its behavior, tense and unprecedented, in which love, passion and drama are mixed with measure: there is no melodrama or unmotivated emphasis; on the contrary, he inclines to intimism and the suggestion of atmospheres.

title: Chong qing sen lin
actors: Tony Leung Chiu Wai, Takeshi Kaneshiro, Brigitte Lin Chin Hsia, Faye Wong, Valerie Chow
description: Two impossible and specular love stories told in two episodes that maybe meet and maybe not: a policeman abandoned by his girlfriend falls madly in love with a drug dealer. A saleswoman is in love with another policeman, who only thinks about the stewardess who left him.
notes: Strange and highly suggestive detective story that shows off inventiveness, class dialogue and fast pace in narrating the chaos and passion of the Hong Kong youth. But also the film that marks the intellectual "westernization" of the author of masterpieces such as "Ashes of Time" and "As Tears Go By". Quentin Tarantino loved and distributed the film in the United States.

title: Never Talk to Stranger
actors: Rebecca De Mornay, Antonio Banderas, Harry Dean Stanton, Dennis Miller
description: Dr. Sarah Taylor is a very bright and very seductive psychologist expert in criminology. After allowing, with his expertise, to frame a dangerous serial killer, he meets a charming young man with whom he establishes a "hot" relationship. At the same time Sarah becomes the object of inexplicable and macabre threats. Who is persecuting her? The killer maniac you are treating? The new, mysterious, boyfriend? Or maybe her weird dad?
notes: Rebecca De Mornay beautiful but can't act. She is also the executive producer of this insipid Freudian thriller alongside Antonio Banderas to whom, in an unusual erotic impulse, she also bites the buttocks: remarkable unscrupulousness, for being made in England. As for the rest, a simple collection of platitudes and clichés.

title: Devil in a Blue Dress
actors: Denzel Washington, Jennifer Beals, Tom Sizemore, Don Cheadle
description: Ezequiel, Easy for friends, a penniless black in search of fortune, lands in Los Angeles in the middle of the war. He is strongly determined to become a respectable and possibly wealthy guy: for this reason, when they propose to find Daphne Monet, he accepts, being dragged into an intricate and risky mess that forces him to improvise as a private detective.
notes: Classic Noir tastefully directed by an interesting young author whose beautiful "Someone is about to die" should be rediscovered. The devil of the title is, of course, woman. Produced by Jonathan Demme.

title: The Englishman Who Went up a Hill but...
actors: Hugh Grant, Tara Fitzgerald, Colm Meaney, Ian McNeice, Ian Hart
description: We are in an anonymous Welsh village, in 1917. In Europe the war is raging, throughout Great Britain thousands of men are enlisted to fight on the French front, but in Ffynnon Garw they have another problem: they have to reject the response of two cartographers of His Majesty who intend to retreat the mountain of the place to the hill, missing six meters to the three hundred necessary to guarantee the denomination. A handful of feet on which pride and boast of the village are played out.
notes: When it comes to humor, the British continue to remain masters. Monger's rustic and spirited comedy, based on a paradoxically true story, oozes pure Welsh blood and shines with the amount of gimmick and fun it manages to concentrate. It's all hilarious and finely rendered.

title: Final Round
actors: Anthony DeLongis, Lorenzo Lamas, Kathleen Kinmont
description: Tyler Verdiccio is a tough guy and can't go unnoticed. Someone notices it during a fight in a bar, but the admiration is not disinterested and the consequences are unpleasant. Tyler is in fact kidnapped together with his girlfriend and taken to a former industrial complex transformed into an arena. Here he will have to fight in televised challenges for a multi-million dollar betting circuit. Lorenzo Lamas has earned a prominent place in the hypermuscular category, but the film is soporific.

title: Buffy - The Vampire Slayer
actors: Kristy Swanson, Donald Sutherland, Paul Reubens, Rutger Hauer, Luke Perry
description: In Southern California lives student Buffy, a majorette at her school, who is told by a mysterious Mr. Merrick that she is the creature chosen to defeat the many vampires that haunt the area. After the necessary training and after many vicissitudes, Buffy will have the opportunity to prove herself in the role of the winning antagonist of the deadly entities.
notes: A modest but important film. Because it inspired the most popular television series in America today, starring Sarah Michelle Gellar as Buffy the Vampire Slayer. Without the stars of the film but with much more charm and above all many more thrills.

title: Al lupo al lupo
actors: Carlo Verdone, Sergio Rubini, Francesca Neri, Barry Morse
description: Of the three brothers, Vanni (Rubini) has always been the most reliable. In fact, he is now an established pianist, unlike Gregorio (Verdone) who had started playing the violin, but today he is a dee jay. Vanni notices at a certain point that their father has disappeared. Contacted Livia (Neri), their sister, the three set off around Tuscany in search of their missing father.
notes: Who knows why Verdone's films often seem unsolved. There is nothing to say about acting (very good Francesca Neri), but the landscapes are fashionable, the dialogues a little stammering, the psychological development a little second-hand.

title: The Dogs of War
actors: Christopher Walken, Tom Berenger, Jean-François Stévenin, Hugh Millais
description: Commissioned by a mysterious and disreputable Endean, James Shannon (Walken) is in Zangaro, an East African state dominated by the tyrannical Kimba. Arrested, tortured and expelled, Shannon is persuaded by Endean to return to the Zangaro to depose Kimba and replace Colonel Bobi. The operation succeeds, but the ending will not be what Endean wanted. The reference, not too implicit, is to the Ugandan dictator Idi Amin Dada.
notes: And that was also the case in Frederick Forsyth's book from which the film is based. Irvin is not a lightning bolt of war, but he is lucky enough to have the usual great Christopher Walken in his hands.

title: Paris Blues
actors: Paul Newman, Sidney Poitier, Joanne Woodward, Diahann Carroll, Serge Reggiani, Louis Armstrong, Barbara Laage
description: Rahm Bowen (Newman) is a jazz musician who has decided to live on the left bank in Paris. With him part Eddie (Poitier), a musician himself, but more intolerant to the climate of the USA for reasons of skin. In Paris, the two meet Lilan (Woodward) and Connie (Carroll). They both fall in love with Connie, but she, again for reasons of skin, prefers Eddie.
notes: Shot at a time when he could still appear brave, Ritt's film is not a masterpiece. But Duke Ellington's (Oscar nominated) music track is absolutely stunning. Great numbers also for Louis Armstrong.

title: La locandiera
actors: Luisa Ferida, Armando Falconi, Osvaldo Valenti, Camillo Pilotto
description: Mirandolina, who runs an inn on the mainland near Venice, is disputed by some nobles who appreciate both her physical appearance and her qualities of extroverted sympathy. However, she seems intent on conquering a misogynistic and grumpy knight. After jealousies, spite and various complications, Mirandolina confesses that she joked a bit with everyone: she only loves her meek and honest waiter. Chiarini, the most accredited Italian film theorist of his time, manages to avoid many of the pitfalls of "filmed theater" while struggling with the theatrical masterpiece of Carlo Goldoni. The actors are excellent.

title: A Simple Twist of Fate
actors: Steve Martin, Gabriel Byrne, Laura Linney, Alana Austin, Catherine O'Hara
description: Michael finds a baby outside the front door. He just got divorced due to his wife's infidelity and being a father to that creature gives his life a meaning. The real father is a politician with a double life who with that gesture intended to save his public image. After ten years, that baby has grown into an intelligent and lively child. The natural father wants her back for himself and to this end he sues Micahel.
notes: Melodrama with psychosocial implications: a critique of the selfishness of adults (men of power and not), unable to read in the world of children. Steve Martin screenwriter prefers the strong colors of denunciation to the shades of affection.

title: One-Eyed Jacks
actors: Marlon Brando, Karl Malden, Pina Pellicer, Katy Jurado
description: The police surround two bandits who have carried out yet another robbery: Dad (Malden) manages to escape, Rio (Brando) is captured. Five years later, released from prison, Rio finds his former partner who has passed on the other side of the fence: he is a sheriff, he is married and has a stepdaughter, Louisa. And by seducing this young woman, Rio takes the first step on the road to her revenge.
notes: Marlon Brando splits: he is the protagonist but also the director of the film (which was to be directed by Kubrick). A narcissistic director, who exaggerates with close-ups of himself as an actor, but nevertheless creates an ambiguous, anomalous and anti-moralistic western.

title: It's All True
actors: Orson Welles, Richard Wilson, Elisabeth Amster
description: The day after finishing the filming of "Pride of the Ambersons", Orson Welles leaves for Brazil to shoot a documentary there on behalf of the US government. He will never be able to complete it, due to opposition and obstacles, until the order to abandon the project. "It's All True" reconstructs this unfortunate undertaking and shows what was recovered from the material shot.
notes: Orson Welles' entire career is studded with unfulfilled projects. Here the direct testimonies and the vision of the splendid surviving sequences give us the bitter taste of regret for the lost work of a genius of the cinema.

title: Salt on Our Skin
actors: Greta Scacchi, Vincent D'Onofrio, Hans Zischler, Anaïs Jeanneret
description: Her name is George, but she is a wealthy and cultured woman; in the long "flashback" on which the film is built, he tells of his encounter with the fisherman Gavin during his holidays in Scotland. The two like each other, but George rejects the marriage application. They will see each other again, in Paris, in London, in the Virgin Islands, short love breaks in the lives of both, now married to others.
notes: The "pink" of Benoîte Groult's mediocre novel from which the film is based is out of place. A "love story" of little flavor and without narrative flashes. And an always identical Greta Scacchi, from twenty to fifty years old, is really difficult to digest.

title: Lorenzo's Oil
actors: Nick Nolte, Susan Sarandon, Peter Ustinov, Kathleen Wilhoite
description: Little Lorenzo is a lively and precociously intelligent five-year-old boy who lives with his parents in the Comoros Islands. He contracted a very rare disease that causes progressive and unstoppable brain degeneration. His father is an economist, his mother a linguist; neither of them has therefore titles to disprove the doctors when they formulate a tragic prognosis that does not grant Lorenzo more than two years of life. Instead of giving up, the child's parents begin to study the case, until, with a therapy using oleic acid, they have, at least partially, the reason for the disease.
notes: The story that the film tells is true, and the film makes use of the calibrated direction of the Australian George Miller, who does not slip into the traps of a worse pathetism and chooses an almost docu-drama module.

title: Alligator
actors: Robert Forster, Robin Ryker, Michael Gazzo
description: From a home aquarium, a small alligator ends up in the city sewers. Feeding on the carcasses of animals raised with superhormones, downloaded from an unscrupulous research laboratory, it takes on monstrous dimensions and hunger. As a genre we are close to the "Shark". Screenplay by John Sayles, with touches of humor and political-ecological colorings. Also in the cast are some old glories such as character actor Henry Silva, specializing in action films, and ex- "Lolita" Sue Lyon.

title: Pierino la peste alla riscossa
actors: Giorgio Ariani, Jenny Tamburi, Didi Perego, Renzo Montagnani
description: Pierino's family is made up of a father, a cheating pharmacist, a naive mother and a biting grandmother. Repeating professional, at school no one escapes his pranks, especially the teacher. Of course, the favorite pastime of the "plague" is still bothering the girls.
notes: An authentically trash film, because it is a draft of a model already considered very low. In place of Alvaro Vitali, the Tuscan comedian Giorgio Ariani.

title: La posta in gioco
actors: Lina Sastri, Turi Ferro, Vittorio Caprioli, Pier Palo Capponi, Flavio Bucci
description: On the trail of the assassins of Renata Fonte, Nardò's councilor for culture, a commissioner and a prosecutor "sniff" the big guns behind the crime. But the investigations are blocked "at the top". Investigative film on a real blood event from 1984, it disappoints for its devoid of imagination and devoid of imagination directing.

title: Resting Place
actors: John Lithgow, Richard Bradford, Morgan Freeman, John Philbin
description: We are in the United States in the seventies. To give a black war hero a worthy burial in a Georgia cemetery, a US military officer comes face to face with the horrid culture of racism and who he wants to put a spoke in his wheel. Not even death is the same for everyone.
notes: Above-average quality television production, thanks to the beautiful script and cast of the likes of John Lithgow and Morgan Freeman. The director examines well a delicate theme such as that of racism and that of war that has always upset the consciences of the American people.

title: Era una notte buia e tempestosa...
actors: Alessandro Benvenuti, Athina Cenci, Daniele Trambusti
description: Felix, who is a stand-up comedian awaiting success, shares a small apartment with Valentina and Riccardino. The coexistence of the three "singles" proceeds between ups and downs, between banal routines and small accidents in a funny and bewildered atmosphere. Until, unexpectedly, the eviction arrives ...
notes: Three years after _Ad Ovest di Paperino_, the Giancattivi (Daniele Trambusti replaced Francesco Nuti) bring the patterns and rhythms of their cabaret back to the screen. Written and directed by a young Alessandro Benvenuti, who had not yet illustrated the provincial world of Casa Gori or the “spicy” world of _Belle al bar_.

title: A Walk in the Clouds
actors: Keanu Reeves, Aitana Sánchez-Gijón, Giancarlo Giannini, Anthony Quinn
description: Victoria, a young daughter of Hispanic immigrants, is terrified of having to confess to her winemaker father that she was pregnant. Luck has it that he meets a chocolate seller who has been betrayed by his wife, disappointed in life, and with a tender heart. The boy, who basically has nothing to lose, pretends to be the girl's husband in front of the most honorable family.
notes: This remake of "Four Steps in the Clouds", an anticipation of "pink neorealism" directed by Blasetti in 1942, applies to the California of Hispanic immigrants a climate that suited the Po valleys, and that leaves us perplexed. Stunned the cast

title: The Usual Suspects
actors: Kevin Spacey, Gabriel Byrne, Chazz Palminteri, Pete Postlethwaite
description: San Pedro, last night: on the deck of a freighter a stranger kills a corrupt ex-policeman. New York, six weeks ago: in a police station five men are lined up for an American confrontation. San Pedro, today: Five charred corpses are lined up on the deck of a ship. Special Agent Kujan is tasked with unraveling the tangled skein of half sentences of the ship's only survivor. He explains to the policeman how it all started six weeks earlier: that is, when the five suspects of the New York plant were dragged into the trap set by an enigmatic genius of crime, the elusive Kaiser Soze, whose identity no one knows. An interlocking screenplay full of twists is for a film directed with irresistible rhythm and great suspense by the very young Singer. Great actors (Spacey won the Oscar as a supporting character) and a mysterious central character, Kaiser Soze, who becomes more and more a diabolical metaphor.

title: Safe
actors: Julianne Moore, Xander Berkeley, Peter Friedman, James LeGros, Mary Carver, Jessica Harper, Jodie Markell, Susan Norman, Chauncey Leopardi, Steven Gilborn, Lorna Scott
description: Carol, a wealthy young lady, lives quietly in her beautiful home in the San Fernando Valley. Her concerns are shopping with friends, hairdressing, aerobics classes. Until he begins to feel the symptoms of a strange disease that progressively worsens. It turns out she is allergic to a frightening number of substances: fabrics, detergents, plastics, leather, perfumes. In practice to all the products of civilized society.
notes: "Safe" looks like a modern horror, in which the interesting idea is that the most terrible threat comes from the implications of everyday normality. A film about a sort of "global allergy", stylized in the first part and ambiguously documentary in the second. Stunning performance by Julianne Moore.

title: Ragazzi della notte
actors: Jerry Calà, Fabio Testi, Sergio Vastano
description: The "good night" of a group of young people, each with its own problems and events behind it, orbits around the world of discos. There are the provincials, the bullies, the good guys, the displaced. Between dances, loves, friendships, awards, car rides and some joints, including hospitalization, it turns out that solidarity and understanding are often found in the most unexpected corners.
notes: Jerry Calà improvises himself as a director and sociologist: he would like us to understand the (well-known) problems of youth, the role of the disco as an escape from a cruel real, the need to understand these guys and help them. Good intentions, but a depressing banality.

title: Yinghung bunsik II
actors: Leslie Cheung, Chow Yun-fat, Ti Lung
description: Ken (Chow Yun Fat) was once a leading exponent of the Hong Kong organized underworld. Now, having abandoned all illegal activities, he decides to go straight. And not only. Having as his brother an honest cop, Ken (Leslie Cheung), he uses his experience and knowledge to help him in his investigation of a very powerful criminal organization. For the two it is not easy, but in the end they succeed. The saga halfway between the criminal and the mélo continues the year before by director John Woo and producer Tsui Hark. The ingredients are the same: familiar feelings mixed with the spectacular action. The result is more than satisfactory, and in some cases (like the final shooting) extraordinary.

title: Separate Lives
actors: James Belushi, Linda Hamilton, Vera Miles
description: Lauren is a successful psychology teacher, beautiful, from a great family and with a brilliant career ahead of her. Too bad that at night the irreproachable teacher turns into Lena, a hot female with unbridled sexual habits. To protect herself from the insane habits of her "hard" side, which could seriously endanger her own life, Lauren asks one of her students, a former cop, to stay behind her.
notes: Very thin pseudo-Freudian thriller. The story is full of holes, with characters being mysteriously abandoned all of a sudden and soap-opera dialogue.

title: Braveheart
actors: Mel Gibson, Sophie Marceau, Catherine McCormack, Patrick McGoohan
description: In the late thirteenth century, William Wallace returns to Scotland, his homeland, after many years away. The King of Scotland is dead, and King Edward I of England, the Plantagenet, has taken his place. After the death of his father and the murder of his wife, Wallace stands up to British oppressors by leading his homeland through the long and bloody war of liberation.
notes: Gibson proves he can confidently move on both sides of the camera (although second unit director Mic Rodgers shot the epic battle scene). "Braveheart" revives the spectacular vein of the best Hollywood tradition.

title: Guantanamera
directors: Tomàs Gutiérrez Alea, Juan Carlos Tabío
actors: Carlos Cruz, Mirta Ibarra, Raul Eguren, Jorge Perugorría
description: In today's Cuba, to the tune of the hugely popular song from the 1950s, a funeral procession, carrying the body of an elderly singer, wanders through the streets and alleys without reaching its destination. Bureaucratic hitches, interference from playboy truck drivers, "impromptu" falls in love, confusion of tombs and surreal encounters: chance plus a good dose of lightness and carelessness do their utmost to hinder and postpone reaching the place of eternal rest. Small comedy of misunderstandings, tinged with black humor and flavored with a fair (but harmless) dose of criticism of the system. The film starts well, but gets stuck along the way: victim of repetitiveness and a macchiettismo that condemns it to a farcical dimension. Too bad, because one could have hoped for a much more biting satire.

title: Under Siege II
actors: Steven Seagal, Eric Bogosian, Everett McGill, Katherine Heigl, Patrick Kilpatrick
description: A former Pentagon employee, psychotic tech whiz, hijacked the Grand Continental. America's most luxurious train is now on a breathtaking ride through the Rocky Mountains. They threaten to raze Washington and the surrounding area using the satellite designed for the government by the former official before being removed from office. The lives of more than three million people are in their hands, and to "pardon" them they are asking for a billion dollars. But they haven't reckoned with ex-cook Casey Ryback ...
notes: True to tradition, Steven Seagal doesn't let a glimmer of expression cross his face for the duration of the film.

title: The Angry Hills
actors: Robert Mitchum, Stanley Baker, Elisabeth Müller, Gia Scala
description: In Nazi-occupied Greece, Mike Morrison (Mitchum), an American war correspondent, finds himself involved in a game that can cost him his life: in fact, he has a list with the names of sixteen Greek partisans, a list that would make the happiness of the German secret services.
notes: Starting from a novel by Leon Uris, Aldrich directs a film full of references to the mythology and history of Greece.

title: Smart Woman
actors: Mary Astor, Robert Ames, John Halliday, Edward Everett Horton
description: One woman discovers that her husband is infatuated with another. To win him back he wants to make him jealous by accepting the court of an Englishman.
